question:
In the early days of television in the 1940s, many people thought that US television programs would rely on the financial support of ad agencies and commercial sponsors, much like radio did. But advertisers hesitated to jump into a new space, particularly at a time when the manufacturing of new television sets was stalled due to the US’s involvement in World War II. Broadcasters, like the National Broadcasting Company (NBC), needed to persuade advertisers to support their programming despite not knowing whether there would be a robust television audience to begin with.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined phrase in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It describes how broadcasters attempted to convince advertisers to support television.
B. It explains why a type of television programming was popular at the time.
C. It identifies a specific reason behind some advertisers’ hesitance to support television.
D. It compares the beginnings of radio programming with the beginnings of television programming in the United States.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
在1940年代电视刚兴起的早期，许多人认为美国的电视节目将像广播一样，依赖广告公司和商业赞助商的财务支持。然而，广告商在进入这一新领域时犹豫不决，尤其是在美国因参与第二次世界大战而导致新电视机的生产停滞不前的时期。像全国广播公司（NBC）这样的广播公司需要说服广告商支持他们的节目，即便他们并不知道是否会有强大的电视观众基础。
中文解析：
划线句论证前面句，指出当时二战期间缘由说面广告商犹豫投资的原因
exam_name: 2024年12月第3套阅读语法（M1和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
The following text is from Armando Palcio Valdés's short story “The love of Clatilde,” originally published in Spanish in 1884. In the story, Don Jerónimo is a financial supporter of artists in the theater.
Any youth from the provinces who arrived in Madrid with a drama in his pocket could take no surer road to seeing it produced than that which led to the home of Don Jeronimo. One and all, he received them with open arms, the good and the had alike. There is no denying that, since he was rather brusque in his ways, he never spared the young author's who asked his advice and read him their productions, but criticized vigorously, even to the verge of insult.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It suggests that Don Jerónimo does not enjoy financially supporting playwrights.
B. It creates a contrast between the reputation of a young playwright and that of Don Jerónimno.
C. It emphasizes the degree to which Don Jerónimo's support is consequential for inexperienced playwrights.
D. It explains Don Jerónimo's view of the quality of theatrical works of the time.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
以下文本摘自阿曼多·帕利西奥·瓦尔德斯的短篇小说《克拉提尔德的爱》，最初于1884年以西班牙语出版。在故事中，赫罗尼莫爵士是剧院艺术家的资助者。
任何从省份来到马德里的年轻人，只要口袋里揣着一部剧本，都可以通过通往赫罗尼莫爵士家的道路找到更可靠的机会来实现自己的作品。他以开放的怀抱接待所有人，无论好坏。不可否认的是，由于他性格较为粗暴，他从不吝啬于给年轻作者提供建议，并认真地阅读他们的作品，但他的批评往往激烈，甚至到了侮辱的边缘。
中文解析：
Don Jerónimo的身份是financial supporter of artists in the theater.文中No surer road 是一种比喻的手法，形容再没有比找Don Jerónimo是年轻作家produce their dramas的必经之路 了，于是和选项C保持一致：它强调了唐Jerónimo的支持对没有经验的剧作家的影响程度。
exam_name: 2024年12月第3套阅读语法（M1和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
The following text is adapted from Yone Noguchi’s 1914 memoir The Story of Yone Noguchi. Noguchi is returning home after eleven years abroad.
I reached Tsushima, my native town, at evening.
I frightened my old father at the station, who was actually trying to find me among some other people. There is no wonder that he could not recognise me; I must have changed a great deal.

As used in the text, what does the word “find” most nearly mean?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
以下文本改编自野口米次的1914年回忆录《野口米次的故事》。米次在国外生活了十一年后，正准备回家。
我在傍晚时分到达了我的家乡对马岛。
我在车站吓到了我的老父亲，他当时正在人群中寻找我。难怪他认不出我了，一定变化很大。
中文解析：
根据后面recognize，find表示认出，找到，于是locate是同义词
exam_name: 2024年12月第3套阅读语法（M1和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Among the most visited art museums in the world, the Museo Reina Sofia in Madrid had approximately 4.4 million visitors in 2019. The Museo Reina Sofia also offers virtual tours that art lovers can view online for free. Although there were initial concerns that people who viewed the virtual tours would then consider an in-person visit unnecessary, museum administrators claim that their surveys of in-person visitors show that those concerns were unjustified.

Which statement, if true, would most directly support the administrators’ claim?
selections: A. Most surveyed visitors to the Museo Reina Sofia indicated that they lived somewhere other than Madrid.
B. Many surveyed visitors to the Museo Reina Sofia indicated that the virtual tours convinced them to plan an in-person visit.
C. Many surveyed visitors to the Museo Reina Sofia indicated that they would likely view the virtual tours in order to reminisce about their in-person visit.
D. Most surveyed visitors to the Museo Reina Sofia indicated that they were unaware of the virtual tours before their first in-person visit.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
在世界上最受欢迎的艺术博物馆中，马德里的索非亚王后博物馆在2019年的参观人数约为440万。索非亚王后博物馆还提供虚拟导览，艺术爱好者可以在线免费观看。尽管最初有人担心观看虚拟导览的人会认为亲自参观变得不必要，但博物馆管理者声称，他们对亲自参观者的调查显示这些担忧并没有根据。
中文解析：
文本结论是the claim that in-person visit would be unnecessary were unjustified,也就是证明其实人们觉得in person visit还是有必要的，B选项符合要求，因为人们再计划in-person visit.
exam_name: 2024年12月第3套阅读语法（M1和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Dubattia raillardioides is a species in a family of plants known collectively as the silversword alliance, all of which grow only on the Hawaiian Islands. Members of this alliance exhibit an extraordinary range of phenotypes, with some species maturing into vines and others into shrubs and trees. All species in the alliance descended from a single ancestral tarweed plant that arrived on the islands around 5 million years ago. The tarweed’s descendants diversified into distinct species as they adapted to live in the wide variety of habitats found on the Hawaiian Islands.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined phrase in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It lists species from a family of plants found only on the Hawaiian Islands.
B. It explains why Dubautia raillardioides is unique among members of the silversword alliance.
C. It supplies the name used to refer to a group of related plant species.
D. It provides the common name for the Dubautia raillardioides plant.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
Dubattia raillardioides 是一种属于被统称为银剑联盟的植物家族的物种，这个家族的植物仅生长在夏威夷群岛。这个联盟的成员表现出惊人的表型多样性，有些物种发育成藤本植物，而另一些则发育成灌木和树木。该联盟的所有物种都源自大约500万年前到达这些岛屿的一种祖先植物——油菜。这种油菜的后代在适应夏威夷群岛上多样的栖息地时，逐渐演化成不同的物种。
中文解析：
被下划线标记的短语“silversword alliance”是用来指代一个植物家族的名称，包括Dubattia raillardioides以及其他相关物种
exam_name: 2024年12月第3套阅读语法（M1和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
The Clouds is a 423 BCE play by Aristophanes, originally written in ancient Greek. At the time, professional intellectuals called sophists taught customers rhetorical techniques to use in public speaking, along with providing instruction in other subjects. In the play, Aristophanes satirizes sophists as teaching people to speak dishonestly, as seen when the character ________

Which choice most effectively uses a quotation from a translation of The Clouds to illustrate the claim?
selections: A. Strepsiades encourages his son to learn to be a sophist, saying. “If you have any concern for your father’s patrimony, become one of them.”
B. Pheidippides says, after taking lessons from a sophist, “How pleasant it is to be acquainted with new and clever things, and to be able to despise the established laws!”

C. Strepsiades, taking lessons from a sophist, says he wants to become “a fabricator of falsehoods, inventive of words, a practiced knave in lawsuits, ... a fox, a sharper, a slippery knave, a dissembler, a slippery fellow, an impostor.”
D. Socrates, a sophist, says to a potential customer, “I wish to briefly learn from you if you are possessed of a good memory.”
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
《云》是公元前423年由阿里斯托芬创作的一部话剧，最初用古希腊语写成。在那个时代，专业的知识分子被称为智者（sophists），他们向顾客教授公共演讲中使用的修辞技巧，同时还提供其他学科的指导。在剧中，阿里斯托芬对智者进行讽刺，认为他们教人们说谎，如当角色________时所表现的那样。
中文解析：
文本claim是关系sophist teach people to speak dishonestly,于是C选项满足，因为fabricator falsehoods，invesntive of words等描述都是不诚实的意思，C选项大意：斯特雷普西阿德斯（Strepsiades）在向一位智者学习时说，他想成为“一个虚假制造者，善于玩弄词句的伎俩，在诉讼中老练的骗子……一个狡猾的家伙，一个狡诈者，一个狡猾的家伙，一个伪装者，一个滑头的家伙，一个冒充者。”

question:
Community science involves professional scientists collaborating with members of the public to study a topic. This approach to research can promote community engagement by offering insight into the daily life of a scientist. It’s also very effective because it greatly increases the amount of data that can be collected, such as when biologist Abbigail Merrill and colleagues studied butterfly size and its relation to behavior and used findings reported by hundreds of students and community members in northwestern Arkansas.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
selections: A. Abbigail Merrill and colleagues used a community science approach in their butterfly research and were surprised at the effect this had on public understanding of the nature of scientists’ work.
B. A community science approach can increase public understanding of the nature of scientists’ work and generate large amounts of data, benefiting both communities and researchers.
C. A community science approach can benefit communities by increasing public understanding of the nature of scientists’ work, but it’s less likely to help researchers obtain accurate data.
D. A community science approach allows researchers to collect significantly more data even though it’s unlikely to have much of an effect on public understanding of the nature of scientists’ work.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
社区科学是指专业科学家与公众成员合作研究某一主题。这种研究方式可以通过提供科学家日常生活的洞察来促进社区参与。同时，它也非常有效，因为它大大增加了可以收集的数据量。例如，生物学家阿比盖尔·梅里尔（Abbigail Merrill）及其同事研究了蝴蝶的大小及其与行为的关系，并利用了来自阿肯色州西北部的数百名学生和社区成员报告的发现。
中文解析：
a community science能够提升科学家的工作，也能够产生大量的数量，带来很多益处，和B选项一致
exam_name: 2024年12月第3套阅读语法（M1和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:

• Her sculpture Uros House is made of smooth multicolored LED domes.
• It occupies 250 cubic feet of space.
• Her sculpture Ocupante is made of entangled blue and white LED tubes.
• It occupies 80,000 cubic feet of space.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Uros House and Ocupante. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. At 80,000 cubic feet in size, Grimanesa Amoros’s Ocupante cuts a larger figure than the 250-cubic-foot Uros House.
B. Uros House is an LED light sculpture made by Grimanesa Amoros, as is Ocupante.
C. The smooth LED domes of Grimanesa Amoros’s Uros House stand in contrast to the tangled LED tubes of Ocupante.
D. Grimanesa Amoros is the artist behind Uros House—a sculpture made of smooth multicolored LED domes.
explanations:

在研究一个主题时，一位学生做了以下笔记：

• 它占据了250立方英尺的空间。

• 它占据了80,000立方英尺的空间。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers in a 2021 study wanted to determine the rate at which 17 languages conveyed both information and syllables.
• They calculated the bits of information conveyed per second (the IR, or information rate).
• The IR was found to be approximately consistent across the 17 languages (an average of 39 bits per second).
• They calculated the number of syllables spoken per second (the SR, or syllable rate).
• Spanish had the second-fastest SR (7.7 syllables per second).
• Vietnamese had the sixteenth-fastest SR (5.3 syllables per second).

The student wants to present an overview of the study’s findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Though some of the languages differed in number of syllables spoken per second, all 17 conveyed information at roughly the same rate.
B. The 2021 study determined the information rate (IR) of 17 languages in bits of information conveyed per second.
C. Vietnamese had the sixteenth-fasted syllable rate, lower than that of Spanish, which had the second-fastest; however, Spanish had the lower information rate of the two.
D. Researchers found that information was conveyed more quickly in Spanish, at 7.7 syllables per second, than in Vietnamese, at 5.3 syllables per second.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
在研究一个主题时，学生做了以下笔记：
• 研究人员在2021年的一项研究中想要确定17种语言传达信息和音节的速度。
• 他们计算了每秒传达的信息位数（信息率，IR）。
• 发现这17种语言的IR大致一致（平均为每秒39位）。
• 他们计算了每秒说出的音节数（音节率，SR）。
• 西班牙语的音节率是第二快的（每秒7.7个音节）。
• 越南语的音节率是第十六快的（每秒5.3个音节）。
中文解析：
根据notes，虽然17语言单位时间内syllables速度不一样，但是意义传递速率是相似的
exam_name: 2024年12月第3套阅读语法（M1和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:

Bhatt et al. found that in comparison with two polymer-derived SiC fibers, a nitrogen-treated SiC fiber exhibited a lower minimum creep rate, a measure of the rate at which a stress-exposed material deforms at a constant temperature and uniaxial load. The finding suggests that ________

B. aerospace composites containing the nitrogen-treated SiC fiber may have the ability to withstand mechanical stress for a longer period of time than can aerospace composites containing either of the two polymer-derived SiC fibers.

C. composites based on the two polymer-derived SiC fibers have chemical properties that may improve the mechanical and thermal stability of aerospace equipment to a greater extent than do composites based on the nitrogen-treated SiC fiber.

question:
A team of public transportation experts in Detroit is creating a new streetcar stop for the Woodward Avenue Streetcar system that will service a neighborhood in which a stop does not currently exist. To decide where to place the stop, the team is using a survey from ten years ago that asked how far neighborhood residents would be willing to walk to a streetcar stop. The team also looked at studies showing that people’s willingness to walk to public transit is influenced by factors like weather and the presence of paved sidewalks and available crosswalks. A researcher has argued that the survey does not accurately reflect the feelings of today’s residents of this neighborhood.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher’s claim?
selections: A. The number of sidewalks and crosswalks in the neighborhood that the streetcar stop will service has increased substantially in the last ten years.
B. Residents of Detroit are much less likely to use public transit on rainy days than on clear days.
C. There has been a sharp increase in the last ten years in cyclists who use the roads in the neighborhood that the streetcar stop will service.
D. Current users of the Woodward Avenue Streetcar are satisfied with the number of stops along the line.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
底特律的一组公共交通专家正在为伍德沃德大道有轨电车系统创建一个新的有轨电车站，以服务于一个目前没有站点的社区。为了决定站点的最佳位置，该团队使用了十年前的一项调查，该调查询问了社区居民愿意为到达有轨电车站走多远。他们还查阅了研究，显示人们愿意步行到公共交通站点的意愿受天气、铺设的人行道以及可用的斑马线等因素的影响。一位研究人员辩称，这项调查并未准确反映当今该社区居民的感受。
中文解析：
文本结论是survey 无法准确反应现在的社区，那么之前提到的因素包括了weather and sidewalks等，那么A选项符合，如果sidewalks and crosswalks数量激增，说明这个因素已经变化了，和之前的情况不一样了。

question:
Some food packaging contains silver nanoparticles (Ag-NPs), which can leach into waterways and soils via wastewater. In a 2015 study, Tina Ramskov and colleagues found that Ag-NPs can accumulate in the bodies of marine annelid worms (Capitella teleta). While bioaccumulation of manufactured nanoparticles may be inherently worrisome, it has been hypothesized that Ag-NP bioaccumulation in invertebrates like C. teleta could serve a valuable proxy role, obviating the need for manufacturers to conduct costly and intrusive sampling of vertebrate species—such as Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), commonly used in regulatory compliance testing—for nanoparticle bioaccumulation, as environmental protection laws currently require.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the hypothesis presented in the text?
selections: A. When C. teleta and S. salar are exposed to similar levels of Ag-NPs, individuals of the two species tend to accumulate similar amounts of Ag-NPs, adjusted for body size.
B. Ag-NP concentrations in C. teleta correlate strongly with Ag-NP levels in the environment, whereas Ag-NP concentrations in S. salar are fairly stable regardless of environment.
C. Compared with S. salar, C. teleta can tolerate significantly higher Ag-NP concentrations without displaying any negative effects.
D. It is easier to detect low and harmless concentrations of Ag-NPs in C. teleta than it is to detect high and harmful concentrations of Ag-NPs in S. salar.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
一些食品包装中含有银纳米颗粒（Ag-NPs），这些颗粒可能通过废水渗入水道和土壤。在2015年的一项研究中，蒂娜·拉姆斯科夫（Tina Ramskov）及其同事发现，Ag-NPs能够在海洋环节动物（如海洋环节虫，Capitella teleta）的体内积累。虽然制造的纳米颗粒的生物积累本身可能令人担忧，但有人假设，像C. teleta这样的无脊椎动物中银纳米颗粒的生物积累可以作为一个有价值的替代指标，从而使制造商无需进行高成本且侵入性的脊椎动物物种（如大西洋鲑鱼，Salmo salar）采样，以检测纳米颗粒的生物积累，这在当前的环境保护法律中是要求的。
中文解析：
proxy role替换角色，需要保持相似环境下，相似的bio-accumulation，也就是两个动物最后体内能检测的particles数量相似，于是A选项正确

 generated by the activity of soil microorganisms). Hydrologist Yonghong Yi and her colleagues developed a model incorporating numerous inputs—years of solar radiation and snow cover data among them—to evaluate the effects of warming on the  
 balance in Alaska, concluding that net  
 is likely to increase if warming hastens spring snow melt. Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers’ conclusion?
selections: A. Early snow melt extends the period in which plant species such as C. palustre can absorb<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal"> C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></math> but has no effect on the rate of heterotrophic respiration.

question:
Text 1
French Impressionist artist Edgar Degas insisted that his paintings be kept in their original frames after they were sold. Like many Impressionist painters, Degas used painted frames that stood in contrast to the gold frames frequently seen at the Paris Salon, a prestigious art exhibition that was sponsored by the French government and promoted traditional painting styles. Impressionist painters likely chose these colorful frames to distinguish themselves from what was considered conventional at the time.
Text 2
Impressionist painters often focused on the interplay of color and light in their works. As such, those Impressionists who placed their works in painted frames instead of the more traditional gold ones did so for aesthetic reasons: a frame’s color was likely chosen because it would harmonize with the colors or subjects in a painting. Gold, conversely, could distract from the subtleties in a painted scene.

Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
selections: A. Many Impressionist painters were intentional about the frames they selected for their works.
B. Degas’s preferred framing style was different from that of most Impressionist painters.
C. The colors in an Impressionist painting were often chosen to complement the colors of the frame it would be placed in.
D. Gold frames were considered especially desirable by those who purchased works from Impressionist painters.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
文本 1
法国印象派艺术家爱德加·德加坚持在作品售出后保持其原有的画框。与许多印象派画家一样，德加使用了彩绘画框，这与巴黎沙龙常见的金色画框形成了鲜明对比。巴黎沙龙是由法国政府赞助的一个享有盛誉的艺术展览，主要推广传统绘画风格。印象派画家选择这些色彩丰富的画框，可能是为了使自己与当时被视为传统的风格区分开来。
文本 2
印象派画家常常专注于作品中色彩与光线的相互作用。因此，那些将作品放在彩绘画框而非更传统的金色画框中的印象派艺术家，出于美学原因作出了这样的选择：画框的颜色很可能是为了与画作中的颜色或主题相协调。相反，金色画框可能会分散观众对绘画场景细微之处的注意。
中文解析：
两篇文章的共同点就是印象主义艺术家对于画框的挑选与重视其意义

question:

(a complex life cycle parasite, or CLP, that requires three host species throughout its life cycle), Gyrodactylus sp. (a directly transmitted parasite, which requires only one host species), and 83 other parasite taxa found on eight fish species. CLPs are transmitted when an infected host is ingested by an individual of another species, typically shielding CLPs from the external environment, whereas directly transmitted parasites are exposed to external conditions during transmission. However, Wood et al. found that three-host CLP abundance decreased as sea temperatures rose, whereas directly transmitted parasite abundance was largely stable, suggesting that ________

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. as the number of host species involved in a parasite’s transmission increases, the parasite is better protected against rising temperatures.
B. directly transmitted parasites identified in the study were more likely to use transmission strategies that shield them from warming temperatures than were three-host CLPs.
C. CLPs primarily transmitted by ingestion were less dependent on host species adversely affected by warming temperatures than were CLPs that use other transmission strategies.
D. any advantages that the transmission strategy used by three-host CLPs may have conferred did not completely offset the negative effects of other temperature-driven factors on CLP abundance.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
切尔西·伍德等人跟踪了温度驱动的Gonocerca sp.（一种复杂生命周期寄生虫，简称CLP，整个生命周期需要三种宿主物种）、Gyrodactylus sp.（一种直接传播的寄生虫，仅需要一种宿主物种）以及在八种鱼类中发现的其他83个寄生虫分类群的丰度变化。CLP在感染宿主被另一种物种摄入时传播，通常使CLP免受外部环境的影响，而直接传播的寄生虫在传播过程中暴露于外部条件。然而，伍德等人发现，随着海水温度的升高，三宿主CLP的丰度下降，而直接传播寄生虫的丰度基本保持稳定，这表明______。
中文解析：
根据文本CLP需要依赖三种寄生虫，但是directly transmitted只需要依赖一种寄生虫，CLP在寄主感染后会发生转移，能起到保护作用，但是另一种是directly transmitted则是直接暴露在外部环境下，但是结果确实前者易受到温度影响，后者反而保持稳定数量，因此可以得出结论CLPs获得的优势不足以抵消温度对其产生的负面影响。

question:
The following text is from Thomas Mann’s 1924 novel The Magic Mountain, translated by John E. Woods in 1995.
The story of Hans Castorp that we intend to tell here—not for his sake (for the reader will come to know him as a perfectly ordinary, if engaging young man), but for the sake of the story itself, which seems to us to be very much worth telling (although in Hans Castorp’s favor it should be noted that it is his story, and that not every story happens to everybody) —is a story that took place long ago, and is, so to speak, covered with the patina of history and must necessarily be told with verbs whose tense is that of the deepest past.
©1995 by Alfred A. Knopf, Inc.

What does the text most strongly suggest about the story of Hans Castorp?
selections: A. Though it is true that stories of even the most uninteresting people are themselves interesting because all people are unique, the reason this story is interesting is nonetheless difficult to understand because of the passage of time.
B. Even though it is a story of a person of no particular importance, its age and the manner in which it therefore must be told are both indicators that the story itself is important.
C. It is a remarkable story that happened to an unremarkable person, though one could plausibly argue that because the story is valuable, some of its value accrues to the person at its center.

D. Like all stories about the lives of inconsequential people, this story must necessarily be related in a particular way if the reason the story is consequential is to be made evident to the audience.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
以下文本摘自托马斯·曼于1924年发表的小说《魔山》，由约翰·E·伍兹于1995年翻译。
我们打算在这里讲述汉斯·卡斯托普的故事——并不是为了他的缘故（因为读者会了解到他只是一个完全普通、但颇具吸引力的年轻人），而是为了这个故事本身，这个故事似乎非常值得讲述（尽管值得一提的是，汉斯·卡斯托普的故事确实是他的故事，并不是每个故事都能适用于每个人）——这是一个发生在很久以前的故事，可以说，它被历史的光晕所笼罩，必须用最深远的过去时态来叙述。
中文解析：
官方答案C。这个故事不因为人，而因为故事本身值得讲，因为故事本身很好，所以人们会觉得里面的中心人物也很unremarkable.

question:
Individual elephants and Arctic herbivores such as caribou tend to have fixed geographic ranges throughout their lifetimes, which had prompted some researchers to speculate that the Arctic woolly mammoth, an extinct elephantid, might have exhibited similar behavior. Mammoth tusks grew in sequential layers, incorporating ingested minerals and organics, and so each ivory stratum reflects the ratio of strontium isotopes (<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>87</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>/</mo></mrow><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>86</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow></math>) in the local environment; thus, the sequence of strata shows where the animal roamed during life. Recent analysis of the strontium ratios in the strata of one Arctic woolly mammoth tusk in relation to the geographic distribution of strontium ratios in the environment shows the animal’s range begin to expand as it reached sexual maturity, only to contract again in its final 1.5 years.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined statement in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It discusses a characteristic shared by certain animals in order to explain why researchers raised a possibility that turned out not to be supported by data described later in the text.
B. It illustrates a pattern of behavior among certain animals in order to present a theory about exceptions to that pattern that is weakened by a finding described later in the text.
C. It describes a similarity in the behavior of certain animals in order to show why a method described later in the text did not reveal whether another animal also showed that behavior.
D. It introduces a trait shared by certain animals in order to contextualizea hypothesis about the origin of that trait that is advanced later in the text.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
个体象和北极草食动物，如驯鹿，通常在其一生中具有固定的地理范围，这促使一些研究人员推测，已经灭绝的北极毛象可能也表现出类似的行为。毛象的牙齿以层状方式生长，包含了摄取的矿物质和有机物，因此每一层象牙反映了当地环境中锶同位素（87Sr/86Sr）的比率；因此，层次的序列显示了动物在生存期间的活动范围。最近对一根北极毛象牙齿层中的锶比率的分析，以及与环境中锶比率的地理分布的比较，显示该动物在达到性成熟时，其活动范围开始扩大，但在其最后的1.5年内又收缩回去。
中文解析：
文本划线句表达一些动物活动在相对固定的区域fixed geographic ranges，这使得之后研究院认为mammoth也是如此，但是最后的结论是mammoth地理分布有时expand或contract，没有支持之前的猜想。

foraging honeybees超过了threshold, 那么根据图表red mason bees更加超过了，那么一定也能够attract the stamens

question:
Spanning the 1920s to the 1980s, Mexican architect Luis Barragán’s prolific career evolved through distinct phases. Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
selections: A. It presents a general claim about a particular architect’s career, describes a design approach that typified the early stages of that career, and then explains a later shift in that career.
B. It names a famous architect, outlines the primary aesthetic model evident in his work, and then offers examples illustrating his commitment to that model.

C. It provides famous examples of an architect’s projects, describes the original inspiration for those projects, and then suggests that lesser-known projects by that architect arose from other sources of inspiration.
D. It summarizes the career of a particular architect, states how that architect’s heritage influenced his career choice, and then emphasizes the impact of that architect’s career.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
跨越1920年代到1980年代，墨西哥建筑师路易斯·巴拉干（Luis Barragán）的丰富职业生涯经历了不同的阶段。正如位于瓜达拉哈拉的佩德罗·洛萨街（Calle Pedro Loza）上的房屋所体现的那样，巴拉干的许多早期项目将传统的墨西哥建筑技术与地中海设计相结合。后来，他的广泛海外旅行激发了他对现代主义和功能主义美学的关注——这些风格强调实用性，并否定传统建筑中更具装饰性的元素，这在巴拉干的皮萨罗·苏亚雷斯住宅（Pizarro Suárez House）中显而易见。

根据原文distinct phrases，first projects，later spark等内容，可以将结构概括为A，对应了general claim，early stages and then 等描述内容

• 一项名为“绿色激增”（GREEN SURGE）的多年研究考察了欧洲城市中四十四种不同类型的城市自然区（UNA）。

Based on the second sample, the research manager estimated that this type of oven takes an average of 15.4 minutes to preheat to <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mn>325</mn> <mrow> <mo>∘</mo> </mrow> </msup> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi> </mrow></math>, with an associated margin of error of 2.2 minutes. Assuming the margins of error were calculated the same way, which of the following best explains why the first sample obtained a smaller margin of error than the second sample?
selections: A. The first sample contained more ovens than the second sample.
B. The first sample contained fewer ovens than the second sample.

C. The first sample took more time on average to preheat to <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mn>325</mn> <mrow> <mo>∘</mo> </mrow> </msup> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi> </mrow></math> than the second sample.

D. The first sample took less time on average to preheat to <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mn>325</mn> <mrow> <mo>∘</mo> </mrow> </msup> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi> </mrow></math> than the second sample.
explanations: margin of error误差边界问题，样本量越大，误差边界越小，本题样本1的误差边界小，说明样本量大，选A

explanations: 代入面积公式计算K面积为4π.总面积为<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>4</mn> <mi>π</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>144</mn> <mi>π</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>148</mn> <mi>π</mi></math>，选D

question: The function f is defined by <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>7</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>4</mn> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>x</mi> </msup> <mo>+</mo> <mn>31</mn></math>. question: Levi and Marissa each have stamp collections. The number of stamps in Levi’s collection is 200% of the number of stamps in Marissa’s collection. If there are 460 stamps in Marissa’s collection, how many stamps are in Levi’s collection?

<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></math>

question:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>19</mn></mfrac><mi>r</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>57</mn></mfrac><mi>x</mi></math>

question: The function p is defined by<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">(</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>5</mn> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mo>−</mo> <mi>b</mi> <mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">)</mo> </mrow> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">(</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>5</mn> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mo>−</mo> <mi>c</mi> <mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">)</mo> </mrow></math> ,where a, b, and c are constants. In the xy-plane, the graph of <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>y</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> passes through the points <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>6</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>30</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> and <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>342</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>. What is the value of <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>10</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>+</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> ?
explanations: 式子中存在<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>5</mn> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mn>2</mn> </msup></math>部分，意味着函数对称轴为x=-5，所以p(-10)=p(0)=342.p(-4)=p(-6)=30,所以p(-10)+p(-4)=372

question:

question: A quadratic function models the height, in feet, of an object above the ground in terms of the time, in seconds, after the object was launched. According to the model, the object was launched from a height of 0 feet and reached its maximum height of 1,600 feet 10 seconds after it was launched. Based on the model, what was the height, in feet, of the object 7 seconds after it was launched?
explanations: 顶点坐标（10，1600）且过点（0，0）（ initial height of 0 feet 意味着x=0），利用顶点式<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo>−</mo> <mn>10</mn> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mo>+</mo> <mn>1600</mn></math>解出<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>a</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>16</mn></math>，再代入x=7求得<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>7</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1456</mn></math>

question:
<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>
In the given equation, a and k are constants, where <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi><mo>></mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi></math>. The sum of the solutions to the equation is <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>35</mn></math> . What is the value of a?
explanations: 问题问的是方程根的和，用韦达定理-b/a，所以式子展开写成二次方程标准形式且只需要关注x项系数即可（<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>系数为1可忽略），展开得到x的系数b为4a-3k，故-b/a=3k-4a=3k+35，解得a=-35/4

question: The equation <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>65</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup></math> gives the predicted population <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> in thousands, of a certain bacteria colony m minutes after the initial measurement, where Q is a constant greater than 1. The predicted population increases by <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></math> every 120 seconds. What is the value of p in terms of Q?
explanations: 120秒为2min，代入m=2得到变化率为<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></math> ,整理此式子可得C

question:
The Age of Innocence is a 1920 novel by Edith Wharton set in New York City in the1870s. In the novel, Newland Archer attends an opera; in the audience is May Welland, with whom he is romantically involved. Newland visualizes the details of a future with May:________

Which quotation from The Age of Innocence best illustrates the claim?
selections: A. A. “[May] dropped her eyes to the immense bouquet of lilies-of-the-valley on her knee, and Newland Archer saw her white-gloved finger-tips touch the flowers softly.”
B. “Newland Archer, leaning against the wall at the back of the club box [where his seat was], turned his eyes from the stage and scanned the opposite side of the house.”

C. “Though there was already talk...of a new Opera House which should compete in costliness and splendour with those of the great European capitals, the world of fashion was still content to reassemble every winter in the shabby red and gold boxes of the sociable old Academy[of Music].”
D. “Already |Newland's] imagination, leaping ahead of the engagement ring, the betrothal kiss and the [wedding] march from Lohengrin, pictured [May] at his side.”
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
《天真的时代》是伊迪丝·沃顿（Edith Wharton）于1920年出版的小说，背景设定在19世纪70年代的纽约市。在小说中，纽兰·阿切尔（Newland Archer）参加了一场歌剧演出，观众席上坐着梅·韦兰（May Welland），她是他正在热恋中的女性。纽兰在此时幻想着与梅的未来细节：________
中文解析：
这段文字（D选项）直接展示了纽兰·阿切尔（Newland Archer）如何幻想与梅（May）共度未来。具体来说，文本描写了他想象他们订婚、接吻以及婚礼等重要时刻，甚至脑海中已经浮现了梅在他身边的画面。通过这一描写，我们可以看出纽兰对与梅未来生活的憧憬和幻想。
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
The following text is adapted from George Eliot’s 1857 short story “The Sad Fortunes of the Rev. Amos Barton.” The Countess Czerlaski is a newcomer to the town of Milby.
I am by no means sure that if the good people of Milby had known the truth about the Countess Czerlaski, they would not have been considerably disappointed to find that it was very far from being as bad as they imagined. Nice distinctions are troublesome. It is so much easier to make up your mind that your neighbour is good for nothing, than to enter into all the circumstances that would oblige you to modify that opinion.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
selections: A. To offer commentary on a human foible that may account for why the people of Milby view the Countess Czerlaski as they do
B. To speculate on the circumstances under which the unfavorable opinion of the Countess Czerlaski that is held by the people of Milby could be improved
C. To explain why the people of Milby are somewhat correct to reproach the Countess Czerlaski for her misdeeds
D. To engage the reader’s compassion for both the Countess Czerlaski and the people of Milby by detailing their different viewpoints
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
以下文本改编自乔治·艾略特1857年的短篇小说《阿莫斯·巴顿牧师的不幸》。切尔拉斯基伯爵夫人是米尔比镇的新来者。
我并不确定，如果米尔比的好人们知道切尔拉斯基伯爵夫人的真实情况，他们是否会感到相当失望，因为事实远没有他们想象的那么糟糕。细微的区别令人困扰。下定决心认为邻居一无是处，远比深入了解所有会迫使你改变这种看法的情况要容易得多。
中文解析：
第一句虚拟语气表达实际中人们对新来的人评价不高，并指出人们很容易就觉得自己的邻居good for nothing，而不愿了解情况来修正自己的误解，于是选择A，这段话评价了人的缺点，这个内在的缺点能够解释当前镇里人对于Countess的看法。
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
The following text is from Julia Alvarez’s 2000 novel In the Name of Salomé. Salomé, a poet, is hosting guests in the front parlor of her family home, and Ramona is her sister. A salon is a social gathering for the exploration of intellectual ideas.
It was evening when the two men got up to leave. Tia Ana had already come into the room several times to see if these guests had departed yet. The front parlor had always been her special province, as she used it for her little school. Now, every evening, it turned into Salomé’s salon, as Ramona called it, and it was never in order for its transformation back to a classroom the following morning.
©2000 by Julia Alvarez

Based on the text, what most likely motivates Tía Ana’s behavior during Salomé’s salon?
selections: A. She is frustrated because she needs assistance elsewhere in the house, but Salomé is unavailable while entertaining the guests.
B. She is anxious for the gathering to disperse so that she can ready the space for her own needs.
C. She is impatient to share her plans to start a new school with the guests and hopes they will support her.
D. She finds the guests to be dull and is eager to find a way to leave the salon.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
以下文本摘自朱莉亚·阿尔瓦雷斯2000年的小说《以萨洛梅之名》。萨洛梅是一位诗人，她在家中的前客厅接待客人，而拉莫娜是她的妹妹。沙龙是一个社交聚会，旨在探讨思想和理念。
当两个男人起身准备离开时，已是傍晚。安娜姑妈已经进来好几次，看看这些客人是否已经离开。前客厅一直是她的专属领地，因为她在这里开办小学校。现在，每个晚上，这里都变成了拉莫娜所称的萨洛梅沙龙，而第二天早上，它又总是无法恢复为课堂的样子。
©2000 朱莉亚·阿尔瓦雷斯
中文解析：
Tia Ana多次进入房间看看客人是否已经离开，说明她急于让聚会散去，以便她可以为自己的需要准备空间。这表明她需要将房间从沙龙状态恢复为之前教室状态。
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Humans have a very strong bias toward right-handedness, with approximately 85-90% having right as their dominant hand. Among studies of nonhuman primates, James Welles’s 1976 study of captive chimpanzees and catarrhine monkeys reported more right-handed individuals than left-handed ones, but William C. McGrew and colleagues’1999 study of wild chimpanzees did not find a tendency toward right-handedness. It’s important to note, however, that captive animals spend significantly more time with humans than wild animals do, and therefore ________

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. the apparent difference between the two studies’ results may be partly attributable to the 1976 study using a different standard to determine handedness than the 1999 study did.
B. the right-handedness exhibited by the captive chimpanzees and catarrhine monkeys might be, in part, an effect of extended contact with humans.
C. the number of individuals in the study of captive chimpanzees and catarrhine monkeys is likely too small to support the claim that the species tends toward right-handedness.
D. the number of individuals in the study of wild chimpanzees is probably too small to support the claim that no tendency toward right-handedness was found in that population.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
人类在使用右手方面有很强的偏好，约85-90%的人以右手为主导手。在对非人类灵长类动物的研究中，詹姆斯·威尔斯（James Welles）1976年对圈养的黑猩猩和类人猴的研究报告显示，右手偏好者多于左手偏好者。然而，威廉·C·麦格鲁（William C. McGrew）及其同事1999年对野生黑猩猩的研究并未发现右手偏好的趋势。然而，值得注意的是，圈养动物比野生动物与人类的接触时间明显更多，因此________。
中文解析：
从文本最后来看captive animals和人类的接触多，于是正是因为这个原因，right-handedness也更加明显。
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Though few critics consider Vasily Grossman’s novel Stalingrad—which focuses on the experience of the Soviet Union in the early years of World War II—to be as well written as his later book Everything Flows, some compliment it despite the damage ________ Soviet censors: Gary Saul Morson in The New York Review of Books called the novel “remarkably bold.”

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

尽管很少有评论家认为瓦西里·格罗斯曼的小说《斯大林格勒》——专注于苏联在第二次世界大战早期的经历——写得如他后来的作品《万物流转》那样好，但一些评论家仍然对其表示赞赏，尽管受到了______苏联审查员的影响：加里·索尔·莫森在《纽约书评》中称这部小说“相当大胆”。

Despite表达前后对比，于是对比前面的compliment（赞美），后面是说soviet censor带来了损害，选择wrought by表示带来了负面影响

question:
Companies involved in petroleum extraction include drilling equipment among their assets. But petroleum extraction is a very carbon-intensive industry, so as social attitudes increasingly favor using less carbon-intensive sources of energy, demand for petroleum falls and the drilling equipment will eventually, or even suddenly, become a liability as reduced petroleum prices make it more difficult to recover the expense of maintaining such equipment.

What claim does the text make about the demand for petroleum?
selections: A. Companies involved in petroleum extraction are not affected by the demand for petroleum.
B. The societal preference for low-carbon energy sources is a factor in the demand for petroleum.
C. The demand for petroleum follows a predictable annual cycle.
D. Companies involved in petroleum extraction can benefit from a decline in the demand for petroleum.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
涉及石油开采的公司将钻探设备作为其资产之一。然而，石油开采是一个碳密集型行业，因此随着社会对使用低碳能源的态度日益倾向，石油的需求逐渐减少，钻探设备最终会变成负资产，因为石油价格的下降使得维持这些设备的费用更加困难。

social attitude favor using less carbon-intensive sources说明社会倾向于低碳，于是对于petroleum的需求降低，B选项正确。

question:
Why do flat-headed cats purr but jaguars roar? Researchers hypothesize that this difference between the two feline species may be partly due to a U-shaped bone in their throats called the hyoid. Flat-headed cats, which are much smaller than jaguars, have a rigid hyoid that rumbles when the cat’s larynx vibrates, resulting in a purr. By contrast, jaguars have a somewhat flexible hyoid, and the bone is attached to the skull with a stretchy ligament that flat-headed cats lack. These traits allow jaguars and most other species of big cats to produce powerful roars. The same traits may also prevent most big cats from purring.

According to the text, which trait do researchers think may contribute to a flat-headed cat’s ability to purr?
selections: A. The shape of the flat-headed cat’s larynx
B. The ligament attaching the hyoid bone to the flat-headed cat’s skull
C. The flat-headed cat’s rigid hyoid bone
D. The relative size of the flat-headed cat’s body and throat
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
为什么扁头猫会咕噜咕噜叫而美洲豹却会咆哮？研究人员推测，这两种猫科动物之间的差异部分可能与它们喉咙中的一个U形骨骼——舌骨有关。扁头猫比美洲豹小得多，拥有一个刚性的舌骨，当猫的喉部振动时，这个舌骨会发出低沉的声音，从而产生咕噜声。相比之下，美洲豹的舌骨则有一定的柔韧性，并且该骨骼通过一种扭动的韧带与颅骨相连，而扁头猫则缺乏这种结构。这些特征使得美洲豹和大多数其他大型猫科动物能够发出强有力的咆哮。而这些特征也可能使大多数大型猫科动物无法发出咕噜声。
中文解析：
段落问答中解释因为hyoid bone的差异造成flat-headed cats purr的具体原因
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Archaeologists studying the ancient city of Pompeii in Italy recently discovered a well-preserved food shop known as a thermopolium. The site contains food remains, artworks, and decorations. These items give researchers a better understanding of what daily life in Pompeii may have been like. For example, the archaeologists found a ceramic jar that they believe likely contained a meat and seafood stew.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
selections: A. To discuss the political system of Italy
B. To present a recent archaeological discovery
C. To describe a region's climate
D. To compare ancient artworks with modern ones
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
考古学家在意大利庞贝古城的研究中，最近发现了一家保存完好的食品店，被称为“热食品店”（thermopolium）。该遗址包含了食品残留物、艺术作品和装饰物。这些物品为研究人员提供了更好地了解庞贝日常生活的线索。例如，考古学家发现了一个陶瓷罐，他们认为这个罐子很可能曾装有一种肉类和海鲜炖汤。
中文解析：
文本没有涉及意大利的政治制度、气候或古代与现代艺术的比较，而是重点讲述了考古学家发现的一个食品店遗址，并描述了这个发现如何帮助我们更好地了解庞贝的日常生活。因此，答案是 B。

question:
Karl Polanyi and other historians of capitalism rarely discuss domestic capitalism in Africa before the period of European colonization, implicitly presenting capitalism as external to and imposed on Africa. Mariana Candido and other Africanist scholars have shown, however, that in parts of Africa, centrally administered industrial production, the legal treatment of land as private property, and other features of capitalism predated colonization. One reason for this discrepancy is that historians of capitalism tend to focus on longitudinal economic data drawn from archival records, which do not exist for much of precolonial Africa.

Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
selections: A. To explain why historians of capitalism and Africanist scholars disagree about which activities are features of capitalism
B. To present and account for a potentially misleading characteristic of the work of historians of capitalism
C. To describe and evaluate a method used by Africanist scholars that distinguishes their work from that of historians of capitalism
D. To summarize a debate between historians of capitalism and Africanist scholars about how to interpret longitudinal economic data from archival records
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
卡尔·波兰尼和其他资本主义历史学家很少讨论欧洲殖民化之前非洲的国内资本主义，暗含地将资本主义视为外部强加于非洲的现象。然而，玛丽安娜·坎迪多和其他非洲学者表明，在部分非洲地区，中央管理的工业生产、将土地视为私有财产的法律处理以及资本主义的其他特征早于殖民化就已经存在。这种差异的一个原因是，资本主义历史学家往往侧重于从档案记录中获取的长期经济数据，而这些数据在许多前殖民时期的非洲并不存在。
中文解析：
historians of capitalism呈现非洲的资本主义是外来的，但是Mariana等人展现出在欧洲殖民之前，非洲部分地区就存在资本主义的特征，同时还给出了discrepancy的具体原因，于是B选项正确，提出一个误导性的特征，然后解释了具体原因。

question:
Water flowing around an obstruction creates vortices (patterns of swirls) of varying size; by detecting the vortices, fish can determine the size and position of the obstruction. Testing by Yuzo R. Yanagisuru, Otar Akanyeti, and James C. Liao using models of three head shapes—narrow (low ratio of width to length), intermediate, and wide (high ratio of width to length) —showed that for large vortices, fish with intermediate heads would be better able than wide-headed fish to distinguish between vortices and general turbulence in the water. A second research team has therefore hypothesized that in low-visibility conditions, intermediate-headed fish will be more likely than wide-headed fish to detect obstructions that create large vortices.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the second research team’s hypothesis?
selections: A. A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the devil catfish (Bagarius bagarius), which has a relatively wide head, bumped into more than half of the obstructions.

B. A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the wide-headed devil catfish (Bagarius bagarius) bumped into obstructions more often than the intermediate-headed rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) did.

C. A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the intermediate-headed rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) bumped into the obstructions just as often as the wide-headed devil catfish (Bagarius bagarius) did.

D. A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that some specimens of the intermediate-headed rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) bumped into the obstructions more often than other specimens of the same fish did.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
水流绕过障碍物时会产生不同大小的涡旋（旋涡模式）；通过检测这些涡旋，鱼类可以判断障碍物的大小和位置。由Yuzo R. Yanagisuru、Otar Akanyeti和James C. Liao进行的测试表明，使用三种头部形状的模型——窄头（宽度与长度比率低）、中等头和宽头（宽度与长度比率高）——对于大的涡旋，中等头的鱼比宽头的鱼更能区分涡旋与水中的一般湍流。因此，第二个研究团队假设在能见度低的情况下，中等头的鱼比宽头的鱼更有可能发现产生大涡旋的障碍物。
中文解析：
最后的结论是intermediate-headed fish更容易detect obstructions，也就是不容易撞到障碍物，反之，wide- headed devil catfish更容易bump into obstructions对应了B选项。

• Betsy Morrow Humphrey was the lighthouse keeper at Monhegan Island Light in Maine.
• She held this position from 1862 to 1880.
• Thelma Austin was the lighthouse keeper at Point Fermin Light in California.
• She held this position from 1925 to 1941.

The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two lighthouse keepers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. As the lighthouse keeper at Point Fermin Light, Thelma Austin helped watercraft navigate at night.
B. From 1862 to 1880, the nighttime waters of Maine were made more navigable thanks to Betsy Morrow Humphrey.

question:

• If a moon orbiting a planet comes close enough to that planet, tidal forces can cause the moon to break apart.
• In a 2022 study, researchers proposed that Saturn was once orbited by a large moon they named Chrysalis.
• Their simulations indicated that Chrysalis would likely have come very close to Saturn around 160 million years ago.
• At that distance, Chrysalis would have been broken apart by tidal forces.
• The researchers hypothesized that the resulting debris formed Saturn’s rings.

B. In a 2022 study, researchers proposed that Saturn was once orbited by a large moon that broke apart.

• 研究人员推测，残留的碎片形成了土星的环。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Little is known about the life of Wong Fei-hung (1847-1925).
• He was born near Foshan, China, and gained local recognition as a physician and Hung Ga (also known as Hung Gar) Kung Fu master.
• He achieved many incredible martial arts feats—some confirmed and some rumored.
• He has become an internationally known folk hero thanks to his depiction in over a hundred films, television shows, and other media.
• In the 1991 film Once Upon a Time in China, actor Jet Li portrays Wong Fei-hung using superhuman kung fu abilities to save his community.

The student wants to emphasize the effect media had on building Wong Fei-hung’s legacy. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Thanks to his depiction in over a hundred pieces of media, Wong Fei-hung was locally known as a successful physician and Hung Ga Kung Fu master.
B. Wong Fei-hung’s abilities as a kung fu master are depicted in many media, including the 1991 film Once Upon a Time in China.
C. Various media have depicted Wong Fei-hung, the successful physician and kung fu master who became an internationally known folk hero.
D. Though he was known locally during his lifetime, Wong Fei-hung’s later depiction in television, film, and other media has turned him into an internationally known folk hero.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
•关于黄飞鸿（1847-1925）的生平知之甚少。
•他出生在中国佛山附近，并因其作为医生和洪家（也称洪拳）功夫大师而获得当地的认可。
•他完成了许多令人难以置信的武术壮举——其中一些已被证实，另一些则是传闻。
•通过在一百多部电影、电视节目和其他媒体中的塑造，他已成为一个国际知名的民间英雄。
•在1991年电影《黄飞鸿》中，演员李连杰饰演黄飞鸿，凭借超凡的功夫能力拯救他的社区。
中文解析：
题目要求强调媒体在塑造黄飞鸿传奇中的作用，D对比了黄飞鸿生前的本地知名度和他在电影、电视等媒体中的形象如何让他成为了全球知名的民间英雄。这个选项最能突出媒体对他遗产的影响。

question:
• Birds of Northern South America is an identification guidebook by ornithologists Robin Restall, Clemencia Rodner, and Miguel Lentino.

• It is identifiable by its dark violet ear patches and its short, black, straight bill.
• The little hermit is a small hummingbird found in Suriname.
• It is identifiable by its white central tail feathers and its long, black, curved bill.

Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize a similarity between the two birds?
selections: A. While each exhibits unique traits of its own, the brown violetear and the little hermit both have black bills.
B. The little hermit is a small hummingbird identifiable by its white central tail feathers and its long, black, curved bill.
C. Though they share several traits in common, the brown violetear is larger than the little hermit.
D. Birds of Northern South America is an expertly compiled guidebook by ornithologists Robin Restall, Clemencia Rodner, and Miguel Lentino.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
《北南美洲的鸟类》是由鸟类学家罗宾·雷斯塔尔 (Robin Restall)、克莱门西亚·罗德纳 (Clemencia Rodner) 和米格尔·伦蒂诺 (Miguel Lentino) 合著的鸟类识别指南。

中文解析：
题目要求强调两类鸟相似性，于是A选项正确，它们都有black bills

question:
HMS Surprise, first published in 1973, is a novel in Patrick O’Brian’s Aubrey/Maturin series, which includes twenty completed books. Some critics have found fault with the abrupt endings of HMS Surprise and other books in the series, saying that they do not finish conclusively but arbitrarily stop. But other critics argue that the books should not be thought of as discrete texts with traditional beginnings and endings but as a single incredibly long work, similar to other multivolume stories, such as John Galsworthy’s The Forsyte Saga.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It presents a reason most critics think the Aubrey/Maturin series should have the literary renown of similar works like The Forsyte Saga.
B. It summarizes a positive assessment of a particular characteristic of the Aubrey/Maturin novels.
C. It explains why many critics find the Aubrey/Maturin novels to be entertaining despite flaws in the novels’ structures.
D. It argues that the unusual structure that O’Brian uses for HMS Surprise makes it one of his most entertaining books.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
《HMS Surprise》是帕特里克·奥布莱恩（Patrick O’Brian）《奥布里/马图林系列》中的一部小说，首次出版于1973年，该系列共有二十本已完结的书籍。某些评论家批评《HMS Surprise》以及该系列其他书籍的结尾过于突兀，认为这些结局并非彻底收尾，而是草率中断。然而，另一些评论家认为，这些书籍不应被视为有传统开始和结尾的独立文本，而应该看作是一部极其漫长的单一作品，类似于其他多卷本的故事，如约翰·高尔斯沃西（John Galsworthy）的《福赛家族》（The Forsyte Saga）。
中文解析：
最后划线句子说明这些书应当被看成一部长书，而非discrete texts，这种形式就像The Forsyte Saga的系列故事一样。于是B选项a positive assessment能够整体概括对Aubrey/ Maturin novels的认可。
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Companies are providing consumers with more opportunities to purchase customized products than ever before. Whether buying customized sneakers, jewelry, or clothing, consumers can participate in the design of products to meet their specific needs and tastes. In turn, companies profit too: studies have shown that consumers are willing to pay more and wait longer for a customized product. Still, it can be difficult for companies to offer customization while keeping costs low, as the standard methods of mass production may not be able to accommodate making a unique product each time.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
selections: A. It describes a company’s recent success with new products and then explains multiple factors that may have contributed to that success.
B. It discusses several recent innovations in product manufacturing and then suggests some potential applications of those innovations.
C. It presents two contrasting product-marketing techniques and then provides examples of one of those techniques.
D. It introduces a trend in consumer products and then explains how the trend both benefits and poses a challenge to companies.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
公司如今为消费者提供了比以往更多购买定制产品的机会。无论是定制运动鞋、珠宝还是服装，消费者都可以参与产品的设计，以满足其特定需求和品味。反过来，公司也能从中获益：研究表明，消费者愿意为定制产品支付更高的价格并等待更长的时间。然而，对于公司而言，提供定制服务同时保持低成本可能会很困难，因为传统的大规模生产方法可能无法适应每次都制造独特产品的要求。
中文解析：
文本先介绍定制服务这一新趋势（customized products），然后指出公司于客户互惠互利（benefit），最后则指出成本高的问题（challenge），和D选项一致
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Vertical gene transfer involves the transmission of genetic material from a parent to offspring; horizontal gene transfer, on the other hand, involves the exchange of genetic material between organisms not in a parent-offspring relationship. While horizontal gene transfer is common among prokaryotes—single-celled organisms, such as the bacteria Brevibacillus borstelensis and Lactococcus lactis—it has rarely been observed among eukaryotes (multicellular organisms). However, new studies suggest that horizontal gene transfer is more common in eukaryotes than originally thought.

Which choice best states the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It indicates a distinction between the mechanics of two kinds of biological processes.
B. It contrasts the frequency with which a biological phenomenon has been detected in two categories of organisms.
C. It explains why a common perception of a biological process is flawed.
D. It argues that two biological phenomena are more similar than they may initially appear to be.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
垂直基因转移指的是遗传物质从父母传递给后代；而水平基因转移则是指不同个体之间交换遗传物质，这些个体之间并非父母与后代的关系。水平基因转移在原核生物（如单细胞生物，例如果胶芽孢杆菌 *Brevibacillus borstelensis* 和 乳酸乳球菌 *Lactococcus lactis*）中较为常见，但在真核生物（多细胞生物）中则较少被观察到。然而，新的研究表明，真核生物中的水平基因转移比最初认为的更为普遍。
中文解析：
while引导的从句和主句形成对比，common 和rarely代表了在单细胞和多细胞生物体内出现频率的不一样。
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
The linguistic niche hypothesis (LNH) posits that the exotericity of languages (how prevalent non-native speakers are) and grammatical complexity are inversely related, which the LNH ascribes to attrition of complex grammatical rules as more non-native speakers adopt the language but fail to acquire those rules. Focusing on two characteristics that are positive indices of grammatical complexity, fusion (when new phonemes arise from the merger of previously distinct ones) and informativity (languages' capacity for meaningful variation), Olena Shcherbakova and colleagues conducted a quantitative analysis for more than 1,300 languages and claim the outcome is inconsistent with the LNH.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Shcherbakova and colleague claim?
selections: A. Shcherbakova and colleagues analysis showed a slightly positive correlation between grammatical complexity and fusion.
B. Shcherbakova and colleagues' analysis showed a slightly negative correlation between grammatical complexity and exotericity.
C. Shcherbakova and colleagues' analysis showed a slightly positive correlation between fusion and exotericity and between informativity and exotericity.
D. D. Shcherbakova and colleagues' analysis showed a slightly negative correlation between grammatical complexity and fusion and between grammatical complexity and informativity.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
语言生态位假说（LNH）认为，语言的外来性（即非母语使用者的普遍性）与语法复杂性之间存在负相关关系，LNH将这种关系归因于随着更多的非母语使用者采用语言，但未能掌握语言中的复杂语法规则，导致这些规则的衰退。Olena Shcherbakova及其同事关注两种能够正面反映语法复杂性的特征：融合（当新音素由原本独立的音素合并而来）和信息性（语言表达有意义变化的能力）。Shcherbakova及其同事对1300多种语言进行了定量分析，并声称其结果与LNH假说不一致。
中文解析：
C选项表明更多的外来性（非母语使用者）与语言的融合性和信息性增加正相关，而根据LNH，外来性越高，语法复杂性应该越低，并且语言的融合性和信息性应该下降。因此，C选项直接反驳了LNH假说，最直接支持Shcherbakova及其同事的发现，即他们的结果与LNH不一致。
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Arthurian legends (tales related to the character of King Arthur) derive from many often contradictory sources, such as Vita Sancti Cadoci, composed in the11th century, and Culhwch and Olwen from the second half of the 12th century. Sir Thomas Malory’s 15th-century text Le Morte d’Arthur was an attempt to compile these stories into a coherent narrative. Many of Malory’s sources derive from Geoffrey of Monmouth’s History of the Kings of Britain, written in the 1130s. While neither History nor any works that predate it mention Arthur’s famous Round Table at which his knights assembled, Le Morte d’Arthur does, suggesting that ________

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. Geoffrey of Monmouth’s accounts of Arthurian legends in History are more similar overall in content to the accounts in Culhwch and Olwen than they are to the accounts in Le Morte d’Arthur.
B. when a version of an Arthurian legend contradicted the version in History, Malory preferred to include Geoffrey of Monmouth’s version in Le Morte d’Arthur.
C. Le Morte d’Arthur is more historically accurate than History, because Culhwch and Olwen had not been written when Geoffrey of Monmouth was writing his work.
D. Malory encountered the Round Table in a source that Geoffrey of Monmouth was not familiar with when writing his History.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
亚瑟王传说（与亚瑟王人物相关的故事）来源于许多往往相互矛盾的资料来源，如11世纪的《圣卡多奇生平》（Vita Sancti Cadoci）和12世纪下半叶的《库尔赫赫与奥尔温》（Culhwch and Olwen）。托马斯·马洛里的15世纪作品《亚瑟之死》（Le Morte d’Arthur）试图将这些故事编纂成一个连贯的叙事。马洛里的许多资料来源于杰弗里·蒙茅斯的《不列颠王史》（History of the Kings of Britain），该书写于1130年代。虽然《不列颠王史》及其之前的作品并未提到亚瑟王著名的圆桌——他与骑士们聚集的地方，但《亚瑟之死》却提到了这一点，这暗示着________。
中文解析：
history及其它任何之前的作品都没有提到Round Table，说明Malory写round table用到的reference是Geoffrey他们没有用到的。
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
In a 2018 article about films depicting the experiences of Black Americans, critics for the New York Times praise Madeline Anderson’s 1970 film I Am Somebody as “galvanizing” and Carl Franklin’s 1995 film Devil in a Blue Dress as “picture-perfect.” Fans of the two films hope that such ________ will attract new audiences to these works.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:

在2018年一篇关于描绘美国黑人经历的电影的文章中，《纽约时报》的评论家称赞玛德琳·安德森1970年的电影《我是某某》为“激动人心”，并称赞卡尔·富兰克林1995年的电影《蓝衣魔鬼》为“完美无缺”。这两部电影的影迷希望这样的________能够吸引新的观众观看这些作品。
中文解析：

question:
The bird species Myiobius barbatus (the bearded flycatcher) shares some territory in French Guiana with Thamnomanes caesius (the cinereous antshrike), which emits a loud alarm call when it detects predators. Biologist Ari Martinez and colleagues recorded T. caesius alarm calls and played them in the vicinity of wild M. barbatus. Finding that the birds often froze in place or scattered into vegetation upon hearing the calls, they concluded that M. barbatus associates T. caesius alarm calls with danger.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Martinez and colleagues’ conclusion?
selections: A. Other bird species than M. barbatus also showed a tendency to freeze in place or scatter into vegetation when Martínez and colleagues played T. caesius alarm calls.
B. Martinez and colleagues played alarm calls from different T. caesius individuals and observed no significant variation in the responses of M. barbatus.
C. In some instances, M. barbatus froze in place or scattered into vegetation when Martinez and colleagues approached but before they began playing sounds.
D. When Martinez and colleagues played control sounds of random noise in the vicinity of M. barbatus, the birds displayed no reaction.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
鸟类物种胡须飞蝇（Myiobius barbatus）与灰背蚁鹊（Thamnomanes caesius）在法属圭亚那的部分区域共享栖息地。灰背蚁鹊在发现捕食者时会发出响亮的警报声。生物学家Ari Martinez及其同事录制了灰背蚁鹊的警报声，并在野生胡须飞蝇附近播放这些声音。研究发现，胡须飞蝇在听到这些警报声后，常常会停顿不动或飞散到周围的植被中。研究人员由此得出结论，胡须飞蝇将灰背蚁鹊的警报声与危险联系在一起。
中文解析：
文本结论是M.barbatus认为T alarm calls是危险声音，为了支持这个结论，，D是满足的，因为M鸟对于control sounds of random noise没有反应，是可以说明T alarm call的作用的，其实有很多可能的evidence（这个题在未来注意选项的变体）
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Optimal foraging theory (OFT) holds that animals’ foraging behaviors reflect cost-benefit trade-offs that vary by species and with dynamic ecological circumstances. One such circumstance is lunar intensity, which Joel Brown and colleagues found to be negatively associated with foraging by Arizona pocket mice but Deborah J. Curtis and colleagues found to be positively associated with foraging by mongoose lemurs. This discrepancy is explicable in terms of OFT: the lemurs’ greater reliance on vision means that higher lunar intensity benefits them more than it benefits the mice.

Which choice best describes the finding made by Curtis and colleagues, as presented in the text?
selections: A. Increased lunar intensity is more beneficial for mongoose lemurs than it is for Arizona pocket mice.
B. As lunar intensity increases, mongoose lemurs increase their foraging activity.
C. During periods of high lunar intensity, mongoose lemurs increase their reliance on vision.
D. As lunar intensity increases, Arizona pocket mice reduce their foraging activity.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
最佳觅食理论（OFT）认为，动物的觅食行为反映了根据物种和动态生态环境变化的成本-收益权衡。其中一种环境因素是月光强度，Joel Brown及其同事发现月光强度与亚利桑那袋鼠鼠的觅食活动呈负相关，而Deborah J. Curtis及其同事则发现月光强度与狐獴猴的觅食活动呈正相关。这种差异可以通过最佳觅食理论来解释：狐獴猴对视觉的依赖较大，因此较强的月光对它们的益处超过对袋鼠鼠的益处。
中文解析：
Deborah J. Curtis Deborah J. Curtis及其同事则发现月光强度与狐獴猴的觅食活动呈正相关，所以对应B。注意此题问的是Curtis的研究不是两个不同团队的研究
exam_name: 2024年12月第1&2套阅读语法（其中M2和第4套重复，第4套不录入）

question:
Biologist Grace Herzel and colleagues conducted a study of how butterfly color and weather conditions relate to butterfly behavior, which wouldn’t have been possible without data gathered by students and other amateur science enthusiasts in the community. Considering over three years’ worth of data, the researchers found that white butterflies were observed on green flowers more often than any other butterflies were, and that butterflies were observed to feed more often on cloudy days than on other days.

According to the text, which factors seemed to be linked to the behavior of butterflies in Grace Herzel and colleagues’ study?
selections: A. Weather conditions but not butterfly color
B. Butterfly color but not weather conditions
C. Neither butterfly color nor weather conditions
D. Both butterfly color and weather conditions
explanations:
题目文本翻译：

question:
Prolonged exposure to anthropogenic noise (sounds from human sources like traffic or mining) can affect animals, as Graeme Shannon and colleagues found in a 2016 study of black-tailed prairie dogs. Researchers conducted a meta-analysis of studies of how such noise affects animals and found that, for every study, relevant traits or behaviors of the animals were observably different between the exposed group and the otherwise similar but unexposed group. Although, on average, studies of mammals showed larger differences than studies of amphibians did, for every class of animals examined, there were individual studies showing differences well above the average for mammals. Therefore, the results of the meta-analysis suggest that ________

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. the differences that studies attribute to exposure to anthropogenic noise are likely to be more pronounced for amphibians than they are for mammals.
B. some studies of amphibians found larger effects of exposure to anthropogenic noise than some studies of mammals did.
C. the difference found in the study conducted by Graeme Shannon and colleagues was likely larger than the average difference for studies of black-tailed prairie dogs included in the meta-analysis.
D. the studies in the meta-analysis that examined mammals were more likely than those that examined amphibians to specify whether the observed effects were detrimental.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
长期暴露于人为噪声（如交通或采矿等人类来源的声音）可能会影响动物，正如Graeme Shannon和其同事在2016年对黑尾土拨鼠的研究中发现的那样。研究人员对人为噪声如何影响动物的研究进行了荟萃分析，结果发现，在每项研究中，接触噪声的动物组与未接触但具有类似特征的动物组之间的相关特征或行为存在明显差异。尽管平均而言，哺乳动物研究中观察到的差异比两栖动物研究中更大，但在所研究的每一类动物中，都有个别研究显示的差异远远高于哺乳动物的平均值。因此，这项荟萃分析的结果表明，________
中文解析：
最后的结论指出有些个体individuals表现出的差异高于mammals的平均数，那么就说明B正确，也就是amphibians有些比mammals的个体还要更多的影响。考察平均值与个体值差异

question:
Text 1
In separate studies, Stephen Meding and Robert J. Zasoski and Xinhua He and colleagues examined whether plants transfer nutrients to one another using a common mycorrhizal network (CMN) —a lattice of fungal strands in the soil. Meding and Zasoski excluded all pathways other than the CMN by using barriers to keep the plants’ root systems separate while allowing mycorrhizal strands through—a crucial step He and colleagues’ study did not take.
Text 2
Meding and Zasoski took the necessary precaution of separating the plants’ root systems (thereby excluding root-to-root transmission). However, any barrier used must allow the thread-like hyphae of a CMN to pass through, and this permeability would also allow liquids through. Thus, the researchers’ experimental design cannot ensure that any nutrient transfer observed can be attributed to a CMN and not to some other pathway.

Based on the texts, the author of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 would most likely agree with which statement?
selections: A. The barriers used in Meding and Zasoski’s study effectively excluded root-to-root transmission of nutrients.
B. A barrier that is impervious to both roots and fungal strands is necessary to evaluate nutrient transfer via a CMN.
C. Excluding root-to-root transfer of nutrients between plants is sufficient to ensure that any observed nutrient transfer must involve a CMN.
D. He and colleagues’ study did not find convincing evidence of nutrient transfer between individual plants.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
文本 1
在不同的研究中，Stephen Meding 和 Robert J. Zasoski，以及 Xinhua He 和同事们研究了植物是否通过共同的菌根网络（CMN）——一种土壤中的真菌丝状结构——相互转移养分。Meding 和 Zasoski 通过使用屏障将植物的根系分开，同时允许菌根丝通过，从而排除了除了 CMN 以外的所有途径，这一步骤是 He 和同事们的研究所没有采取的关键步骤。
文本 2
Meding 和 Zasoski 采取了必要的预防措施，将植物的根系分开（从而排除了根际间的传输）。然而，任何使用的屏障必须允许 CMN 的丝状菌丝通过，而这种通透性也会让液体通过。因此，研究人员的实验设计无法确保观察到的任何养分转移可以归因于 CMN，而不是通过其他途径进行的转移。
中文解析：
第一篇文章的第2句话和第二篇文章的第一句话都明确承认了Meding团队能排除营养物质通过根部系统传播。

question:
Neuroscientist Kiyohito Iigaya and colleagues developed a computational model to predict how much a person will enjoy a particular work of art on a scale from 1 (not at all) to 4 (very much). They then recruited participants to use the same scale to rate several sets of paintings in various styles and calculated the correlation between the ratings predicted by the model and those reported by the participants. Assuming participant P7 gave equal ratings to the impressionist and color-field paintings, the data in the graph suggest that the model predicted that ________

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
selections: A. P7’s ratings for impressionist and color-field paintings would differ from one another.
B. P7 would derive more aesthetic pleasure from impressionist paintings than from color-field paintings.
C. P7’s ratings for impressionist and color-field paintings would equal one another.
D. P7 would derive less aesthetic pleasure from impressionist paintings than from color-field paintings.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
神经科学家伊井喜人（Kiyohito Iigaya）及其同事开发了一个计算模型，用于预测一个人对特定艺术作品的欣赏程度，评分范围从1（完全不喜欢）到4（非常喜欢）。接着，他们招募了参与者，要求其使用相同的评分标准对几组不同风格的画作进行评分，并计算模型预测的评分与参与者实际评分之间的相关性。假设参与者P7对印象派画作和色域画作给出了相同的评分，那么图表中的数据表明，模型预测______。
中文解析：
首先，注意correlation只代表P7的真实给分和model的预测分数是否一致，通过图表可以看出两者不一样，但是P7评分一样，所以model预测的P7对于两者的评分有所不同，导致了correlation（相关度）的不同

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Generally, an object will heat up when twisted.
• The twisting of an object is known as torsion.
• A 2019 study led by Zunfeng Liu and Ray Baughman tested the torsional heating of various fibers.
• When a 0.7-millimeter-thick sample of single-ply nickel-titanium (NiTi) wire was twisted, its average surface temperature increased by 21.3°C.
• When a 2-millimeter-thick sample of ethylene propylene diene monomer (EPDM) rubber fiber was twisted, its average surface temperature increased by 12℃.

The student wants to contrast the two samples. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. In 2019, researchers studied the effect of torsional heating on various fibers, including samples of EPDM rubber and single-ply NiTi wire.
B. The EPDM rubber sample used in the 2019 study was thicker than the single-ply NiTi wire sample.
C. Twisting an object will generally cause its temperature to increase, a process known as torsional heating.
D. When the fibers were twisted as part of the 2019 study, the surface temperature of both samples increased.
explanations:
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
•通常，当物体被扭曲时，它会变热。
•物体的扭曲现象被称为扭转。
•2019年，由Zunfeng Liu和Ray Baughman领导的一项研究测试了各种纤维的扭转加热效应。
•当一根厚度为0.7毫米的单层镍钛（NiTi）线被扭转时，其平均表面温度上升了21.3°C。
•当一根厚度为2毫米的乙烯丙烯二烯单体（EPDM）橡胶纤维被扭转时，其平均表面温度上升了12°C。
中文解析：
题目要求对比两个样本差异，于是根据notes，差异有厚度和twisted之后升高的温度，因此B正确，对比了样本厚度差异

question:
The following text is from Jhumpa Lahiri’s 2003 novel The Namesake. Gogol, a child, is at a beach in Massachusetts with his father.
He watches his father raise a kite within minutes into the wind, so high that Gogol must tip his head back in order to see, a rippling speck against the sky. The wind whips around their ears, turning their faces cold.
@2023 by Jhumpa Lahiri

As used in the text, what does the word “tip” most nearly mean?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
他看到父亲在风中放起风筝，不到几分钟，风筝就升得很高，高到戈戈尔不得不仰起头才能看见，成了天际中一个闪烁的小点。风在他们耳边呼啸，冷风吹得他们的脸颊发凉。
中文解析：
文中的画面是放风筝，于是Gogol仰着头才能看到，tip的意思是lean

Dandelions are a kind of weed found in North America. Although dandelions are unwelcome in gardens and on farms, weeds like this do provide some benefits. For example, they can be helpful to pollinators.

B. A variety of plants grow in North America.

question:
Literary production in the period after the Mexican Revolution (which lasted from 1910-1920) was ________, with writers like Octavio Paz contributing to the outpouring of poetry, fiction, essays, and more. Unfortunately, this flood of interesting writing can divert scholarly attention from the fascinating work of nineteenth-century figures like Guillermo Prieto.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
墨西哥革命（1910-1920年）后的文学创作是_______，像奥克塔维奥·帕斯（Octavio Paz）这样的作家为诗歌、小说、散文等文学形式的涌现做出了贡献。不幸的是，这股有趣的写作洪流可能会分散学术界对像吉列尔莫·普里埃托（Guillermo Prieto）这样十九世纪人物的迷人作品的关注。

根据文本中outpouring，this flood of writing 等提示，可以推断前面时表达该时期写作较多，多产丰富选择prolific

question:
The Chauvet Cave paintings—detailed paintings of animals found in what is now France and dating from 30,000-32,000 years ago—are thought of as art today, but how the people of the time understood the paintings is ________ . They may have thought of the paintings as something akin to art in our modern sense, but it is entirely possible that they did not—we simply cannot say for certain.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
这幅描绘动物的肖维洞穴壁画——这些画作出土于现在的法国，距今大约有30,000到32,000年——今天被视为艺术，但当时人们如何理解这些画作却是______的。他们可能将这些画作看作类似于我们现代意义上的艺术，但也完全有可能他们并非如此——我们无法确定这一点。
中文解析：
but前后是对比，前面讲现在认为是艺术，但是从前人们如何看待是不知晓的，于是选择unknown

question:
Describing adverbs “as damaging to a writer,” novelist Graham Greene is one of several authors and literary critics who have recommended minimizing the use of adverbs, especially those ending in -ly (e.g., “obediently”), in works of fiction. To investigate the prevalence of -ly adverbs in novels, author and statistician Ben Blatt used natural language processing—machine learning technology that reads and interprets text—to calculate the rates at which these words occur in the novels of Ernest Hemingway, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954. Blatt concluded that in Hemingway’s oeuvre, there is a negative correlation between -ly adverb proliferation and perceived literary merit.

Which choice most effectively support Blatt’s conclusion?
selections: A. Whereas Hemingway’s acclaimed novel The Sun Also Rises has one of the lowest -ly adverb rates among Hemingway’s works, F. Scott Fitzgerald’s classic novel The Great Gatsby has the lowest -ly adverb rate among Fitzgerald’s novels.

B. Whereas Hemingway used on average 80 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words in the 10 novels of Hemingway’s that Blatt investigated, Toni Morrison, winner of the 1993 Nobel Prize in Literature, used on average 76 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words in her novels.

C. In his celebrated novel A Farewell to Arms, Hemingway used 67 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words, whereas 67% of celebrated authors’ novels that have fewer than 50 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words have been classified as great by critics.

D. In The Sun Also Rises, which is widely recognized as a literary masterpiece, Hemingway used 63 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words, whereas in his less-acclaimed novel True at First Light, Hemingway used 102 -ly adverbs per 10,000 words.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
小说家格雷厄姆·格林（Graham Greene）将副词描述为“对作家有害的”，他是几位提议减少使用副词的作家和文学评论家之一，特别是那些以-ly结尾的副词（例如，“obediently”）。为了研究-ly副词在小说中的普遍性，作家兼统计学家本·布拉特（Ben Blatt）使用自然语言处理技术——一种读取和解释文本的机器学习技术——来计算这些词在欧内斯特·海明威（Ernest Hemingway）小说中的出现频率。布拉特得出结论，在海明威的作品中，-ly副词的泛滥与文学作品的感知文学价值之间存在负相关关系。
中文解析：
根据最后一句海明威的作品里ly副词词尾的适用频率和literary merit成反比，D选项举了两个例子，masterpiece比另外一步less-acclaimed novel适用的ly副词要少可以支持篇章末尾的结论
exam_name: 2024年11月第6套阅读语法（只保留M1，M2和第5套重复）
