question:
“A Pair of Silk Stockings” is an 1897 short story written by Kate Chopin. In the story, Mrs. Sommers is depicted as sometimes making decisions without conscious deliberation: _______

Which quotation from “A Pair of Silk Stockings” most effectively illustrates the claim?
selections: A. “She handed the girl a five-dollar bill and waited for her change and for her parcel. What a very small parcel it was!”
B. “She had no time — no second of time to devote to the past. The needs of the present absorbed her every faculty.”

C. “She was not thinking at all. She seemed for the time to be taking a rest from that laborious and fatiguing function and to have abandoned herself to some mechanical impulse that directed her actions and freed her of responsibility.”
D. “Mrs. Sommers selected a black pair and looked at them very long and closely. She pretended to be examining their texture, which the clerk assured her was excellent.”
explanations:
A.中文解析
文本证据题三类题型之一illustrate用细节阐述文本观点，文本重点是making decisions without conscious deliberation,C选项中not thinking，mechanical impulse, freed her of responsibility都能说明了她的冲动与自发，与题目的without conscious deliberation（没有深思熟虑）是一致的。
B.题目文本翻译
《一双丝袜》是凯特·肖邦于1897年写的短篇小说。在故事中，梭默太太有时被描述为在没有意识思考的情况下做出决定：________。

question:
Florence Este and Lily Everett were among the 300 artists who exhibited at the 1913 Armory Show, a groundbreaking New York City art exhibition that introduced modernism to American audiences. Though shocking at the time, an abstract cubist painting exhibited by Marcel Duchamp— one of several works that received scorn from critics— ______ the Western art canon more than a century later.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 主语是单数painting，于是只能选项谓语三单的现象，C选项has entered是正确答案。

question:
Increasing the heat on an uncovered boiling pot of water does not increase the temperature of the water. What increases is the rate at which the water turns to ______ a pressure cooker pot, though, an airtight seal traps the vapor in the pot, creating pressure that allows the temperature of the water to increase past its boiling point.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 这是两个句子间的连接，不是长句内部连接，选A，句号连接两个完整句子。

question:
Each year, the Nobel Prize in Literature is given to an author who has, in the words of its founder Alfred Nobel, “produced the most outstanding work in an idealistic ______ in 1912, for instance, judges recognized Gerhart Johann Robert Hauptmann “[for] his fruitful, varied and outstanding production in the realm of dramatic art.”

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 前面完整句的连接需要用分号，其它选项都无法连接完整句子。

question:
Paintings by the renowned twentieth-century US ______ were featured in Artist to Artist, an exhibition at the Smithsonian Art Museum that paired the works of artists whose career trajectories intersected in meaningful ways.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
selections: A. artists Thomas Hart Benton, and Jackson Pollack,
B. artists: Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollack,
C. artists Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollack
D. artists, Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollack
explanations: US artists修饰人物的名字，不用符号分割，主语和谓语（were featured）之间不用符号分割，于是选项C正确。

question:
Generally, sleek vehicles are more aerodynamic than bulkier ones. The streamlined nose of the Airbus A320 jet, ______ helps it glide through wind with relative ease, while a boxy pickup truck encounters more wind resistance, making it less aerodynamic.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
第一句是概括讲sleek vehicles are more aerodynamic 即光滑的交通工具更加符合空气动力学，后面则是具体的飞机例子，选项A ，for example适合
B.题目文本翻译
通常情况下，造型流线的车辆比更笨重的车辆更具有空气动力学效果。空客A320喷气式飞机的流线型机头 ______ 有助于它相对轻松地穿越风，而一个笨拙的皮卡遇到更多风阻，使其空气动力学性能较差。

question:
The London Array, an offshore wind farm located off the coast of England, produces about 630 megawatts (MW) of electricity per year. _____ England’s Hornsea Project One offshore wind farm, which generates the most power of any single offshore farm, produces 1,218 MW of electricity.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
两个不同地点的风力发现场，不同的发电量进行比较用by comparison。
B.题目文本翻译
伦敦阵列是位于英格兰海岸外的一座海上风力发电场，每年产生约630兆瓦（MW）的电力。_____ 英格兰的Hornsea Project One海上风电场产生了任何单个海上风电场中最大的电力，达到1,218兆瓦的电力。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●A merchant vessel is any ship hired to carry cargo or passengers.
●Common merchant vessels include bulk carriers, cruise liners, and oil tankers.
●A vessel’s carrying capacity is also known as its deadweight tonnage (DWT).
●In 2021, there were a total of 1,236 merchant vessels registered in Greece.
●The combined DWT of these vessels was 64.9 million tons.

The student wants to explain what a merchant vessel is and provide examples. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. There were a total of 1,236 ships hired to carry cargo or passengers registered in Greece in 2021.
B. The carrying capacity of bulk carriers, cruise liners, and oil tankers is measured in deadweight tonnage.
C. A merchant vessel is any ship hired to carry cargo or passengers— like bulk carriers, cruise liners, and oil tankers.
D. In total, Greece’s 1,236 merchant vessels had a carrying capacity of 64.9 million tons in 2021.
explanations:
A.中文解析
题目要求explain what a merchant vessel is and provide examples,于是需要定语和例子，C选项前面半句是定义，破折号后是具体的例子。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个话题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 商船是指被聘用运载货物或乘客的任何船只。
- 常见的商船包括散货船、游轮和油轮。
- 船只的载重量也被称为其总吨位（DWT）。
- 截至2021年，希腊共有1,236艘商船注册。
- 这些船只的总载重量为64.9百万吨。

question:
● Springtails are a group of noninsect hexapods (six-legged animals).
● Researchers Claudia Marcela Ospina-Sánchez, Felipe N. Soto-Adames, and Grizelle González conducted a study to determine how many springtail species are present in Puerto Rico.
● They found a total of 146 springtail species.
● They found 1 springtail species belonging to the genus Hemisotoma.
● They found 3 springtail species belonging to the genus Sphaeridia.

Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to present the study and its findings?
selections: A. In Puerto Rico, the genus Hemisotoma contains one springtail species, and the genus Sphaeridia contains three springtail.

B. According to a study by researchers Claudia Marcela Ospina-Sanchez, Felipe N. Soto-Adames, and Grizelle Gonzalez, there are 146 springtail species present in Puerto Rico, including one from the genus Hemisotoma and three from the genus Sphaeridia.

C. Researchers Claudia Marcela Ospina-Sanchez, Felipe N. Soto-Adames, and Grizelle Gonzalez studied springtails in Puerto Rico, and they wanted to know how many species there are in the genus Hemisotoma and the genus Sphaeridia.
D. There are 146 species of springtail (noninsect hexapods) in Puerto Rico, but there are more species from the genus Sphaeridia than from the genus Hemisotoma.
explanations:
A.中文解析
根据题目需要present study and its findings，notes中的最后三行是findings，于是B选项具体列举的findings包括数据在内，符合题目要求。
B.题目文本翻译
● 弹簧尾虫是一类非昆虫类六足动物。
● 研究人员Claudia Marcela Ospina-Sánchez、Felipe N. Soto-Adames和Grizelle González进行了一项研究，以确定波多黎各有多少种弹簧尾虫物种。
● 他们总共发现了146种弹簧尾虫物种。
● 他们发现了1种属于Hemisotoma属的弹簧尾虫物种。
● 他们发现了3种属于Sphaeridia属的弹簧尾虫物种。

question:
In 1974, Mexican chemist Mario Molina and US chemist F. Sherwood Rowland discovered that chemicals called CFCs were harmful to the ozone layer. Their research was extremely influential in the fight against CFCs. ______ it laid the foundation for a 1987 treaty that phased out the use of CFCs across the globe.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
前面讲述他们的研究extremely influential，后面是influential的具体展示，也就是1987年的treaty，是前面后置，后面具体的情况，选specifically。
B.题目文本翻译
1974年，墨西哥化学家马里奥·莫利纳和美国化学家F.舍伍德·罗兰发现了称为氟氯碳化合物（CFCs）对臭氧层有害。他们的研究对于对抗CFCs产生了极大的影响。______ 这为1987年的一项条约奠定了基础，该条约逐步淘汰了全球范围内对CFCs的使用。

question:
With a blend of traditional design elements, such as arched Gothic ceilings, and modern ones, such as floor-to-ceiling _____ design splits the difference between old and new, a mixture that is increasingly seen in home interiors in the US.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 这是一个长句，状语前置和主句间逗号隔开，transitional design是主句的主语。

question:
In March 1862, John Ahoy joined the US Navy, where he went on to serve aboard the USS Pinola during the US Civil War. ________ he earned a place in US history as one of the war’s few Chinese-born American soldiers.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
In doing so 表达because of that，翻译为正因为如此，常常用来引导结果，尤其是结果出乎意料，这里第一句表达John Ahoy参军的事情，后一句形容其成为美国历史上有自己的地位，是罕见的Chinese-born American soldiers，这符号前因后果，且结果令人惊讶。
B.题目文本翻译
在1862年3月，约翰·阿霍伊加入了美国海军，随后在美国内战期间担任了USS Pinola号的服役。______ 他成为美国历史上少数几位作为中国出生的美国士兵之一的人物。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●Musicians around the world have used protest songs to raise awareness about human rights violations.
●US folk singer Aunt Molly Jackson released the protest song “Poor Miner’s Farewell” in 1932.
●It exposed the unlivable wages and dangerous working conditions coal miners faced in Kentucky during the 1920s and 1930s.
●South African singer-songwriter Hugh Masekela released the protest song “Bring Him Back Home” in 1987.
●It called on the South African government to free Nelson Mandela, an anti-apartheid leader who’d been unjustly imprisoned.

The student wants to contrast the song “Poor Miner’s Farewell” with the song “Bring Him Back Home.” Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. While both are protest songs, “Poor Miner’s Farewell” is about coal miners in Kentucky, whereas “Bring Him Back Home” is about the anti-apartheid leader Nelson Mandela.
B. Hugh Masekala’s song “Bring Him Back Home,” released in 1987, called on the South African government to free Nelson Mandela.
C. The songs “Poor Miner’s Farewell” and “Bring Him Back Home” both raised awareness about human rights violations.
D. Released in 1932 by Aunt Molly Jackson, the song “Poor Miner’s Farewell” was a protest against the unlivable wages and dangerous working conditions faced by Kentucky coal.
explanations:
A.中文解析
题目要求contrast两首歌，于是A选项whereas是表示对比，对比两首歌作为protest song不同的主题内容。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个话题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 世界各地的音乐家利用抗议歌曲来唤起人们对人权侵犯的意识。
- 美国民谣歌手Aunt Molly Jackson于1932年发布了抗议歌曲《Poor Miner’s Farewell》。
- 歌曲揭露了1920年代和1930年代肯塔基州煤矿工人面临的无法生存的工资和危险工作条件。
- 南非歌手兼创作人Hugh Masekela于1987年发布了抗议歌曲《Bring Him Back Home》。
- 歌曲呼吁南非政府释放被不公正监禁的反种族隔离领袖纳尔逊·曼德拉。

question:
Like all species of baleen whales, the humpback whale feeds on tiny creatures known as krill by filtering water through bristlelike keratin structures called baleen plates. In this way, baleen whales can eat up to 30 percent of their total mass per day. And while no one would call the humpback whale small— it can have a mass as high as 30,000 kg— it is one of the smaller baleen whales and is much smaller than the fin whale, which can weigh a whopping 80,000kg and consume as much as 24,000kg of krill per day.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
selections: A. It draws a distinction between the sizes of the humpback whale and the fin whale and then presents a feature that they have in common.
B. It details a relationship between humpback and fin whales and krill and then discusses an unexpected consequence of a change in baleen whale populations.
C. It discusses a unique feature of the humpback whale and how the lack of that feature in the fin whale explains differences in the two species’ behavior.
D. It describes a characteristic shared by all baleen whales and then illustrates a difference between the humpback whale and the fin whale that is relevant to that characteristic.
explanations:
A.中文解析
Overall structure需要按照句子顺序概括文本，本文第一句先讲like all of baleen whales, 也就是一个common characteristic，然后介绍了两类whale体型大小差异，也就是D选项的a difference related，都相应吃体重30%质量的食物。
B.题目文本翻译
像所有须鲸类动物一样，座头鲸通过将水通过鲸须板这种毛细的角质结构过滤，从而以食用称为磷虾的微小生物。通过这种方式，须鲸类动物每天可以摄入总体质量的高达30%。虽然没有人会称座头鲸为小动物——它的体重可能高达30,000千克——但它是较为较小的须鲸类动物之一，比鲸鲨要小得多，鲸鲨可能重达惊人的80,000千克，并每天消耗高达24,000千克的磷虾。

question:
Today, the Michelin Guide is widely known as the arbiter of fine dining, but when it was created in 1900, it was little more than a marketing gimmick; brothers Andre and Edouard Michelin sought to increase profits for their tire company by encouraging their customers to drive across France, visiting the guide’s recommended hotels and restaurants along the way. Nevertheless, the guide soon grew in scope and _______ its modest French eateries were replaced with some of the most esteemed restaurants from around the world, including La Yeon in Seoul and Sushi Shikon in Hong Kong.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 两个完整句子连接逗号+and是可以的，其它选项都不可以连接完整句。

question:
In what is now Minnesota, the Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community operates the Hocokata Ti, a cultural center. Relying on traditional knowledge to guide the design of exhibits, this institution presents Dakota history and culture to the tribe’s citizens. The Comanche Nation, a tribe in Oklahoma, employs a similar strategy in its own cultural center. Both centers contrast with museums that aren’t Indigenous-led; when displaying Indigenous artifacts, such museums tend to anticipate mainly non-Indigenous audiences and rely on Euro-centric strategies for designing exhibits.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It defines a term used earlier in the sentence.
B. It addresses a potential criticism of a claim made earlier in the sentence.
C. It elaborates on a claim made earlier in the sentence.
D. It acknowledges an exception to the general principle proposed earlier in the sentence.
explanations:
A.中文解析
最后一句划线句解释了non-indigenous-led museums针对的audience群体与依赖的策略，是对前文museums that aren’t Indigenous-led的解释，于是选C选项。
B.题目文本翻译
在如今的明尼苏达州，夏科皮梅达瓦坎顿苏族社区运营着Hocokata Ti文化中心。该机构依靠传统知识来指导展览设计，向部落公民展示达科他族的历史和文化。奥克拉荷马州的科曼切族国也在其文化中心采用类似的策略。这两个中心与不由土著人领导的博物馆形成对比；在展示土著人的文物时，这些博物馆往往主要预期非土著观众，并依赖以欧洲为中心的策略来设计展览。

question:
Text 1
A conservation group representing 11 tribal nations in the Great Lakes region reported to various state and federal natural resources agencies operating in the region that the northern wild rice plant (manoomin in the Ojibwe language) will likely fare significantly worse than the American crow (aandeg in Ojibwe) due to rising temperatures over the next 50 years. This collaborative approach has helped build trust between government and tribal groups, which will likely improve the quality of any joint conservation projects.
Text 2
State and federal natural resources agencies are increasingly incorporating traditional ecological knowledge from tribal groups in the agencies’ plans to address threats to natural resources due to increasing temperatures. This approach has helped build positive relationships between tribal groups and these agencies and furthermore tends to lead to better conservation outcomes.

Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
selections: A. A collaborative approach to conservation is likely to help reduce the predicted temperature increases in the Great Lakes region.
B. In the Great Lakes region, conservation efforts focused on the northern wild rice plant are likely to be more effective than those focused on the American crow.
C. Natural resources conservation projects are likely to benefit from collaboration between tribal and government groups.
D. In the Great Lakes region, it is more important to focus conservation efforts on the northern wild rice plant than it is to focus on the American crow.
explanations:
A.中文解析
题目要求答两篇文章的共同特征，那么text 1 and 2的共同点是认可tribal and government groups之间的合作会带来好处，本题有很多变体，不要思维定式，比如错误选项D在其它变体题目中出现过。
B.题目文本翻译
文本1
代表五大湖地区的11个部落的一个保护组织向该地区各州和联邦自然资源机构报告，称未来50年内，由于气温升高，北方水稻植物（奥杰布韦语中的manoomin）的状况可能会比美洲乌鸦（奥杰布韦语中的aandeg）遭受更严重的影响。这种合作方式有助于建立政府与部落团体之间的信任，这可能会改善任何联合保护项目的质量。
文本2
州和联邦自然资源机构越来越多地将部落团体的传统生态知识纳入机构计划中，以应对由气温升高引起的自然资源威胁。这种方法有助于建立部落团体与这些机构之间的积极关系，而且往往导致更好的保护结果。

question:
An analysis by Alain Elayi and colleagues of coins minted in Sidon in the fifth and fourth centuries BCE reveals a change in their composition over time: while a coin from circa 450 BCE contains about 98% silver and 1% copper, a coin from 367 BCE (the end of Ba’alsillem II’s reign) contains 74.2% silver and 24.7% copper, giving it a relatively yellowish appearance that traders would have noticed. Because coins with a silver content below 80% were widely considered unsuitable for trade, Elayi et al. speculate that a crisis in confidence in the currency occurred in Sidon around 367 BCE, which was likely relieved— despite Sidon’s persistent oppressive financial obligations— as a result of Ba’alsillem II’s successor Abd’astart I’s decision to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. keep the amount of silver in Sidonian coins consistent with that in coins minted in 367 BCE but decrease their weight.
B. proclaim that the percentage of silver in coins suitable for trade would be raised to a threshold higher than 80%.
C. fund the mining of some copper deposits that were not available to Ba’alsillem II.
D. begin minting heavier coins with a proportion of silver to copper similar to that in coins minted in 367 BCE.
explanations:
A.中文解析
根据文本silver content占比低于80%不适合交易，从而产生货币的信任危机，缓解的方式（relieve）就是保持银占比达到80%以上，那么A选项保持银含量不变，减轻硬币的总重量，从而提高银占比的方式是可行的。
B.题目文本翻译
阿兰·埃莱伊及其同事对公元前五世纪和四世纪在西顿铸造的硬币进行的分析显示，随着时间的推移，它们的成分发生了变化：大约公元前450年的硬币含有约98%的银和1%的铜，而公元前367年（巴阿尔西莱姆二世统治末期）的硬币含有74.2%的银和24.7%的铜，使其呈现出相对黄色的外观，这是贸易商会注意到的。由于银含量低于80%的硬币被广泛认为不适合用于贸易，埃莱伊等人推测，公元前367年左右，西顿的货币信心危机发生了，这很可能是因为巴阿尔西莱姆二世的继任者阿卜德阿斯塔尔特一世做出了决定而得以缓解——尽管西顿的财政负担持续加重——这一决定是________。

question:
Water flowing around an obstruction creates vortices (patterns of swirls) of varying size; by detecting the vortices, fish can determine the size and position of the obstruction. Testing by Yuzo R. Yanagisuru, Otar Akanyeti, and James C. Liao using models of three head shapes— narrow (low ratio of width to length), intermediate, and wide (high ratio of width to length)— showed that for large vortices, fish with intermediate heads would be better able than wide-headed fish to distinguish between vortices and general turbulence in the water. A second research team has therefore hypothesized that in low-visibility conditions, intermediate-headed fish will be more likely than wide-headed fish to detect obstructions that create large vortices.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the second research team’s hypothesis?
selections: A. A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the Synodontis macropunctata, which has a relatively wide head, bumped into more than half of the obstructions.

B. A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low visibility conditions found that some specimens of the intermediate-headed dusky smooth-hound (Mustelus canis) bumped into the obstructions more often than other specimens of the same fish did.

C. A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low-visibility conditions found that the wide-headed Synodontis macropunctata bumped into obstructions more often than the intermediate-headed dusky smooth-hound (Mustelus canis) did.
D. A study using obstructions that created large vortices in low visibility conditions found that the intermediate-headed dusky smooth-hound (Mustelus canis) bumped into the obstructions.
explanations:
A.中文解析
题目要求支持最后一句话second research team’s hypothesis, 也就是支持intermediate-headed fish 更容易detect obstructions，换句话说就是wide-headed fish更容易撞到障碍物，和C选项是一致的。
B.题目文本翻译
水流经阻碍物会产生不同大小的涡旋（涡流图案）；通过检测这些涡旋，鱼类可以确定阻碍物的大小和位置。由柳良裕三（Yuzo R. Yanagisuru）、奥塔尔·阿坎耶蒂（Otar Akanyeti）和詹姆斯·C·廖（James C. Liao）进行的实验使用了三种头部形状的模型——窄头（宽度与长度比低）、中等头和宽头（宽度与长度比高）——结果显示，在大涡流情况下，头部中等的鱼类比头部宽的鱼类更能够区分涡旋和水流的一般湍动。因此，第二个研究团队假设在能见度低的条件下，头部中等的鱼类比头部宽的鱼类更有可能检测到产生大涡旋的阻碍物。

question:
The Reckoning and Resilience (2022) exhibition at Duke University’s Nasher Museum of Art in Durham, North Carolina, is dedicated to the work of thirty North Carolina artists, including Lien Truong. Kennedi Carter, and Meg Stein. Although the Nasher Museum has focused exhibitions entirely on North Carolina artists before, as it did previously in the photography exhibition Across County Lines, the breadth of disciplines in Reckoning and Resilience sets it apart.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the underlined claim?
selections: A. Reckoning and Resilience and Across County Lines were curated to emphasize works that are not owned by the Nasher Museum.
B. Truong is a painter, Carter is a photographer, and Stein is a sculptor.
C. The Nasher Museum has a world-class collection of contemporary art that includes many paintings and sculptures from artists both inside and outside North Carolina.
D. Carter is a North Carolina photographer, as were all of the artists featured in Across County Lines.
explanations:
A.中文解析
划线句子是让步状语从句部分指出了Nasher Museum共同点就是关注North Carolina artists，主句则指出了本次展览Reckoning and Resilience的特色，即the breadth of disciplines ,也就是学科范围之广度。B选项painter，photographer，sculptor能够支持。
B.题目文本翻译
杜克大学纳舍艺术博物馆（Nasher Museum of Art）在北卡罗来纳州达勒姆市（Durham, North Carolina）举办的“清算与韧性（2022）”展览致力于展示三十位北卡罗来纳州艺术家的作品，包括连忠（Lien Truong）、肯尼迪·卡特（Kennedi Carter）和梅格·斯坦（Meg Stein）。尽管纳舍艺术博物馆之前曾完全专注于北卡罗来纳州艺术家的展览，就像在摄影展“穿越县界”中所做的那样，但“清算与韧性”展览中各种学科的广泛涵盖使其与众不同。

question:
Arthurian legends (tales related to the character of King Arthur) derive from many sources, such as Preiddeu Annwfn, composed around 900, and the Mabinogion from the 12th and 13th centuries. One of the most significant sources, Geoffrey of Monmouth’s History of the Kings of Britain, was written in Latin in the 1130s; some material from it was later adapted by the Norman poet Wace into the Roman de Brut in 1155. But while no source before 1155 includes references to the famous Round Table at which Arthur’s knights assembled, both the Roman de Brut and Sir Thomas Malory’s 15th-century compilation of Arthurian legends, Le Morte d’Arthur, do. It can therefore be inferred that _______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. Le Morte d’Arthur is more historically accurate than History, because the Mabinogion had not been written when Geoffrey of Monmouth was writing his work.
B. Malory did not use Preiddeu Annwfn as a source for information he presented about the Round Table.
C. Geoffrey of Monmouth was unaware of stories of the Round Table when composing his History, though historians know that works containing such stories were available to him.
D. Geoffrey of Monmouth’s accounts of Arthurian legends in his History are more similar overall in content to the accounts in the Mabinogion than they are to the accounts in Roman de Brut.
explanations:
A.中文解析
Preiddeu Annwfn 创作于900年，早于1155年，于是不会有reference to the Round Table，因此15世纪Malory创作中呈现Round Table不可能用Preiddeu Annwfn 作为自己的source。选择B选项。
B.题目文本翻译
亚瑟王传说（关于亚瑟王角色的故事）源自许多来源，如约公元900年创作的《Preiddeu Annwfn》，以及12至13世纪的《马宾尼悟集》。其中最重要的来源之一是杰弗里·蒙茅斯的《不列颠诸王史》，于1130年代以拉丁文写成；该作品中的部分材料后来被诺曼诗人瓦斯在1155年改编为《不列颠之罗马》。但是在1155年之前的任何来源中都没有提到亚瑟的骑士聚集的著名圆桌，而《不列颠之罗马》和托马斯·马洛里的15世纪亚瑟王传说汇编《亚瑟之死》都有这方面的内容。因此可以推断________。

question:
The fossil remains of the individual known as KNM-KP 271, discovered in Kenya in 1965, can help paleoanthropologists not only identify steps in the evolution of hominids but also ______ the Pliocene epoch generally, revealing important details about the time in which KNM-KP 271 lived.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
句子结构not only .....but alse...表达递进关系，前面是identify steps ，后面是illuminate the Pliocene epoch generally，呼应了后面的revealing important details
B.题目文本翻译
肯尼亚1965年发现的编号为KNM-KP 271的个体的化石遗骸不仅可以帮助古人类学家确定人科动物演化过程中的阶段，而且还能揭示普通更新世时期的______，从而揭示KNM-KP 271生活的时代的重要细节。

question:
The following text is adapted from Guy de Maupassant’s 1884 short story “A Recollection,” from the collection Guy de Maupassant Short Stories (translated by Albert M.C. McMaster et al. in 1903). The narrator is taking a boat down the Seine river from Paris, France, to the surrounding countryside.
I took up a position in the bows [front of the boat], standing up and looking at the quays, the trees, the houses and the bridges disappearing behind us. And suddenly I perceived the great viaduct of Point du Jour which blocked the river. It was the end of Paris, the beginning of the country, and behind the double row of arches the Seine, suddenly spreading out as though it had regained space and liberty, became all at once the peaceful river which flows through the plains, alongside the wooded hills, amid the meadows, along the edge of the forests.

Based on the text, which choice best expresses the narrator’s characterization of the Seine?
selections: A. As the journey progressed from Paris to the countryside, the waters of the Seine gradually cleared.
B. The journey along the Seine is mostly peaceful, but the current intensifies briefly under the Point du Jour.
C. The waters of the Seine are more confined and rough in Paris than they are in the countryside.
D. The Seine’s loveliness is surpassed only by that of Paris.
explanations:
A.中文解析
Characterization of Seine主要是看文章的前面对于水流描述的对比，the end of Paris，the beginning of the country，水流因为空间开阔变得spreading out， 变得peaceful，这些可以让我们得出在巴黎段更加的confined and rough（狭窄湍急），在乡村段更加平缓开阔。
B.题目文本翻译
以下文本改编自盖伊·德·莫泊桑（Guy de Maupassant）1884年的短篇小说《回忆》，收录于1903年阿尔伯特·M·C·麦克马斯特（Albert M.C. McMaster）等人翻译的《盖伊·德·莫泊桑短篇小说集》中。叙述者正乘船沿塞纳河从法国巴黎到周边乡村。
我站在船头，仰望着码头、树木、房屋和消失在我们身后的桥梁。突然，我看到了挡住河道的朱尔日大桥。这是巴黎的尽头，乡村的开始，在双排拱门背后，塞纳河突然蔓延开来，仿佛重新获得了空间和自由，一瞬间变成了流经平原、沿着木丘旁、穿过草地、森林边缘的宁静河流。

question:
Rafael Nunez and colleagues studied how members of the Yupno, an Indigenous group in Papua New Guinea, conceptualize time. The researchers recorded Yupno speakers explaining certain temporal words and phrases, such as abjuk sonda, a present-oriented expression that translates to “this week,” and coded each speaker’s manual gestures. Previous research has found a tendency in many cultures to make temporal distinctions using spatial concepts and gestures, particularly along egocentric axes (i.e., relative to the orientation of the speaker): for instance, Spanish speakers often refer to the left/right axis to describe events in time. In an anthropology paper, a student claims that the tendency toward ego-based conceptualizations of time is universal.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the student’s claim?
selections: A. Yupno speaker points in opposite directions when indicating a past event versus a future event.
B. Some Yupno grammatical structures used when talking about time are also used in Spanish.
C. When Yupno speakers who are outdoors use gestures to refer to the future, they point uphill from their current location regardless of which way they are facing.
D. Although Yupno speakers and Spanish speakers both use gestures to indicate orientation in time, Yupno speakers tend to use fewer gestures overall when speaking than Spanish speakers do.
explanations:
A.中文解析
Weaken the claim,就是否定最后一句内容，最后一句的关键词是ego-based conceptualization of time is universal,那么C选项中Yupno speakers point uphill 则是based on outside factor不是ego-based，于是可以削弱文章的claim。
B.题目文本翻译
拉斐尔·努涅斯（Rafael Nunez）和同事研究了巴布亚新几内亚原住民尤普诺（Yupno）部落如何构想时间。研究人员记录了尤普诺族人解释某些时间词汇和短语的过程，比如“abjuk sonda”，这是一个表示“本周”的面向现在的表达方式，并记录了每位说话者的手势。先前的研究发现，在许多文化中，人们倾向于使用空间概念和手势来进行时间区分，特别是沿着以自我为中心的轴线（即相对于说话者的朝向）：例如，西班牙语使用左/右轴来描述时间事件。在一篇人类学论文中，一位学生声称，朝向以自我为基础的时间概念化倾向是普遍存在的。

question:
The following text is from Sarojini Naidu’s 1896 poem “Alabaster.”
Like this alabaster box whose art
Is frail as a cassia-flower, is my heart,
Carven with delicate dreams and wrought
With many a subtle and exquisite thought.

Which choice best describes the function of the two underlined portions in the text as a whole?
selections: A. They describe the subjects, one physical and one abstract, of a comparison that extends throughout the text.
B. They symbolize two attitudes, one logical and one emotional, that are contrasted throughout the text.
C. They indicate potential reactions, one hoped for and one feared, to a decision the speaker considers throughout the text.
D. They provide examples, one literal and one figurative, of a change that the speaker describes throughout the text.
explanations:
A.中文解析
这是修辞中比喻的考察，a comparison between alabaster box and my heart,前者physical，后者abstract，这个比喻贯穿整首诗歌。
B.题目文本翻译
以下文本摘自Sarojini Naidu的1896年诗歌《雪白》：
就像这块雪白的盒子，它的工艺
像一朵薄荷花一样娇嫩，我的心，
雕刻着精致的梦想，铸造
伴随着许多微妙而精致的思想。

question:
Before the Mariner 2 mission completed a successful flyby of Venus in 1962, astronomers’ ideas about the planet were little more than ______. Venus’s atmosphere is so thick that Earth-based observations had yielded very little information about the planet.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
Before...讲述之前的认知仅仅是猜想而已，little more than表示不过是，仅仅是，第二句话具体解释大气层后，没有太多的信息了解，所以前面的猜想选择conjecture。
B.题目文本翻译
在1962年“水手2号”任务成功飞越金星之前，天文学家对该行星的想法几乎只是______。金星的大气层非常厚，以至于地面观测几乎没有提供有关该行星的任何信息。

question:
Over 600 languages are spoken in New York City in addition to English— one can find Bambara spoken in the neighborhood of Kingsbridge, for example, or Ghale in Jackson Heights. English is the most common, with 65% of New Yorkers speaking it at home; Spanish is second, at 20%. A linguist hypothesizes that a Spanish dialect— a variation differing from the parent language in some of its vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar— has developed in New York City, partly due to its linguistic interaction with English. Previous research shows that younger speakers of nonmajority languages are more likely to borrow words from the majority language of a region than are older speakers. If the linguist’s hypothesis is correct, it is therefore likely to be the case that _______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. the proportion of younger speakers who use a Spanish dialect specific to New York City is higher in neighborhoods where many languages are spoken than in neighborhoods where Spanish and English predominate.
B. both the number of languages spoken in New York City and the number of dialects of each of those languages will increase over time.
C. Spanish used by younger speakers in New York City tends to have more words borrowed from other nonmajority languages than borrowed from English.
D. younger speakers of Spanish in New York City would be more likely to use a dialect specific to New York City than older speakers living in the same neighborhood would be.
explanations:
A.中文解析
文本最后是猜想的重点依据，也就是non-majority languages人群中，年轻人比老一辈更有可能borrow words from majority language，具体可以理解为西班牙语的年轻一代比老一代更可能从英文中借来词汇使用，这和D选项的表意一致，注意dialect specific to New York City根据文本定义就是因为borrow words而和老一辈不同的Spanish dialect。
B.题目文本翻译
纽约市除了英语外还有600多种语言被使用——例如在金斯布里奇社区可以找到班巴拉语，或者在杰克逊海茨可以找到加勒语。英语是最常用的语言，65%的纽约人在家中使用英语；西班牙语排名第二，占20%。一位语言学家假设，纽约市已经发展出了一种西班牙语方言——一种与母语在一些词汇、发音和语法方面有所不同的变体，部分原因是由于其与英语的语言互动。先前的研究表明，非主流语言的年轻说话者更有可能从该地区的主要语言中借用词汇，而老年说话者则较少。如果语言学家的假设是正确的，那么很可能会发生这种情况________。

question:
The work of Tobias Gerstenberg et al. on tracking eye movements supports a theory that people engage in _______ thinking when making causal judgments: when subjects were asked to look at two colliding billiard balls and judge whether one caused or prevented the other’s movement through a gate, their eyes looked at where the target ball would have gone if the ball that altered its path did not exist.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
Tracking eye movement 在后面台球相撞的例子中，人们的眼睛会看向球本来应该的走向，这里的虚拟语气可以看出，本来球已经改变了方向，但是我们会看向事实上不存在的方向，于是选择counterfactual 的英文意义是what did not happen or what does not exist, 和文本需要的意义一致counterfactual thinking。
B.题目文本翻译
Tobias Gerstenberg等人对追踪眼动的研究支持了一个理论，即人们在做因果判断时会参与_______思维：当被试被要求观看两个相撞的台球，并判断一个是否导致或阻止了另一个通过大门运动时，他们的眼睛会盯着目标球会到达的位置，如果改变路径的球不存在的话。

question:
Interest in mechanotransduction, the mechanism by which cells sense and convert mechanical stimuli into biochemical signals, is expanding because of innovative work by biomedical scientists—many of whom, like neuroscience and biophysics expert Elba Serrano, _______ this mechanism to better understand how the body’s neurological and biomechanical systems interact.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 判断从句的主语many of whom是复数，于是对应的谓语动词study，其它都是对应主语为单数。

question:
If you had turned on the radio in the winter of 1970, chances are you would have heard the hit _______ “Oh What a Day” by the Dells. The song spent ten straight weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 chart that year.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: the hit song 这个表达还不够具体明确，所以后面的名字不能和前面the hit song用符号分开。

question:
Integrating insights from economics and psychology, researchers in the field of behavioral economics explore a variety of topics. Lucia Macchia of the University of Oxford studies socioeconomic ______ other researchers investigate areas such as organizational behavior and personal finance.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 副词词组for instance所在的句子和前一句间形成例证关系。第一句和第二句间构成例证关系，for instance需要放在第二句内，第二三句间是完整句子，需要分号连接。

question:
Mountain climbing routes that incorporate metal rungs and cables are known as via ferratas, from the Italian phrase for “iron path.” As climbing these routes has shifted from a mode of travel to a sporting activity, modern via ferratas are rarely designed to simply reach a summit. _____ new routes favor recreation over utility, aiming to provide a challenging climb or showcase dramatic scenery.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
逻辑词前一句的内容是...are rarely designed to simply reach a summit, 后一句是类似的意义，但是更加细致的描述了路线的设计，于是选择递进关系more often。
B.题目文本翻译
融入金属阶梯和钢缆的登山路线被称为via ferratas，源自意大利短语“铁路”。随着攀登这些路线从一种旅行方式转变为一项体育活动，现代via ferratas很少被设计只是为了到达山顶。 _____ 新的路线更偏向于娱乐而非实用性，旨在提供具有挑战性的攀登或展示戏剧性景观。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●Documentary TV programs in the slow TV genre consist of uninterrupted broadcasts of ordinary events in real time.
●Reinflytting is a Norwegian slow TV program.
●The 9-day-long program documented a wild reindeer migration from their winter to summer pastures.
●It first aired in 2017.
●Slow TV has been called “the world’s most boring television.”
●American journalist Nathan Heller praises it, writing that “it affords a visceral kind of armchair tourism.”

The student wants to use a quotation to refute the claim that slow TV programs are boring. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. While some have praised slow TV for affording “a visceral kind of armchair tourism,” others have called it “the world’s most boring television.”
B. Far from boring, slow TV programs can provide a “visceral kind of armchair tourism,” as Heller puts it, whereby viewers can watch reindeer migrations in real time.
C. With broadcasts of ordinary events, like reindeer migrations, occurring in real time, slow TV just might be “the world’s most boring television.”
D. Reinflytting can afford a “visceral kind of armchair tourism,” as Heller puts it.
explanations:
A.中文解析
题目要求 use a quotation to refute the claim that slow TV programs are boring, B选项 far from boring就是反驳，“visceral kind of armchair tourism”就是恰当的quotation。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，一个学生记录了以下内容：
- 慢电视类别的纪录片电视节目由实时的普通事件的不间断广播组成。
- “Reinflytting”是挪威的一部慢电视节目。
- 这个持续9天的节目记录了野生驯鹿从冬季到夏季牧场的迁徙过程。
- 该节目首次播出于2017年。
- 慢电视被称为“世界上最无聊的电视”。
- 美国记者纳森·海勒称赞它，写道“它提供了一种贴身的椅子旅游体验。”

question:
William Kittredge’s short essay on “krummholz,” a word referring to twisted and stunted trees growing near the tree line, is included in the collection Home Ground: A Guide to the American Landscape. The book wasn’t written solely by ______ other authors, such as Linda Hogan and Barry Lopez, also contributed essays.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: However作为副词，所在句和前一句形成转折关系，第一句和第二句间存在转折关系，需要however在第二句内，第二句和第三句完整句连接需要分号，不可以用逗号。于是选A选项。

question:
●At London and New York Fashion Weeks, fashion designers debut new clothing collections.
●Color consultants create trend reports on the popular colors at a given Fashion Week.
●A report on 2018 New York Fashion Week noted the popularity of a delicate petal pink shade that was warm in tone and soft in intensity.
●A report on 2021 London Fashion Week noted the popularity of a stirring ocean blue shade that was cool in tone and bright in intensity.

Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to describe a color that was popular at 2021 London Fashion Week?
selections: A. Shades of delicate petal pink and stirring ocean blue have both been featured in Fashion Week reports prepared by color consultants.
B. Each Fashion Week, color consultants compile reports on the colors that have been popular among designers.
C. The shade favored by designers at 2021 London Fashion Week was a departure from the warm, soft shade of delicate petal pink that had proved popular at 2018 New York Fashion Week.
D. At 2021 London Fashion Week, many designer collections featured a cool, bright shade of stirring ocean blue.
explanations:
A.中文解析
题目要求描述2021年London Fashion Week 的popular color，于是D选项满足，a cool, bright shade of stirring ocean blue.
B.题目文本翻译
- 在伦敦和纽约时装周上，时装设计师推出新的服装系列。
- 色彩顾问们会为某一时装周上流行的颜色创建趋势报告。
- 2018年纽约时装周的一份报告指出了一种淡粉色调的热门色调，色调温暖而强度柔和。
- 2021年伦敦时装周的一份报告指出了一种令人振奋的海洋蓝色调的热门色调，色调凉爽而强度明亮。

question:
Recent pollen analyses of the Aran Islands have led some researchers to propose that the now treeless islands were once wooded. This hypothesis _______ that certain trees, such as P. sylvestris, survived without interruption or human intervention throughout the Holocene cannot stand, researchers Michael O’Connell and Karen Molloy counter, unless other explanations can first be ruled out.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: This hypothesis是第二句话的主语，谓语是cannot stand，suggesting that是分词短语作后置定语。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●Chromosomes are cellular structures that contain genes.
●Genes carry critical instructions for determining an organism’s physical traits.
●Members of the same species typically have the same number of chromosomes.
●The fennec fox (Vulpes zerda) and the red fox (Vulpes vulpes) are species of foxes.
●The fennec fox has sixty-four chromosomes.
●The red fox has thirty-four chromosomes.

The student wants to specify how many chromosomes the fennec fox has. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. The fennec fox (Vulpes zerda) and the red fox (Vulpes vulpes) both have chromosomes, but the fennec fox has more than the red fox does.
B. The fennec fox (Vulpes zerda) has sixty-four chromosomes.
C. The fennec fox’s chromosomes contain genes, which are critical to determining an organism’s physical traits.
D. The red fox, a species of fox, has thirty-four structures called chromosomes.
explanations:
A.中文解析
题目要求回答fennec fox具体有多少条chromosomes，B选项回答sixty-four。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，一个学生记录了以下内容：
- 染色体是细胞结构，其中包含基因。
- 基因携带决定生物体外貌特征的关键指令。
- 同一物种的成员通常具有相同数量的染色体。
- 貉狐（Vulpes zerda）和红狐（Vulpes vulpes）是狐的物种。
- 貉狐有六十四条染色体。
- 红狐有三十四条染色体。

question:
With his room-sized installation Unicorn/My Private Sky, Norwegian artist Borre Saethre succeeds in creating a whimsical yet perplexing experience. _______ when visitors set foot inside the fantastically blue room and encounter the life-sized stuffed unicorn preening at the far end of it, they are both dazzled and confused— as if stepping into a strange and enchanting new world.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
第一句和第二句的意义是相近的，都是表达进入这样的房间以及具体的感受，于是选择indeed来表达强调。
B.题目文本翻译
挪威艺术家博雷·萨特雷凭借他的房间大小的装置作品《独角兽/我的私人天空》成功地创造出一种奇幻而令人困惑的体验。 _______ 当游客踏入这个梦幻般的蓝色房间，看到远端摆放着真人大小的填充独角兽时，他们既被眼花缭乱又感到困惑——仿佛踏入了一个奇异而迷人的新世界。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●The Mohs scale of mineral hardness is a ten-point scale that orders minerals by hardness based on their ability to scratch other minerals.
●Minerals with larger numbers are harder than minerals with smaller numbers and can leave visible scratches on them.
●Minerals with smaller numbers are softer than minerals with larger numbers and cannot leave visible scratches on them.
●The mineral calcite has a Mohs scale number of 3.
●The mineral apatite has a Mohs scale number of 5.
●The mineral topaz has a Mohs scale number of 8.

The student wants to make a generalization about minerals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Based on their Mohs scale numbers, topaz (8) is harder than apatite (5), and apatite is harder than calcite (3).
B. Topaz can leave visible scratches on calcite, which is why topaz has a higher number than calcite on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness.
C. Any mineral with a Mohs number of 8, like topaz, can scratch a mineral with a Mohs number of 5, like apatite.
D. The Mohs scale can be used to order calcite, topaz, and apatite by their ability to scratch other minerals.
explanations:
A.中文解析
题目要求make a generalization about minerals, 只有C选项符合对mineral的generalization，A太具体了，D选项是对mohs的总结，不是对 mineral的总结。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，一个学生记录了以下内容：

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●The fifth Solvay Conference on Physics was held in 1927.
●It brought together twenty-nine of the era’s preeminent scientists to discuss the emerging field of quantum theory.
●The conference famously featured a debate between physicists Albert Einstein and Niels Bohr.
●Bohr proposed that subatomic entities like electrons had only probable realities until they were observed.
●Einstein argued that subatomic entities like electrons had a reality independent of observation.
●Bohr’s position, later called the Copenhagen interpretation, remains the most widely accepted theory of quantum mechanics.

The student wants to place Einstein’s argument within its historical context. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. During the dawn of quantum theory, Einstein maintained the independent reality of some subatomic entities, although Bohr’s opposing interpretation would become the widely accepted view.
B. The attendees of the 1927 Solvay Conference were among the preeminent scientists of their era, including Einstein, who opposed Bohr’s proposal.
C. In 1927, Einstein and Bohr engaged in a famous debate; Bohr’s argument, later called the Copenhagen interpretation, would remain popular decades after.
D. At the 1927 Solvay Conference on Physics, Einstein disagreed with Bohr’s argument that subatomic entities like electrons had a reality independent of observation.
explanations:
A.中文解析
题目要求Einstein’ argument, A选项 Einstein maintained ... 就是爱因斯坦的argument，后半句although Bohr’s interpenetration would have become the widely accepted view,就是题目要求的historical context。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，一个学生记录了以下内容：
- 第五届索尔维物理学会议于1927年举行。
- 该会议汇集了当时二十九位杰出科学家，讨论新兴的量子理论领域。
- 会议中著名的一场辩论是由物理学家阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦和尼尔斯·玻尔之间展开的。
- 玻尔提出，亚原子实体如电子只有在观察之前有可能的现实。
- 爱因斯坦则认为亚原子实体如电子存在与观察无关的现实。
- 玻尔的立场，后来被称为哥本哈根解释，仍然是量子力学中最广泛接受的理论。

question: A line intersects two parallel lines, forming four acute angles and four obtuse angles. The measure of one of the acute angles is <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>9</mn> <mi>x</mi> <mo>−</mo> <mn>490</mn> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>∗</mo> </msup></math>. The sum of the measures of one of the acute angles and three of the obtuse angles is <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>18</mn> <mi>x</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>w</mi> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>∗</mo> </msup></math>. What is the value of w?
explanations: 根据题意，直线相交产生4个角，相邻角之和180°，对顶角相等，其中一个锐角为(9x-490)°，相邻钝角为180-(9x-490)=(-9x+670)°,一个锐角+3个钝角（1锐角+1钝角为180）为180+2*（-9x+670）=1520-18x，所以w为1520

question: The exponential function f is defined by <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></math>, where a and b are positive constants. If <math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>82</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, where n is a constant, what is the value of b?
explanations: 指数函数中下一个数值是上一个数值b倍，即f(n)/f(n-1)=b，本题中f(n)=（18/100）f(n-1),即f(n)/f(n-1)=0.18，所以b=0.18

question:
The following text is from Charles Chesnutt’s 1905 novel The Colonel’s Dream. Mr. French and Mr. Kirby work together.
Mr. French, the senior partner, who sat opposite Kirby, was an older man-a safe guess would have placed him somewhere in the debatable ground between forty and fifty; of a good height, as could be seen even from the seated figure, the upper part of which was held erect with the unconscious ease which one associates with military training.

As used in the text, what does the word “placed” most nearly mean?
explanations:
题目文本翻译
以下文字选自查尔斯·切斯纳特1905年的小说《上校的梦》。弗兰奇先生和柯比先生一起工作。
坐在柯比对面的资深合伙人弗兰奇先生年纪比较大——保守地说，他的年龄应该在40到50岁之间;甚至从那坐着的人身上也可以看出，他的上半身是挺直的，不知不觉就像在接受军事训练一样轻松。
中文解析：
基于文本中的guess和后面between forty and fifty，可以看出place表示推测，估计estimate

question:
The Dhaka Stock Exchange in Dhaka, Bangladesh, is a dedicated exchange for investing in companies operating in Bangladesh, ensuring those companies receive certain regulatory oversight. Knowing this can ________ potential investors’ worries about bureaucratic minutiae and thereby allow them to instead focus on identifying sound business opportunities.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译
孟加拉国达卡的达卡证券交易所(Dhaka Stock Exchange)是一家专门投资于在孟加拉国经营的公司的交易所，确保这些公司受到一定的监管。了解这一点可以减轻潜在投资者对官僚主义细节的担忧，从而使他们能够专注于发现良好的商业机会。
中文解析
第一个句子中ensuring those companies receive regulatory oversight,这样的做法和最后的focus on identifying sound business opportunities，都说明这段话表述了积极的意义，于是应该是要减少投资人的担忧。选择D选项assuage，表示ease or release。

question:
Immanuel Wallerstein and other historians of capitalism rarely discuss domestic capitalism in Africa before the period of European colonization, implicitly presenting capitalism as external to and imposed on Africa. Crislayne Alfagali and other Africanist scholars have shown, however, that in parts of Africa, wage labor competition, the manufacture of surplus goods for monetized sale, and other features of capitalism predated colonization. One reason for this discrepancy is that historians of capitalism tend to focus on longitudinal economic data drawn from archival records, which do not exist for much of precolonial Africa.

Which statement about Alfagali and other Africanist scholars is best supported by information in the text?
selections: A. They likely make use of different types of evidence than historians of capitalism typically rely on.
B. They likely differ from historians of capitalism in the methods they use to derive longitudinal economic data from archival records.
C. They likely have a different view about which activities should be considered capitalist in nature than historians of capitalism do.
D. They likely view capitalism as having been more beneficial for Africa than historians of capitalism do.
explanations:
题目文本翻译
伊曼纽尔·沃勒斯坦(Immanuel Wallerstein)等资本主义历史学家很少讨论欧洲殖民时期之前非洲的国内资本主义，含蓄地将资本主义呈现为外部和强加于非洲的资本主义。然而，Crislayne Alfagali和其他非洲学者已经表明，在非洲的部分地区，雇佣劳动力竞争、生产剩余商品用于货币化销售，以及资本主义的其他特征早在殖民之前就存在了。造成这种差异的一个原因是，资本主义历史学家倾向于关注从档案记录中提取的纵向经济数据，而这些数据在殖民前的非洲并不存在。
中文解析
文章解释说，像Crislayne Alfagali这样的非洲学者已经证明，在殖民统治之前，资本主义在非洲的部分地区存在，他们使用的证据不同于资本主义历史学家通常依赖的从档案记录中提取的纵向经济数据。这表明，非洲主义学者使用不同类型的证据来支持他们关于非洲资本主义的论点。

question:
Animals use many objects as tools to achieve goals more easily. Such goals include grooming, finding food, and protecting themselves. For a long time, people thought tool use was unique to primates. Elephants and other animals, though, have busted the myth that tool use requires hands. Inventively, elephants use branches to scratch themselves. Woodpecker finches also get creative. They use cactus spines to pry insects from hiding places.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
selections: A. To establish that tool use doesn’t indicate intelligence
B. To compare tool use in humans with tool use in woodpecker finches
C. To question the belief that birds are intelligent
D. To argue that a variety of animals use tools
explanations:
题目文本翻译
动物使用许多物体作为工具来更容易地实现目标。这些目标包括梳理毛发、寻找食物和保护自己。很长一段时间以来，人们认为使用工具是灵长类动物独有的。然而，大象和其他动物已经打破了使用工具需要手的神话。大象很有创意地用树枝挠自己。啄木鸟也很有创造力。它们用仙人掌刺把昆虫从藏身之处撬出来。
中文解析
这个选择最好地抓住了文本的主要目的，即强调使用工具实现各种目标的动物的多样性，挑战传统观念；不仅灵长类动物或有手的动物，很多动物都可以用工具。

question:
The following text is from Virginia Woolf’s 1919 novel Night and Day. The text describes a gathering of young artists and intellectuals.
One person after another rose, and, as with an ill-balanced axe, attempted to hew out his conception of art a little more clearly, and sat down with the feeling that, for some reason which he could not grasp, his strokes had gone awry. As they sat down they turned almost invariably to the person sitting next them, and rectified and continued what they had just said in public.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portions in the text as a whole?
selections: A. To reveal individuals’ uncertainty about the meaning of a particular artwork
B. To emphasize the extent of individuals’ struggles to articulate thoughts on art
C. To highlight the physical effort involved in individuals’ construction of large-scale works of art
D. To draw attention to individuals’ discontent with the group’s conversation about art
explanations:
题目文本翻译
以下文字摘自弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫1919年的小说《夜与日》。这篇文章描述了青年艺术家和知识分子的聚会。
一个又一个人站起来，像拿着一把不平衡的斧头，想把他的艺术观念砍得更清楚一些，然后坐下来，觉得由于某种他不知道的原因，他的笔划出了差错。当他们坐下时，他们几乎总是转向坐在他们旁边的人，纠正并继续他们刚刚在公共场合所说的话。
中文解析
在聚会上的个人面临着试图清楚地表达他们对艺术的想法和观念。他们把自己比作一把“不平衡的斧头”，感觉自己“挥错了”，这传达了他们在表达自己的想法时所经历的挑战。这强调了他们在有效沟通艺术方面的努力程度，是比喻的手法。

question:
Wireless headphones and other small electronic devices sometimes use batteries that can’t be taken out and swapped for new ones. Environmental policy researcher Jessika Richter warns that once these internal batteries stop working, the devices become ________ and are typically thrown away, creating harmful waste.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译
无线耳机和其他小型电子设备有时使用的电池不能取出来换新的。环境政策研究员杰西卡·里希特警告说，一旦这些内部电池停止工作，这些设备就会变得无用，通常会被扔掉，产生有害的废物
中文解析
Stop working, thrown away, harmful waste全都是重要的线索词，于是选择同义词useless，无用的。

question:
New Zealand has classified the rainbow lorikeet as an invasive species that could harm some of the country’s native species. But researchers Alejandro Camacho and Jason McLachlan have pointed out that Earth’s climate is changing in ways that challenge such classifications. Climate changes may force animals from their current ranges. Climate changes may also create good habitats in areas where a species couldn’t live previously. These observations suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. New Zealand was previously home to some rainbow lorikeets but they were outcompeted by invading species.
B. even if Earth’s climate doesn’t change in the way scientists predict, the rainbow lorikeet will likely establish itself in New Zealand.
C. labels like the one that New Zealand has applied to the rainbow lorikeet reflect environmental conditions that may not persist.
D. it’s useful at present for New Zealand to distinguish between invasive and native species in some instances but not in the case of the rainbow lorikeet.
explanations:
题目文本翻译
新西兰将彩虹吸蜜鹦鹉列为入侵物种，可能会伤害该国的一些本土物种。但研究人员亚历杭德罗·卡马乔和杰森·麦克拉克兰指出，地球气候正在以挑战这种分类的方式变化。气候变化可能会迫使动物离开它们目前的活动范围。气候变化也可能在物种以前无法生存的地区创造良好的栖息地。这些观察结果表明______
中文解析
新西兰给彩虹鹦鹉贴上的invasive species标签反映了环境条件，但是这种状况随着环境的进一步变化，可能不会持续下去。

question:
It is hardly an exaggeration to characterize modern Hawaiian literature as having _______ the traditional stories of the Kānaka Maoli, the Native Hawaiian people. In a variety of ways, Samuel Kamakau, Kristiana Kahakauwila, and other acclaimed writers have drawn on these stories to craft a rich portrait of the Hawaiian Islands and their people.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译
将现代夏威夷文学描述为借鉴Kānaka毛利人(夏威夷原住民)的传统故事并不夸张。塞缪尔·卡马考(Samuel Kamakau)、克里斯蒂安娜·卡哈考威拉(Kristiana Kahakauwila)和其他广受赞誉的作家以各种方式借鉴这些故事，为夏威夷群岛及其人民描绘了一幅丰富的肖像。
中文解析
A沉思B取代C预期D派生自，text中have drawn on these stories和derived from是同意表达。

question:
Uncle Vanya: Scenes from Country Life in Four Acts is an 1898 play by Anton Chekhov, originally written in Russian. In the play, Professor Serebrakoff and his wife Helena have come to stay at their country estate, which Vanya manages with the help of Sonia, the professor’s daughter from a previous marriage. Chekhov portrays the professor as being unable to adjust to living at the country estate, as is evident when _________

Which quotation from a translation of Uncle Vanya most effectively illustrates the claim?
selections: A. Vanya says to himself, “I was proud of [Professor Serebrakoff] and of his learning; I received all his words and writings as inspired and now? Now he has retired, and what is the total of his life? A blank!”
B. Professor Serebrakoff says to Helena, “Ever since I have been old I have been hateful to myself, and I am sure, hateful to you all as well.”
C. Professor Serebrakoff says, “I am a book-worm and a scholar, and am unfamiliar with practical affairs. I cannot, I find, dispense with the help of well-informed people.”

D. Professor Serebrakoff says to Helena, “I am used to my library and the lecture hall and to the esteem and admiration of my colleagues. Now I suddenly find myself plunged into this wilderness [the estate], condemned to see the same stupid people from morning till night and listen to their futile conversations.”
explanations:
题目文本翻译
《万尼亚叔叔:四幕乡村生活》是安东·契诃夫1898年创作的话剧，最初是用俄语写成的。在剧中，教授Serebrakoff和他的妻子Helena来到他们的乡村庄园，Vanya在教授前妻的女儿Sonia的帮助下管理庄园。契诃夫将教授描绘成无法适应乡村庄园的生活，这一点在_________
中文解析
塞雷布雷科夫教授对海伦娜说:“我习惯了我的图书馆和演讲厅，习惯了同事们的尊重和钦佩。现在我突然发现自己陷入了这片荒野[庄园]，注定要从早到晚看到同样的愚蠢的人，听他们徒劳的谈话。”这句话最有效地说明了契诃夫把塞雷布雷科夫教授描绘成无法适应乡间庄园生活的人。它显示了教授对庄园里的人和谈话的蔑视，突出了他无法适应环境的变化

question:
In 2016 Marta S. Pimentel and colleagues published a study concluding that ocean acidification has a strong effect on the behavior of Sparus aurata, a species of fish. However, Pimentel and colleagues’ study relied on a mean sample size of only 12 fish. In a 2022 review of various scientists’ conclusions about the impacts of ocean acidification on fish behavior, Timothy D. Clark and colleagues caution that relying on such a relatively small sample size can increase the potential for biased analysis. Such analysis, in turn, can contribute to reports of exaggerated effects.

What does the text most directly suggest about Pimentel and colleagues’ conclusion?
selections: A. It was based on the same mean sample size used in many earlier studies of fish species.
B. It likely has broad implications for other species of fish besides Sparus aurata.
C. It may overstate the effect of ocean acidification on the behavior of Sparus aurata.
D. It has been largely invalidated by results obtained from similar studies.
explanations:
题目文本翻译
2016年，Marta S. Pimentel及其同事发表了一项研究，得出的结论是，海洋酸化对Sparus aurata(一种鱼类)的行为有很强的影响。然而，Pimentel和同事的研究依赖于平均只有12条鱼的样本量。2022年，蒂莫西·d·克拉克(Timothy D. Clark)和他的同事在一篇综述中，回顾了各种科学家关于海洋酸化对鱼类行为影响的结论，他们警告说，依赖这样一个相对较小的样本量，可能会增加偏见分析的可能性。这样的分析反过来又可能导致夸大效应的报告。
中文解析
这篇文章表明，Pimentel及其同事关于海洋酸化对光斑Sparus aurata行为的强烈影响的结论可能被夸大了，因为他们研究中使用的样本量很小。Clark和他的同事们警告说，由于样本量小，分析可能存在偏见，这意味着从这些研究中得出的结论可能被夸大了。

question:
Shedding light on the thermal biology of fungi, research by Radamés Cordero et al. indicates that certain mushrooms (including Marasmius capillaris and species from the genus Russula) can achieve a hypothermic state through evaporative cooling. Effects of this thermoregulation were not limited to the fungi’s fruiting bodies and root-like hyphae: temperature reductions were observed in the air immediately surrounding the mushrooms. Though slight, the reductions inspired an air-cooling device; using approximately 400 grams of mushrooms, the team’s prototype lowered the air temperature in a controlled environment by 10℃ in forty minutes.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It presents a tangential finding about thermoregulation in certain fungal species that the experiment described later in the text was designed to explain.
B. It provides empirical evidence to bolster the claim made earlier in the text that certain fungal species maintain a hypothermic state.
C. It identifies an unexpected observation that motivated the study of evaporative cooling in fungi that is discussed earlier in the text.
D. It establishes a finding central to the text’s discussion of a practical application resulting from the team’s study of fungal thermal biology.
explanations:
题目文本翻译
在真菌的热生物学方面，radam·科德罗(Cordero)等人的研究表明，某些蘑菇(包括Marasmius capillaris和来自rusia属的物种)可以通过蒸发冷却达到低温状态。这种温度调节的影响并不局限于真菌的子实体和根状菌丝:在蘑菇周围的空气中观察到温度降低。虽然减少幅度很小，但却激发了一种空气冷却装置的灵感;使用大约400克蘑菇，该团队的原型在40分钟内将受控环境中的空气温度降低了10℃。
中文解析
Temperature reduction surrounding the mushrooms 是一项发现，随后的air-cooling device是来自团队的实际应用，与D选项匹配。

question:
Gottfried Schlaug et al. established that musical training is associated with physical alterations in the brain. Noting that such alterations may affect how sonic stimuli engender a hedonic response (a feeling of satisfaction and pleasure), Antonia Olivia Dolan et al. recently had musicians and nonmusicians listen to recordings—Led Zeppelin’s “Whole Lotta Love,” Jose Gonzalez’s “Heartbeats,” and others—and adjust the volume to the most pleasurable level for each recording. Although musicians and nonmusicians were clinically comparable in terms of their ability to detect sounds, musicians preferred to hear the recordings at a higher volume than nonmusicians did, leading Dolan et al. to conclude that _______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. previous research may have overstated the effects of the physical differences between musicians’ brains and nonmusicians’ brains.
B. physical aspects of musicians’ brains may suppress the hedonic response to music at volumes that provoke the hedonic response in nonmusicians.
C. characteristics of musicians’ brain anatomy that are not shared with nonmusicians result in musicians experiencing the hedonic response due to characteristics of music other than its volume.
D. musical training may alter musicians’ brains such that they have a reduced ability to detect sounds that are unlikely to incite the hedonic response.
explanations:
题目文本翻译
Gottfried Schlaug等人证实，音乐训练与大脑的生理变化有关。注意到这样的改变可能会影响声音刺激如何产生享乐反应(一种满足和愉悦的感觉)，Antonia Olivia Dolan等人最近让音乐家和非音乐家听录音——齐柏林飞艇的“Whole Lotta Love”，何塞·冈萨雷斯的“Heartbeats”，以及其他——并为每个录音调整音量到最令人愉快的水平。尽管音乐家和非音乐家在检测声音的能力方面具有临床可比性，但音乐家比非音乐家更喜欢以更高的音量听录音，这导致Dolan等人得出结论_______
中文解析
B选项指出，音乐家的大脑结构可能导致他们在普通人觉得愉快的音量下并不觉得愉快，需要更高的音量才能产生同样的愉悦感。这与前文提到的研究结果相吻合，即音乐训练与大脑的物理变化相关，这些变化可能影响他们对声音刺激的愉悦反应。

question:
Founded in Denver in 1991, the Museo de Las Americas is dedicated to art from Latin America, including the art of Indigenous peoples. Since its founding, it has acquired more than 4,800 objects for its permanent collection. More recently founded US-based institutions devoted to Latino cultures include the Latino Cultural Center. Located in Dallas, it focuses on Latino cultures and art in the United States.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
selections: A. It explains how one cultural institution was founded, then explains its plans to expand further.
B. It describes a trend among cultural institutions in the United States, then identifies an institution that rejects that trend.
C. It defines a certain type of cultural institution, then argues that this type of institution decisively influences society.
D. It discusses one cultural institution, then discusses a more recently founded cultural institution.
explanations:
题目文本翻译
拉斯维加斯美洲博物馆于1991年在丹佛成立，致力于拉丁美洲的艺术，包括土著人民的艺术。自成立以来，它已经获得了超过4800件物品作为永久收藏。最近在美国成立的致力于拉丁文化的机构包括拉丁文化中心。它位于达拉斯，专注于美国的拉丁文化和艺术。
中文解析
根据文本，它首先介绍了1991年成立的拉丁美洲博物馆，然后提到了最近在达拉斯成立的拉丁文化中心。

question:
Round Rock Chapter is one of the 110 chapters of the Navajo Nation (Naabeehó Bináhásdzo). The chapter, known as Tsé Nikání in the Navajo language (Diné bizaad), was the subject of a profile ________ in the Navajo Times on February 13, 2014.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

question:
Researchers Tammy Kernodle and Christina Zanfagna have lent their expertise on Black history and music to an important new _______ Timeline of African American Music, a digital resource that traces the development of individual musical genres (such as swing and bebop) while also revealing the connections between them.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 首先这不是句子间的链接，于是不可以用C/D，其次, 前后是解释关系，所以用冒号。

question:
Bill Belew’s talent for intricately and expertly detailed costume design was on full display with the Blue Rain jumpsuit, created for musical icon Elvis Presley to wear onstage. ________ the suit’s blue rhinestones showcased Belew’s careful attention to detail.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations: 文本第一句表达比尔·贝卢(Bill Belew)展示了他在复杂而细致的服装设计方面的才能，第二句套装的蓝色水钻展示了Belew对细节的细心关注。于是两个句子是递进强调细节选择in particular。

question:
Published in 1945, Gwendolyn Brooks’s poem “Queen of the Blues” demonstrates Brooks’s penchant for crafting short, compressed lines infused with bursts of vivid imagery and ________ the syncopated rhythms of the blues into her work.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: Incorporating与infused with充当后置定语修饰 lines，infused是过去分词表被动，incorporating是现在分词表示主动

question:
As comet C/1911 N1 (Kiess) orbits the Sun, it is trailed by a stream of rocky particles. When Earth passes through this meteoroid stream each year, typically between August 28 and September 5, the 66-kilometer-per-second collision between these meteoroids and atmospheric gases _______ streaks of light in the sky —the Aurigid meteor shower.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
