在19世纪初，切罗基学者Sequoyah为美国的一个土著语言创造了第一个文字系统。因为它准确地表示了切罗基语言的发音，他的书写系统易于学习，因此迅速实现了______（空白）使用：到1830年，超过90%的切罗基人能够阅读和书写这种文字。

question:
Kelp forests grow underwater along the eastern Pacific Coast. These underwater forests are important to fish and other marine animals. Ocean currents can be powerful and rough, making it difficult for animals to find safe places to hide from predators. The underwater forests slow down the currents. This creates a more ______ environment with calmer waters where animals can take shelter.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
中文解析
选择A是最佳答案，因为它最合理地完成了文本对海带森林如何帮助海洋动物的讨论。在这个语境中，“宁静”意味着没有干扰或平静。文本指出海洋洋流强劲，使海洋动物难以躲避捕食者，而海带森林减缓了洋流，创造了更平静的区域。换句话说，海带森林创造了一个更加宁静的环境。
题目文本解析
海带森林生长在太平洋东海岸的水下。这些水下森林对鱼类和其他海洋动物至关重要。海洋洋流可能强劲而剧烈，使动物很难找到安全的地方躲避捕食者。水下森林减缓了洋流。这创造了一个更加______（空白）环境，水域更加平静，动物可以在这里避难。

question:
Along with carbon dioxide concentration and temperature, light intensity affects the chemical reaction rate of ______ as light intensity increases, so does the rate at which the reactants (water and carbon dioxide) are converted into their products (glucose and oxygen).

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选择C是最佳答案。测试的规范是句子中的标点使用。在这个选项中，冒号正确地用于标记一个主句（“Along with...photosynthesis”）和另一个主句（“as light...oxygen”）之间的界限，并引入后面关于光强度如何影响光合作用的内容。

question:
Paintings by the renowned twentieth-century US ______ were featured in Artist to Artist, an exhibition at the Smithsonian Art Museum that paired the works of artists whose career trajectories intersected in meaningful ways.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
selections: A. artists: Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock,
B. artists Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock
C. artists Thomas Hart Benton, and Jackson Pollock,
D. artists, Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock
explanations: 选择B是最佳答案。测试的规范是名词短语周围的标点使用。因为协调名词短语“Thomas Hart Benton and Jackson Pollock”是一个限制性同位语，所以不需要标点，这意味着它提供了关于前面名词短语“the renowned twentieth-century US artists”的必要识别信息。

question:
In Death Valley National Park’s Racetrack Playa, a flat, dry lakebed, are 162 rocks—some weighing less than a pound but others almost 700 pounds—that move periodically from place to place, seemingly of their own volition. Racetrack-like trails in the ______ mysterious migration.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
selections: A. playas sediment mark the rock’s
B. playa’s sediment mark the rocks
C. playa’s sediment mark the rocks’
D. playas’ sediment mark the rocks’
explanations: 选择C是最佳答案。测试的规范是复数名词和所有格名词的使用。单数所有格名词“playa’s”和复数所有格名词“rocks’”正确地表明沉积物属于一个playa（Racetrack Playa），并且有多块岩石神秘地在沉积物上迁移。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·Dr. Sunil Bajpai studies dinosaurs at the Indian Institute of Technology.
·Bajpai’s research team recently found a 167-million-year-old dicraeosaurid fossil.
·It is the oldest fossil from the dicraeosaurid dinosaur group ever recovered.
·It was found in the Thar Desert in western India.

The student wants to indicate where the dicraeosaurid fossil was found. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. The dicraeosaurid fossil was found in western India’s Thar Desert.
B. Bajpai’s team recently found the oldest dicraeosaurid fossil ever recovered.
C. Dr. Sunil Bajpai, of the Indian Institute of Technology, is part of a research team.
D. The fossil, which is from the dicraeosaurid dinosaur group, is 167 million years old.
explanations:
中文解析
选择A是最佳答案。该句指出了dicraeosaurid化石的发现地点：印度西部的塔尔沙漠。
题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 苏尼尔·巴杰潘博士在印度理工学院研究恐龙。
- 巴杰潘的研究团队最近发现了一具1亿6700万年前的dicraeosaurid化石。
- 这是迄今为止从dicraeosaurid恐龙群中恢复的最古老化石。
- 它是在印度西部的塔尔沙漠中发现的。

question:
One poll taken after the first 1960 presidential debate suggested that John Kennedy lost badly: only 21 percent of those who listened on the radio rated him the winner. ______ the debate was ultimately considered a victory for the telegenic young senator, who rated higher than his opponent, Vice President Richard Nixon, among those watching on the new medium of television.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
中文解析
选择D是最佳答案。“Nevertheless”在逻辑上表明，尽管之前关于收音机听众投票的信息，这句话中的主张——即具有电视魅力的肯尼迪最终被认为是辩论的赢家——依然成立。
题目文本解析
在1960年第一次总统辩论后进行的一项民调显示，约翰·肯尼迪（John Kennedy）输得很惨：只有21%的收听广播的人认为他是赢家。______ 然而，在观看新媒体电视的观众中，这场辩论最终被认为是那位充满魅力的年轻参议员的胜利，他的表现比对手、副总统理查德·尼克松（Richard Nixon）更受欢迎。

question:
While many video game creators strive to make their graphics ever more ______ others look to the past, developing titles with visuals inspired by the “8-bit” games of the 1980s and 1990s. (The term “8-bit” refers to a console whose processor could only handle eight bits of data at once.)

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选择C是最佳答案。测试的规范是从属子句和主句之间的标点。这个选项正确地使用了逗号来标记从属子句（“虽然……栩栩如生”）和主句（“其他人则向过去看”）之间的界限。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·Ancient Native American and Australian Aboriginal cultures described the Pleiades star cluster as having seven stars.
·It was referred to as the Seven Sisters in the mythology of ancient Greece.
·Today, the cluster appears to have only six stars.
·Two of the stars have moved so close together that they now appear as one.

The student wants to specify the reason the Pleiades’ appearance changed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Ancient Native American and Australian Aboriginal cultures described the Pleiades, which was referred to in Greek mythology as the Seven Sisters, as having seven stars.
B. Although once referred to as the Seven Sisters, the Pleiades appears to have only six stars today.
C. In the time since ancient cultures described the Pleiades as having seven stars, two of the cluster’s stars have moved so close together that they now appear as one.
D. The Pleiades has seven stars, but two are so close together that they appear to be a single star.
explanations:
中文解析
选择C是最佳答案。该句说明了七姐妹星团外观变化的原因，指出该星团中的两颗恒星已经靠得如此之近，以至于现在看起来像是一颗星星。
题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 古代美洲土著和澳大利亚土著文化将七姐妹星团描述为有七颗星星。
- 在古希腊神话中，它被称为七姐妹。
- 如今，这个星团似乎只有六颗星星。
- 其中两颗星已经靠得如此之近，以至于现在看起来像是一颗星。

question:
As British scientist Peter Whibberley has observed, “the Earth is not a very good timekeeper.” Earth’s slightly irregular rotation rate means that measurements of time must be periodically adjusted. Specifically, an extra “leap second” (the 86,401st second of the day) is ______ time based on the planet’s rotation lags a full nine-tenths of a second behind time kept by precise atomic clocks.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选择D是最佳答案。测试的规范是动词和介词之间的标点。当动词（“is added”）紧接着后面跟着介词（“whenever”）时，不需要标点。

question:
In her 2012 analysis of tree rings from Japan’s Yaku Island, cosmic ray physicist Fusa Miyake noted an anomalous carbon-14 spike dating to 774–775 CE, indicating that a massive burst of radiation reached Earth during that time. ______ this unprecedented radiocarbon surge was dubbed a “Miyake event” in honor of its discoverer.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
中文解析
选择A是最佳答案。“Fittingly”在逻辑上表明，将前所未有的放射性碳激增命名为Fusa Miyake是适合该情境的，因为Miyake是通过她对屋久岛树轮的分析识别出这一激增的人。
题目文本解析：
在她2012年对日本屋久岛树轮的分析中，宇宙射线物理学家宫崎富佐（Fusa Miyake）注意到一个异常的碳-14峰值，日期为公元774年至775年，这表明在那段时期内，一次巨大的辐射爆发到达了地球。______ 这个前所未有的放射性碳激增被称为“宫崎事件”，以此来纪念它的发现者。

question:
In his 1925 book The Morphology of Landscape, US geographer Carl Sauer challenged prevailing views about how natural landscapes influence human cultures. ______ Sauer argued that instead of being shaped entirely by their natural surroundings, cultures play an active role in their own development by virtue of their interactions with the environment.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
中文解析
选择D是最佳答案。“Specifically”在逻辑上表明，这句话中关于Sauer论点的信息——根据Sauer的说法，文化在自身发展中发挥作用，而不仅仅是受到自然环境的影响——提供了对前一句中关于Sauer如何挑战关于自然景观影响人类文化的主流观点的更一般信息的具体、精确的细节。
题目文本解析
在他1925年的著作《景观的形态学》中，美国地理学家卡尔·绍尔（Carl Sauer）挑战了当时关于自然景观如何影响人类文化的普遍观点。______ 绍尔认为，文化并不是完全被自然环境所塑造的，而是通过与环境的互动，在自身发展中发挥着积极作用。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·In the late 1890s, over 14,000 unique varieties of apples were grown in the US.
·The rise of industrial agriculture in the mid-1900s narrowed the range of commercially grown crops.
·Thousands of apple varieties considered less suitable for commercial growth were lost.
·Today, only 15 apple varieties dominate the market, making up 90% of apples purchased in the US.
·The Lost Apple Project, based in Washington State, attempts to find and grow lost apple varieties.

The student wants to emphasize the decline in unique apple varieties in the US and specify why this decline occurred. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish these goals?
selections: A. The Lost Apple Project is dedicated to finding some of the apple varieties lost following a shift in agricultural practices in the mid-1900s.
B. While over 14,000 apple varieties were grown in the US in the late 1890s, only 15 unique varieties make up most of the apples sold today.
C. Since the rise of industrial agriculture, US farmers have mainly grown the same few unique apple varieties, resulting in the loss of thousands of varieties less suitable for commercial growth.
D. As industrial agriculture rose to prominence in the mid-1900s, the number of crops selected for cultivation decreased dramatically.
explanations:
中文解析
选择C是最佳答案。该句强调了美国独特苹果品种的减少，并具体说明了这一减少的原因，指出由于美国农民开始主要种植少数几种独特品种，导致数千种苹果品种的消失。
题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 在1890年代末，美国种植了超过14,000种独特的苹果品种。
- 20世纪中叶，工业农业的兴起缩小了商业种植作物的范围。
- 数千种被认为不太适合商业种植的苹果品种消失了。
- 如今，市场上只有15种苹果品种占主导地位，占美国购买的苹果的90%。
- 总部位于华盛顿州的失落苹果项目试图寻找和种植失去的苹果品种。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·Severo Ochoa discovered the enzyme PNPase in 1955.
·PNPase is involved in both the creation and degradation of mRNA.
·Ochoa incorrectly hypothesized that PNPase provides the genetic blueprints for mRNA.
·The discovery of PNPase proved critical to deciphering the human genetic code.
·Deciphering the genetic code has led to a better understanding of how genetic variations affect human health.

The student wants to emphasize the significance of Ochoa’s discovery. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Ochoa’s 1955 discovery of PNPase proved critical to deciphering the human genetic code, leading to a better understanding of how genetic variations affect human health.
B. Ochoa first discovered PNPase, an enzyme that he hypothesized contained the genetic blueprints for mRNA, in 1955.
C. In 1955, Ochoa discovered the PNPase enzyme, which is involved in both the creation and degradation of mRNA.
D. Though his discovery of PNPase was critical to deciphering the human genetic code, Ochoa incorrectly hypothesized that the enzyme was the source of mRNA’s genetic blueprints.
explanations:
中文解析
选择A是最佳答案。该句强调了Ochoa发现的重要性，指出它对破译人类基因组至关重要，从而更好地理解遗传变异如何影响人类健康。
题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 塞韦罗·奥乔亚在1955年发现了酶PNPase。
- PNPase参与mRNA的合成和降解。
- 奥乔亚错误地假设PNPase为mRNA提供遗传蓝图。
- PNPase的发现对破译人类基因组至关重要。
- 破译基因组已经促进了对遗传变异如何影响人类健康的更好理解。

question:
“To You” is an 1856 poem by Walt Whitman. In the poem, Whitman suggests that he deeply understands the reader, whom he addresses directly, writing, ______

Which quotation from “To You” most effectively illustrates the claim?
selections: A. “Your true soul and body appear before me.”
B. “Whoever you are, now I place my hand upon you, that you be my poem.”
C. “I should have made my way straight to you long ago.”
D. “Whoever you are, I fear you are walking the walks of dreams.”
explanations:
中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它最直接地说明了文本对惠特曼的诗《致你》的论断。文本指出，在这首诗中，惠特曼暗示他对诗的读者有深刻的理解。这句话说，读者的“真实灵魂和身体在惠特曼面前显现”，从而断言他能够看到读者的真实样貌，这暗示着他对读者有着深刻的理解。
题目文本解析
《致你》是沃尔特·惠特曼于1856年创作的一首诗。在这首诗中，惠特曼直接对读者发言，暗示他对读者有深刻的理解，写道，______

question:
When hibernating, Alaska marmots and Arctic ground squirrels enter a state called torpor, which minimizes the energy their bodies need to function. Often a hibernating animal will temporarily come out of torpor (called an arousal episode) and its metabolic rate will rise, burning more of the precious energy the animal needs to survive the winter. Alaska marmots hibernate in groups and therefore burn less energy keeping warm during these episodes than they would if they were alone. A researcher hypothesized that because Arctic ground squirrels hibernate alone, they would likely exhibit longer bouts of torpor and shorter arousal episodes than Alaska marmots.

Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researcher’s hypothesis?
selections: A. The Alaska marmots’ arousal episodes lasted for days, while the Arctic ground squirrels’ arousal episodes lasted less than a day.
B. The Alaska marmots and the Arctic ground squirrels both maintained torpor for several consecutive days per bout, on average.
C. The Alaska marmots had shorter torpor bouts and longer arousal episodes than the Arctic ground squirrels did.
D. The Alaska marmots had more torpor bouts than arousal episodes, but their arousal episodes were much shorter than their torpor bouts.
explanations:
中文解析
选项C是最佳答案，因为它描述了支持研究者假设的数据。根据文本，研究者假设北极地松鼠的冬眠时间会比阿拉斯加土拨鼠的冬眠时间更长，而清醒时间则更短，换句话说，阿拉斯加土拨鼠的冬眠时间会更短，清醒时间会更长。该表显示了2008年至2011年这两种动物的冬眠时间和清醒时间的数据。根据表格，阿拉斯加土拨鼠的冬眠时间平均为13.81天，短于北极地松鼠的平均16.77天；而阿拉斯加土拨鼠的清醒时间平均为21.2小时，长于北极地松鼠的平均14.2小时。因此，该表通过显示阿拉斯加土拨鼠的冬眠时间比北极地松鼠短、清醒时间更长来支持研究者的假设。
题目文本解析
在冬眠时，阿拉斯加土拨鼠和北极地鼠进入一种称为冬眠状态的状态，这种状态可以最小化它们身体所需的能量。冬眠中的动物通常会暂时从冬眠状态中苏醒（称为觉醒期），其代谢率会升高，消耗更多宝贵的能量，以维持冬季生存。阿拉斯加土拨鼠以群体形式冬眠，因此在这些觉醒期内，它们消耗的能量相比于单独冬眠时要少。研究者假设，由于北极地鼠是单独冬眠，它们可能会表现出更长的冬眠时间和更短的觉醒期，相较于阿拉斯加土拨鼠。

question:
The work of Kiowa painter T.C. Cannon derives its power in part from the tension among his ______ influences: classic European portraiture, with its realistic treatment of faces; the American pop art movement, with its vivid colors; and flatstyle, the intertribal painting style that rejects the effect of depth typically achieved through shading and perspective.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
中文解析
选项C是最佳答案，因为它最合理地完成了文本关于影响Cannon作品的艺术风格的讨论。在这个上下文中，“不同的”意味着独特或不相似。文本指出，影响Cannon作品的风格之间存在一种紧张关系，并进一步描述了这些风格的不同：经典的欧洲肖像画偏爱现实主义，美国流行艺术使用鲜艳的色彩，而部落间的平面风格则拒绝使用阴影和透视来实现深度。这个背景表明，影响Cannon作品的风格是不同的。
题目文本解析
Kiowa画家T.C. Cannon的作品部分源于他______的影响之间的张力：经典的欧洲肖像画，以其对面部的真实表现；美国流行艺术运动，以其鲜艳的色彩；以及平面风格，这是一种拒绝通过阴影和透视来实现深度效果的部落间绘画风格。

question:
In the mountains of Brazil, Barbacenia tomentosa and Barbacenia macrantha—two plants in the Velloziaceae family—establish themselves on soilless, nutrient-poor patches of quartzite rock. Plant ecologists Anna Abrahão and Patricia de Britto Costa used microscopic analysis to determine that the roots of B. tomentosa and B. macrantha, which grow directly into the quartzite, have clusters of fine hairs near the root tip; further analysis indicated that these hairs secrete both malic and citric acids. The researchers hypothesize that the plants depend on dissolving underlying rock with these acids, as the process not only creates channels for continued growth but also releases phosphates that provide the vital nutrient phosphorus.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers’ hypothesis?
selections: A. Other species in the Velloziaceae family are found in terrains with more soil but have root structures similar to those of B. tomentosa and B. macrantha.
B. Though B. tomentosa and B. macrantha both secrete citric and malic acids, each species produces the acids in different proportions.
C. The roots of B. tomentosa and B. macrantha carve new entry points into rocks even when cracks in the surface are readily available.
D. B. tomentosa and B. macrantha thrive even when transferred to the surfaces of rocks that do not contain phosphates.
explanations:
中文解析
选项C是最佳答案，因为它提出了一个发现，如果为真，将支持研究者关于植物依赖溶解岩石的假设。文本指出，这两种植物的根直接生长在石英岩中，根上的毛状结构分泌酸以溶解岩石。研究者假设植物依赖这一过程，因为溶解岩石会为根的生长打开空间，并释放磷酸盐，为植物提供重要的营养素磷。如果植物在岩石中已经有根可以生长的空间的情况下仍然进行溶解岩石的过程，这将支持研究者的假设，因为这表明植物从溶解岩石的行为中获得了一些好处，例如获得磷。如果植物从溶解岩石中没有获益，它们应当会选择在已经存在的裂缝中生长，因为这样做意味着植物不必花费能量去创造和分泌酸；然而，如果植物在已经存在裂缝的情况下通过溶解岩石创造新的入口点，这将支持它们依赖溶解岩石获取某种好处的假设。
题目文本解析
在巴西的山脉中，**Barbacenia tomentosa** 和 **Barbacenia macrantha**——这两种属于 Velloziaceae 科的植物——在无土、养分贫乏的石英岩裸露地带生长。植物生态学家安娜·阿布拉哈（Anna Abrahão）和帕特里夏·德·布里托·科斯塔（Patricia de Britto Costa）通过显微镜分析确定，**B. tomentosa** 和 **B. macrantha** 的根部直接生长在石英岩中，根尖附近有细小的毛状结构簇；进一步分析表明，这些毛状结构分泌苹果酸和柠檬酸。研究者假设植物依赖这些酸来溶解底层岩石，因为这一过程不仅为植物的持续生长创造了通道，还释放出磷酸盐，提供重要的营养素磷。

question:
Critics have asserted that fine art and fashion rarely ______ in a world where artists create timeless works for exhibition and designers periodically produce new styles for the public to buy. Luiseño/Shoshone-Bannock beadwork artist and designer Jamie Okuma challenges this view: her work can be seen in the Metropolitan Museum of Art and purchased through her online boutique.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
中文解析
选项D是最佳答案，因为它最合理地完成了文本关于美术与时尚关系的讨论。在这个上下文中，“交叉”意味着连接或重叠。文本指出，Jamie Okuma挑战了批评家所持的观点，因为她的作品可以在艺术博物馆中展示，也可以通过她的在线精品店供公众购买。文本还展示了批评家的观点，认为美术艺术家创作的作品是“永恒的”，并且旨在展出，而时尚设计师则定期推出新款式，供人购买。这个背景表明，批评家认为美术与时尚往往不重叠——换句话说，它们很少交集。
题目文本解析
批评家们主张，在一个艺术家创作永恒作品以供展览，设计师定期推出供公众购买的新款式的世界中，美术和时尚很少______。Luiseño/Shoshone-Bannock珠饰艺术家及设计师Jamie Okuma挑战了这一观点：她的作品可以在大都会艺术博物馆中看到，并可以通过她的在线精品店购买。

question:
A team of biologists led by Jae-Hoon Jung, Antonio D. Barbosa, and Stephanie Hutin investigated the mechanism that allows Arabidopsis thaliana (thale cress) plants to accelerate flowering at high temperatures. They replaced the protein ELF3 in the plants with a similar protein found in another species (stiff brome) that, unlike A. thaliana, displays no acceleration in flowering with increased temperature. A comparison of unmodified A. thaliana plants with the altered plants showed no difference in flowering at 22° Celsius, but at 27° Celsius, the unmodified plants exhibited accelerated flowering while the altered ones did not, which suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. temperature-sensitive accelerated flowering is unique to A. thaliana.
B. A. thaliana increases ELF3 production as temperatures rise.
C. ELF3 enables A. thaliana to respond to increased temperatures.
D. temperatures of at least 22° Celsius are required for A. thaliana to flower.
explanations:
中文解析
选项C是最佳答案，因为它最合乎逻辑地补充了文本关于**A. thaliana**植物加速开花的讨论。文本指出，**A. thaliana**植物在高温下表现出加速开花。为了研究这一加速开花的机制，生物学家将一组**A. thaliana**植物中的ELF3蛋白替换为另一种植物物种中发现的类似蛋白，而该物种并没有表现出加速开花。研究小组随后将这些经过修改的植物与保留原始ELF3蛋白的**A. thaliana**植物进行了比较。文本指出，这两组植物在22°C时的开花没有差异，但在27°C时，保留ELF3的未改变植物表现出加速开花，而没有ELF3的植物则没有。如果在较高温度下，含ELF3的**A. thaliana**植物发生了加速开花，而没有该蛋白的植物则没有，那么ELF3很可能使**A. thaliana**能够对温度升高做出反应。
题目文本解析
由Jae-Hoon Jung、Antonio D. Barbosa和Stephanie Hutin领导的一组生物学家研究了使**Arabidopsis thaliana**（紫花前胡）植物在高温下加速开花的机制。他们将植物中的ELF3蛋白替换为另一种物种（硬禾草）中发现的类似蛋白，而该物种与**A. thaliana**不同，在温度升高时不会表现出加速开花。对未修改的**A. thaliana**植物与经过改变的植物进行比较时，在22°C时开花没有差异，但在27°C时，未修改的植物表现出加速开花，而经过改变的植物则没有，这表明______。

question:
The domestic sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) descends from a wild plant native to South America. It also populates the Polynesian Islands, where evidence confirms that Native Hawaiians and other Indigenous peoples were cultivating the plant centuries before seafaring first occurred over the thousands of miles of ocean separating them from South America. To explain how the sweet potato was first introduced in Polynesia, botanist Pablo Muñoz-Rodríguez and colleagues analyzed the DNA of numerous varieties of the plant, concluding that Polynesian varieties diverged from South American ones over 100,000 years ago. Given that Polynesia was peopled only in the last three thousand years, the team concluded that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. the cultivation of the sweet potato in Polynesia likely predates its cultivation in South America.
B. Polynesian peoples likely acquired the sweet potato from South American peoples only within the last three thousand years.
C. human activity likely played no role in the introduction of the sweet potato in Polynesia.
D. Polynesian sweet potato varieties likely descend from a single South American variety that was domesticated, not wild.
explanations:
中文解析
选项C是最佳答案，因为它最合乎逻辑地补充了文本关于波利尼西亚甘薯的讨论。文本指出，甘薯在波利尼西亚被发现，但起源于南美洲，并且在南美洲与波利尼西亚之间的海上航行开始之前，夏威夷土著和其他波利尼西亚原住民早就开始种植甘薯。文本进一步提到，Muñoz-Rodríguez及其同事的研究表明，波利尼西亚的甘薯品种在10万多年前就与南美洲的品种分化，这比人类定居波利尼西亚的时间早了几千年。如果波利尼西亚人民在南美洲与波利尼西亚之间的海上航行开始之前就已经种植甘薯，并且波利尼西亚的甘薯品种在距离人类到达波利尼西亚的时间上有很长的分化过程，那么可以合理得出结论，人类并没有在将甘薯引入波利尼西亚方面发挥作用。
题目文本解析
家用甘薯（Ipomoea batatas）起源于一种原产于南美洲的野生植物。它也分布于波利尼西亚群岛，证据表明，夏威夷土著和其他原住民在海洋航行首次发生之前的几个世纪就已经开始种植这种植物，这些航行将他们与南美洲隔开了数千英里的海洋。为了解释甘薯是如何首次引入波利尼西亚的，植物学家Pablo Muñoz-Rodríguez及其同事分析了多种甘薯品种的DNA，得出结论，波利尼西亚的品种在10万多年前就与南美洲的品种分化。考虑到波利尼西亚仅在过去三千年内有人定居，研究小组得出结论______。

question:
The following text is adapted from Aphra Behn’s 1689 novel The Lucky Mistake. Atlante and Rinaldo are neighbors who have been secretly exchanging letters through Charlot, Atlante’s sister.
[Atlante] gave this letter to Charlot; who immediately ran into the balcony with it, where she still found Rinaldo in a melancholy posture, leaning his head on his hand: She showed him the letter, but was afraid to toss it to him, for fear it might fall to the ground; so he ran and fetched a long cane, which he cleft at one end, and held it while she put the letter into the cleft, and stayed not to hear what he said to it. But never was man so transported with joy, as he was at the reading of this letter; it gives him new wounds; for to the generous, nothing obliges love so much as love.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
selections: A. It describes the delivery of a letter, and then portrays a character’s happiness at reading that letter.
B. It establishes that a character is desperate to receive a letter, and then explains why another character has not yet written that letter.
C. It presents a character’s concerns about delivering a letter, and then details the contents of that letter.
D. It reveals the inspiration behind a character’s letter, and then emphasizes the excitement that another character feels upon receiving that letter.
explanations:
中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它最准确地描述了文本的整体结构。叙述者首先解释了Charlot是如何小心翼翼地将Atlante的信件递给Rinaldo的，然后提到Rinaldo在阅读信件后感到“欣喜若狂”。因此，文本的整体结构最恰当地被描述为对信件递送的描述，随后是对角色在阅读信件后的快乐的描绘。
题目文本解析
以下文本摘自阿夫拉·贝恩（Aphra Behn）于1689年出版的小说《幸运的错误》（The Lucky Mistake）。阿特兰特（Atlante）和里纳尔多（Rinaldo）是邻居，他们通过阿特兰特的妹妹夏洛特（Charlot）秘密地交换信件。
[阿特兰特]将这封信交给了夏洛特；她立即跑到阳台上，那里她仍然发现里纳尔多正以忧郁的姿势靠着手臂：她给他看了信，但因为担心信会掉到地上，所以不敢把信扔给他；于是他跑去拿了一根长竹竿，在一端劈开，拿着竹竿的同时，她将信放入劈开的缝隙中，并没有停下来听他对信说了些什么。但从来没有人像他在阅读这封信时那样欣喜若狂；这封信给了他新的伤痛；因为对于慷慨的人来说，没有什么比爱更能激发爱的义务。

question:
Eighteenth-century economist Adam Smith is famed for his metaphor of the invisible hand, which he putatively used to illustrate a robust model of how individuals produce aggregate benefits by pursuing their own economic interests. Note “putatively”: as Gavin Kennedy has shown, Smith deploys this metaphor only once in his economic writings—to make a narrow point about the then-dominant economic theory of mercantilism—and it was largely ignored until some twentieth-century economists eager to secure an intellectual pedigree for their views elevated it to a fully-fledged paradigm.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
selections: A. Although Smith is famed for his metaphor of the invisible hand, the metaphor was largely ignored until economists in the twentieth century came to realize that the metaphor was a robust model that anticipated their own views.

B. Some twentieth-century economists gave Smith’s metaphor of the invisible hand a significance it does not have in Smith’s work, but it is nevertheless a useful model of how individuals produce aggregate benefits by pursuing their own economic interests.

C. Smith’s metaphor of the invisible hand has been interpreted as a model of how individuals acting in their own interest produce aggregate benefits, but it was intended as a subtle critique of the economic theory of mercantilism.

D. The reputation of Smith’s metaphor of the invisible hand is not due to the importance of the metaphor in Smith’s work but rather to the promotion of the metaphor by some later economists for their own ends.
explanations:
中文解析
选项D是最佳答案，因为它最准确地陈述了文本的主要观点。文本解释了经济学家亚当·斯密（Adam Smith）著名的“看不见的手”隐喻被认为是用来说明一个强有力的模型（即一种始终准确的概括），即个人追求自身经济利益如何能够为更大群体创造更广泛的利益。接着，文本通过指出“被认为”（putatively）这一术语，强调了这一观点缺乏确凿证据，并解释说，根据加文·肯尼迪（Gavin Kennedy）的说法，斯密在他的著作中仅使用过一次这一隐喻，且是指特定的与当时已过时的经济观点（即重商主义）相关的情况，并且这一隐喻直到二十世纪的经济学家们将其视为典范（即该领域的理论框架）时才引起了关注，从而暗示斯密与他们的经济观点有某种共鸣。通过强调“被认为”，文本暗示没有独立的理由相信斯密会同意在他写作的特定背景之外使用这一隐喻，因此，使用这一隐喻的二十世纪经济学家们是在支持自己的观点，而没有考虑到这一隐喻在斯密作品中的重要性。
题目文本解析
十八世纪的经济学家亚当·斯密因其“看不见的手”隐喻而闻名，他被认为是用这一隐喻来说明个人如何通过追求自身经济利益来产生整体利益的强有力模型。注意“被认为”（putatively）：正如加文·肯尼迪所示，斯密在他的经济著作中只使用过一次这一隐喻——是为了对当时主导的重商主义经济理论提出一个狭义的观点——而且这一隐喻在很大程度上被忽视，直到一些二十世纪的经济学家渴望为他们的观点确立知识渊源，将其提升为一个完整的范式。

question:
Barring major archaeological discoveries, we are unlikely to ever have ______ account of ancient Egypt under the female pharaoh Hatshepsut, as much of the evidence of her reign was deliberately destroyed by her successors.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
中文解析
选项C是最佳答案，因为它最合理地完成了文本关于古埃及在女法老哈特谢普苏特统治下的历史证据的讨论。在这个上下文中，“详尽的”叙述将是一个全面的叙述。文本指出，她统治期间的大部分证据被故意毁坏——换句话说，幸存记录的缺乏。这个背景传达了除非有重大的新考古发现，否则对哈特谢普苏特统治的详尽叙述是不太可能的。
题目文本解析
除非有重大的考古发现，否则我们不太可能拥有关于女法老哈特谢普苏特统治下古埃及的______。因为她统治期间的大部分证据被她的继任者故意毁坏了。

question:
The following text is from Edith Wharton’s 1905 novel The House of Mirth. Lily Bart and a companion are walking through a park.
Lily had no real intimacy with nature, but she had a passion for the appropriate and could be keenly sensitive to a scene which was the fitting background of her own sensations. The landscape outspread below her seemed an enlargement of her present mood, and she found something of herself in its calmness, its breadth, its long free reaches. On the nearer slopes the sugar-maples wavered like pyres of light; lower down was a massing of grey orchards, and here and there the lingering green of an oak-grove.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It creates a detailed image of the physical setting of the scene.
B. It establishes that a character is experiencing an internal conflict
C. It makes an assertion that the next sentence then expands on.
D. It illustrates an idea that is introduced in the previous sentence.
explanations:
中文解析
选项D是最佳答案，因为它最恰当地描述了下划线句子在整个文本中的功能。文本的第一句表明莉莉（Lily）能够“敏锐地感知”那些作为她情感“合适背景”的场景——也就是说，她非常清楚何时环境似乎反映了她的情绪。接下来的句子，即下划线部分，则展示了这种意识：莉莉将自己所处的景观视为她当前情绪的大规模反映，认同其中的宁静等元素。因此，下划线句子的功能是说明前一句中引入的一个观点。
题目文本解析
以下文本摘自爱迪丝·沃顿（Edith Wharton）于1905年出版的小说《欢愉之家》（The House of Mirth）。莉莉·巴特（Lily Bart）和一位伴侣正在公园里散步。
莉莉与自然并没有真正的亲密关系，但她对合适的事物充满热情，能够敏锐地感知那些与她自身感受相称的场景。她眼前展开的景观似乎是她当前情绪的放大，她在那宁静、广阔和悠长的自由之中找到了自己的某种存在。在较近的坡地上，糖枫树像光的火葬堆一样摇曳；而在更低处则是一片灰色的果园，时不时可以看到一片苍翠的橡树林。

question:
Rows in table may not add up to 100 due to rounding.
Over the past two hundred years, the percentage of the population employed in the agricultural sector has declined in both France and the United States, while employment in the service sector (which includes jobs in retail, consulting, real estate, etc.) has risen. However, this transition happened at very different rates in the two countries. This can be seen most clearly by comparing the employment by sector in both countries in ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
selections: A. 1900 with the employment by sector in 1950.
B. 1800 with the employment by sector in 2012.
C. 1900 with the employment by sector in 2012.
D. 1800 with the employment by sector in 1900.
explanations:
中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它提供了来自表格的数据，最有效地补充了关于法国和美国就业转变速度的陈述。文本指出，在过去两百年中，法国和美国的农业部门就业人数减少，而服务部门就业人数增加，表格中的数据反映了这些趋势。然而，文本声称，农业向服务业的转变“在两个国家发生的速度非常不同”。这一说法最有力地得到1900年和1950年数据比较的支持：表格显示，在这些年份，法国农业就业从43%降至32%（下降11个百分点），而美国则从41%降至14%（下降27个百分点）；同时，法国服务业就业从28%升至35%（增加7个百分点），而美国则从31%升至53%（增加22个百分点）。换句话说，在这两个部门中，美国的变化速度均大于法国。
题目文本解析
表格中的各行可能由于四舍五入而无法加总至100。
在过去的两百年中，法国和美国农业部门就业人数所占的百分比均有所下降，而服务部门（包括零售、咨询、房地产等职业）的就业人数则有所上升。然而，这一转变在两个国家的速度非常不同。这一点通过比较两个国家在______年的按部门就业情况可以最清晰地看出。

question:
In 1966, Emmett Ashford became the first African American to umpire a Major League Baseball game. His energetic gestures announcing when a player had struck out and his habit of barreling after a hit ball to see if it would land out of ______ transform the traditionally solemn umpire role into a dynamic one.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项A是最佳答案。所测试的语法规则是主句中有限动词的使用。主句需要一个有限动词来执行主语的动作（在本例中是Ashford的“手势”和“习惯”），而这个选项提供了有限的过去式动词“helped”，以指示Ashford的手势和习惯帮助达成了什么。

question:
Several studies have found negligible electoral consequences for governments that impose fiscal austerity measures, yet some European governments recently suffered electorally due to their austerity programs. Evelyne Huebscher and colleagues attribute this incongruity to governments’ tendency—not followed in the recent European cases—to implement austerity programs strategically to avoid electoral costs (e.g., setting spending cuts to take effect only after the next election), which has obscured the inherent political risks of austerity measures in the election data scholars have examined.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It explains a discrepancy between what has been observed in study settings and what has been observed in real-world settings that the text goes on to assert is attributable to the studies not using real-world data.
B. It identifies a conflict between research findings and recent events that the text goes on to suggest is a consequence of a complicating factor in the data used to generate those findings.
C. It presents a long-standing divergence in research findings that the text goes on to say is due to different groups of researchers using data that derive from different electoral circumstances.

D. It describes a recent exception to a general pattern in research findings that the text goes on to explain is a result of researchers underestimating the significance of inconsistencies in the data they’ve analyzed.
explanations:
中文解析
选项B是最佳答案，因为它最恰当地描述了下划线句子在整个文本中的功能。下划线句子解释了与几项研究所暗示的相反，最近的欧洲政府在启动财政紧缩政策后遭遇了选举上的失败。文本接着指出，研究人员的发现是基于一些数据，这些数据并没有揭示紧缩措施所带来的真正政治风险，因为这些数据基于的是政府在下一次选举后才会实施紧缩政策的案例，而最近遭遇选举失败的欧洲政府并没有遵循这一做法，从而引入了一个复杂因素，导致研究结果与近期事件之间出现了冲突。
题目文本解析
几项研究发现，实施财政紧缩措施的政府在选举中几乎没有显著的后果，然而一些欧洲政府最近因其紧缩政策遭遇了选举失败。埃芙琳·赫布舍（Evelyne Huebscher）及其同事将这一不一致归因于政府的倾向——在最近的欧洲案例中并未遵循——即战略性地实施紧缩政策以避免选举成本（例如，仅在下一次选举后生效的支出削减），这模糊了学者们所研究的选举数据中紧缩措施固有的政治风险。

question:
Proposals to raise the age at which retirees begin receiving government transfers of funds are generally discussed in terms of the effects on transfer recipients, but Andria Smythe has argued that delaying such transfers could ______ wealth creation among working adults by lengthening the period in which they are providing financial support to their nonworking parents.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它最合理地完成了文本关于提高退休人员开始领取政府资金年龄的后果的讨论。文本指出，通常在讨论这些资金的年龄提高时，关注的是对资金接受者的影响，但Andria Smythe却考虑了照顾退休人员的在职家庭成员的影响。Smythe提到，提高领取资金的年龄将增加退休人员依赖在职家庭成员提供财务援助的时间。这被认为会对这些工人的财富创造产生影响，而最合理的推测是，这种影响将是不利的。因此，“阻碍”这个词在上下文中是最合适的选择，它意味着防止或大大妨碍。
题目文本解析
关于提高退休人员开始领取政府资金转移的年龄的提议通常是从对资金接受者的影响来讨论的，但Andria Smythe则认为，延迟这些转移可能会______在职成年人创造财富，因为这会延长他们为不工作的父母提供财务支持的时间。

question:
In the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, automobiles were commonly referred to as horseless carriages after the older technology they still resembled. Known as the Brass Era, this period in automotive design is remembered for its grandeur and artistry, its vehicles ______ by collectors for their ornate detailing and gleaming brass fittings.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项C是最佳答案。所测试的语法规则是句子中动词形式的使用。非限定的过去分词短语“highly prized”被正确地用来构成一个补充成分，修饰主句“this…artistry”，描述了铜器时代汽车设计的令人难忘的特征。

question:
Researchers Helena Mihaljević-Brandt, Lucía Santamaría, and Marco Tullney report that while mathematicians may have traditionally worked alone, evidence points to a shift in the opposite direction. ______ mathematicians are choosing to collaborate with their peers—a trend illustrated by a rise in the number of mathematics publications credited to multiple authors.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
中文解析
选项D是最佳答案。“Increasingly”在逻辑上表明该句中的主张——数学家们正在与同行合作——相较于传统做法标志着一种变化。正如前一句所解释的，虽然数学家们可能传统上是独自工作的，但证据表明出现了相反的趋势。这个主张描述了这种变化：合作的增加。
题目文本解析
研究人员赫琳娜·米哈尔耶维奇-布兰特（Helena Mihaljević-Brandt）、露西亚·圣塔玛丽亚（Lucía Santamaría）和马尔科·图尔尼（Marco Tullney）报告称，尽管数学家们传统上可能是独立工作的，但证据显示出相反的趋势。______ 数学家们选择与同行合作——这一趋势体现在以多位作者署名的数学出版物数量的增加上。

question:
The ghazal, a poetic form originating in seventh-century Arabic poetry, has an intricate structure. The twentieth-century Kashmiri American poet Agha Shahid Ali explains that each one of a ghazal’s couplets, while adhering to the patterns of rhyme (qafia) and refrain (radif) established in the poem’s opening lines (matla), ______ thematically and logically autonomous, resulting in a poem with “a stringently formal disunity.”

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项A是最佳答案。所测试的语法规则是句子中动词形式的使用。单数动词“is”与单数主语“each one of a ghazal’s couplets”在数上保持一致。尽管主语中的介词短语“of a ghazal’s couplets”包含一个复数名词，但主语的核心部分（“each one”）是单数，这表明每一个个体的对句（而不是作为一个整体的对句）是“主题和逻辑上独立的”或自成一体的。

question:
In November 1934, Amrita Sher-Gil was living in what must have seemed like the ideal city for a young artist: Paris. She was studying firsthand the color-saturated style of France’s modernist masters and beginning to make a name for herself as a painter. ______ Sher-Gil longed to return to her childhood home of India; only there, she believed, could her art truly flourish.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
中文解析
选项A是最佳答案。“Still”在逻辑上表示该句中关于Sher-Gil的信息——她渴望离开巴黎回到印度——与在前几句中关于Sher-Gil在巴黎的经历所预期的信息形成对比。
题目文本解析
1934年11月，阿姆丽塔·谢尔吉尔（Amrita Sher-Gil）生活在一个对年轻艺术家来说似乎理想的城市：巴黎。她亲自学习着法国现代主义大师们色彩饱和的风格，并开始在绘画界崭露头角。______ 然而，谢尔吉尔渴望回到她的童年故乡印度；她相信，只有在那里，她的艺术才能真正蓬勃发展。

question:
With the development of new technologies that use natural resources more efficiently, the overall consumption of those resources might be expected to decrease. Economists have observed that improvements in efficiency often correlate negatively with resource ______ efficiency gains, lowering the cost of use, may increase demand to the extent that resource consumption ultimately rises.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项C是最佳答案。所测试的语法规则是句子内部标点的使用。这个选项正确地使用了逗号，将补充副词“though”与前面的主句（“Economists…conservation”）分开，并用分号将下一个主句（“efficiency gains…rises”）与句子的其余部分连接起来。此外，将分号放在“though”之后表明，前一个主句中的信息（“效率的改善通常与资源保护呈负相关”）与前一句中的信息（资源消费预计会随着新技术的开发而减少）相悖。

question:
Stomata, tiny pore structures in a leaf that absorb gases needed for plant growth, open when guard cells surrounding each pore swell with water. In a pivotal 2007 article, plant cell ______ showed that lipid molecules called phosphatidylinositol phosphates are responsible for signaling guard cells to open stomata.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项C是最佳答案。所测试的语法规则是标题和专有名词之间的标点使用。没有必要用标点符号将专有名词“Yuree Lee”与描述Lee的标题“植物细胞生物学家”分开。

question:
During the English neoclassical period (1660–1789), many writers imitated the epic poetry and satires of ancient Greece and Rome. They were not the first in England to adopt the literary modes of classical ______ some of the most prominent figures of the earlier Renaissance period were also influenced by ancient Greek and Roman literature.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项C是最佳答案。所测试的语法规则是从句后面补充短语的标点使用。这个选项使用逗号将补充副词短语“however”与其修饰的独立从句（“They...antiquity”）分开，并使用分号连接第一个独立从句（“They...antiquity”）和第二个独立从句（“some...literature”）。此外，将分号放在“however”之后表明，该从句所包含的信息（即新古典主义作家并不是第一个采用古典文学风格的人）与前一句中的信息（即新古典主义作家在模仿古典史诗和讽刺诗方面是独特的）相悖。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·NASA uses rovers, large remote vehicles with wheels, to explore the surface of Mars.
·NASA’s rovers can’t explore regions inaccessible to wheeled vehicles.
·Rovers are also heavy, making them difficult to land on the planet’s surface.
·Microprobes, robotic probes that weigh as little as 50 milligrams, could be deployed virtually anywhere on the surface of Mars.
·Microprobes have been proposed as an alternative to rovers.

The student wants to explain an advantage of microprobes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Despite being heavy, NASA’s rovers can land successfully on the surface of Mars.
B. Microprobes, which weigh as little as 50 milligrams, could explore areas of Mars that are inaccessible to NASA’s heavy, wheeled rovers.
C. NASA currently uses its rovers on Mars, but microprobes have been proposed as an alternative.
D. Though they are different sizes, both microprobes and rovers can be used to explore the surface of Mars.
explanations:
中文解析
选项B是最佳答案。该句解释了微探针的一个优点，指出由于微探针的重量仅为50毫克，它们能够探索探测器无法到达的区域。
题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- NASA使用探测器，即大型轮式遥控车辆，来探索火星表面。
- NASA的探测器无法探索轮式车辆无法到达的区域。
- 探测器也很重，这使得它们在火星表面着陆变得困难。
- 微探针是一种重量仅为50毫克的机器人探针，可以在火星表面的几乎任何地方部署。
- 微探针被提出作为探测器的替代方案。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·When medical students mention their patients on social media, they may violate patient confidentiality.
·Terry Kind led a study to determine how many medical schools have student policies that mention social media use.
·Kind and her team reviewed 132 medical school websites, examining publicly available student policies.
·Only thirteen medical schools had guidelines that explicitly mention social media, and only five defined what constitutes acceptable social media use.

The student wants to emphasize the study’s methodology. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. The student policies of 132 medical schools can be found online, according to research by Terry Kind.
B. To find out how many medical schools have guidelines about student social media use, Terry Kind and her team examined the student policies of 132 medical schools.
C. Out of 132 medical schools, only thirteen had student policies that mentioned social media, and only five specified what use was acceptable.
D. Terry Kind and her team wanted to know how many medical schools have student social media policies in place about protecting patient confidentiality.
explanations:
中文解析
选项B是最佳答案。该句有效地强调了Kind的研究方法：审查132所医学院的学生政策，以寻找关于学生社交媒体使用的指导方针。
题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 当医学生在社交媒体上提及他们的患者时，可能会违反患者的保密性。
- Terry Kind 领导了一项研究，以确定有多少医学院的学生政策提到了社交媒体使用。
- Kind及其团队审查了132所医学院的网站，检查了公开可用的学生政策。
- 只有十三所医学院有明确提到社交媒体的指导方针，只有五所定义了什么构成可接受的社交媒体使用。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·Puntius javanicus is a species of commercially raised fish.
·Researchers in Indonesia recently found that adding pineapple extract to fish food increased both the feed utilization efficiency and the growth rate of P. javanicus.
·Adding the pineapple extract did not affect total food consumption.
·The researchers thus determined that the increased growth rate resulted from the increased feed utilization efficiency.
·The enzyme bromelain in pineapple extract enhances the hydrolysis of ingested proteins.
·This allows the fish to more readily absorb them.

The student wants to explain how pineapple extract increased the growth rate of P. javanicus. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Researchers in Indonesia recently found that adding pineapple extract to fish food increased the growth rate of P. javanicus.
B. An enzyme in pineapple extract, bromelain increased the growth rate of P. javanicus by enhancing the hydrolysis of ingested proteins, in turn affecting the fish’s total food consumption.
C. According to the researchers, the growth rate of P. javanicus was affected not by food consumption but by feed utilization efficiency.
D. The enzyme bromelain enhanced P. javanicus’s absorption of ingested proteins, increasing the growth rate of fish fed pineapple extract.
explanations:
中文解析
选项D是最佳答案。该句有效地解释了菠萝提取物如何提高鱼的生长速度，指出菠萝提取物中的酶溴酶（bromelain）增强了食用菠萝提取物的鱼对摄入蛋白质的吸收。
题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- Puntius javanicus 是一种商业养殖的鱼类。
- 印度尼西亚的研究人员最近发现，向鱼饲料中添加菠萝提取物可以提高 P. javanicus 的饲料利用效率和生长速度。
- 添加菠萝提取物并未影响总的食物摄入量。
- 因此，研究人员确定生长速度的提高是由于饲料利用效率的增加。
- 菠萝提取物中的酶溴酶（bromelain）增强了摄入蛋白质的水解。
- 这使鱼能够更 readily 吸收这些蛋白质。

question:
The prime meridian, the global indicator of zero degrees longitude established in 1884, was originally determined using astronomically derived coordinates. ______ as decades passed, new calculations would reveal increasingly precise coordinates, yet the prime meridian remained unchanged; it wasn’t until the 1980s that, spurred by improved geodetic data, the prime meridian was officially moved—roughly one hundred meters east.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
中文解析
选项C是最佳答案。“Again and again”在逻辑上表明该句中的信息——新的计算揭示了越来越精确的本初子午线坐标——指的是在1884年本初子午线确立之后的几十年里发生的多次事件（这一点在前一句中有所描述）。
题目文本解析
本初子午线是1884年设定的全球零度经度标志，最初是通过天文学推导的坐标确定的。______ 随着时间的推移，新的计算显示出越来越精确的坐标，但本初子午线保持不变；直到1980年代，受到改进的测地数据的推动，本初子午线才正式向东移动了大约一百米。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·British musicians John Lennon and Paul McCartney shared writing credit for numerous Beatles songs.
·Many Lennon-McCartney songs were actually written by either Lennon or McCartney, not by both.
·The exact authorship of specific parts of many Beatles songs, such as the verse for “In My Life,” is disputed.
·Mark Glickman, Jason Brown, and Ryan Song used statistical methods to analyze the musical content of Beatles songs.
·They concluded that there is 18.9% probability that McCartney wrote the verse for “In My Life,” stating that the verse is “consistent with Lennon’s songwriting style.”

The student wants to make a generalization about the kind of study conducted by Glickman, Brown, and Song. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Based on statistical analysis, Glickman, Brown, and Song claim that John Lennon wrote the verse of “In My Life.”
B. There is only an 18.9% probability that Paul McCartney wrote the verse for “In My Life”; John Lennon is the more likely author.
C. It is likely that John Lennon, not Paul McCartney, wrote the verse for “In My Life.”
D. Researchers have used statistical methods to address questions of authorship within the field of music.
explanations:
中文解析
选项D是最佳答案。该句利用笔记中的信息对Glickman、Brown和Song所进行的研究类型进行了概括。具体来说，该句表明这项研究使用了统计方法来解决音乐领域内的作者身份问题。
题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 英国音乐家约翰·列侬和保罗·麦卡特尼共同分享了许多披头士歌曲的创作版权。
- 许多列侬-麦卡特尼的歌曲实际上是由列侬或麦卡特尼单独创作的，而不是两人共同创作的。
- 许多披头士歌曲中特定部分的确切作者身份存在争议，例如《In My Life》的歌词。
- 马克·格利克曼、杰森·布朗和瑞安·宋使用统计方法分析了披头士歌曲的音乐内容。
- 他们得出结论，麦卡特尼创作《In My Life》歌词的概率为18.9%，并表示这段歌词“与列侬的创作风格一致”。

question:
Domestic sheep’s wild ancestor, the mouflon, has a coarse outer coat and an inner coat of wool fiber that is finer in diameter and therefore much softer. In some domestic breeds, such as the Spanish Merino, the outer fiber is only marginally coarser than the inner, and the wool is soft overall. Thus, Merino wool is ideal for delicate garments worn against the skin. Meanwhile, the Navajo-Churro has been selected to retain the marked distinction between outer and inner fiber that the Merino has lost. Being coarser than Merino wool overall, Navajo-Churro wool yields a more durable yarn, which Diné (Navajo) weavers use in their celebrated rugs. Yet a comparison of the fiber characteristics of all three sheep reveals that ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
selections: A. the selection process that enabled the Navajo-Churro to retain its somewhat coarse outer fiber also resulted in inner fiber that, at its softest, is softer than either the mouflon’s or the Merino’s inner fiber.

B. the Navajo-Churro more closely resembles its ancestor, the mouflon, in the uniform softness of its inner fiber, while the Merino more closely resembles the mouflon in the variable diameter of its outer fiber.

C. domestication resulted in a counterintuitive increase in the inner fiber’s minimum diameter, making the inner fiber of the Merino and the Navajo-Churro less suitable for delicate garments than the mouflon’s inner fiber is.
D. the domestication of the mouflon and the subsequent selection process that produced the Merino and the Navajo-Churro resulted in greater softness of outer and inner fiber alike.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
家养绵羊的野生祖先——欧洲盘羊，具有粗糙的外层毛和直径更细、因此更柔软的绒毛内层。在一些家养品种中，如西班牙美利奴羊，外层毛纤维仅略粗于内层毛，整体羊毛柔软。因此美利奴羊毛非常适合制作贴身佩戴的精致衣物。与此同时，纳瓦霍-楚罗羊则被选育保留了外层与内层纤维之间的显著差异，而这一差异在美利奴羊身上已消失。纳瓦霍-楚罗羊毛总体上比美利奴羊毛更粗糙，因而纺出的纱线更耐用，纳瓦霍织工用它来编织其著名的地毯。然而，对这三种羊纤维特征的比较却揭示出：______
答案解析：
根据表格数据，欧洲盘羊内层纤维直径为15微米，美利奴羊内层直径为17–21微米（最小17微米），纳瓦霍-楚罗羊内层直径为10–35微米（最细可达10微米）。因此纳瓦霍-楚罗羊最柔软的内层纤维（10微米）比欧洲盘羊（15微米）和美利奴羊（17微米）都更细、更软。选项A准确描述了这一发现：纳瓦霍-楚罗羊保留粗糙外层的同时，其最柔软的内层纤维比欧洲盘羊和美利奴羊的内层纤维更软。其他选项与表格数据不符。因此选A。

question:
Outi Tervo and team studied the effect of human-caused noise on narwhals (Monodon monoceros), arctic marine mammals that are sensitive to acoustic changes in their environment. Hypothesizing that elevated sound levels affect foraging among narwhals, Tervo’s team compared narwhal diving behaviors in natural sound conditions with those behaviors in two human-caused sound exposure conditions—ship sounds and ship sounds coupled with sonic pulses. Both exposure conditions resulted in significant decreases in the number and target depth of deep dives (associated with foraging) relative to natural conditions. However, differences between diving behaviors in the two exposure types were negligible, a finding that could be attributed to the fact that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. sonic pulses can be heard at significantly greater ocean depths than ship sounds can.
B. ship sounds contribute so much to the overall sound level that the addition of sonic pulses has little effect on the narwhals’ auditory environment.
C. narwhals forage at shallower depths in the presence of ship sounds alone than in the presence of ship sounds coupled with sonic pulses.
D. the narwhals weren’t as sensitive to human-caused sounds as the researchers had predicted.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
Outi Tervo 及其团队研究了人为噪音对独角鲸（Monodon monoceros）的影响。独角鲸是一种对环境中声学变化敏感的北极海洋哺乳动物。研究团队假设，提高的声波水平会影响独角鲸的觅食行为，于是比较了独角鲸在自然声音条件下与在两种人为声音暴露条件（船舶声音、船舶声音加声脉冲）下的潜水行为。相较于自然条件，两种暴露条件均导致深潜（与觅食相关）的次数和目标深度显著减少。然而，两种暴露条件下的潜水行为差异可忽略不计，这一发现可能归因于______
答案解析：
研究指出，船舶声音与船舶声音加声脉冲两种条件下，独角鲸的潜水行为几乎没有差异。最合理的解释是船舶声音本身对噪音环境的贡献已经很大，额外添加声脉冲未能显著改变整体声学环境，因此对独角鲸行为的影响有限。选项B准确描述了这一逻辑。其他选项与“两种条件差异可忽略”的发现不一致。因此选B。

question:
A casual description of Scherezade García’s 2019 mural Blame It on the Bean: The Power of Coffee can make the work seem ______—a painting that is housed in a coffee shop and that depicts three women drinking coffee may not sound particularly ambitious—but in fact the work is a complex, dynamic meditation on gender and the legacy of colonialism that demands serious attention.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
对舍雷扎德·加西亚2019年壁画《怪罪于豆：咖啡的力量》的随意描述可能会让这幅作品显得______——一幅挂在咖啡店里、描绘三位女性喝咖啡的画作听起来可能并不特别宏大——但事实上，这部作品是对性别与殖民主义遗产的一次复杂、动态的深刻思考，值得严肃关注。
答案解析：
根据上下文，“随意描述让作品显得______”与后文“但事实上它复杂且深刻”形成转折，因此该空应表达“朴素、不张扬”之意。选项A “unassuming”（谦逊的、不引人注目的）最符合这一语境。其他选项“shrewd”（精明的）、“incongruous”（不协调的）、“pretentious”（矫饰的）均与转折逻辑不符。因此选A。

question:
Curious about how people visually perceive objects in their dreams, Stephen LaBerge and team recruited lucid dreamers—people aware that they’re dreaming as it’s happening—for a research study. These participants were reliably able to signal when they had entered a dream state; the team then observed participants’ eye movements as they slept. The smoothness with which participants’ eyes tracked objects in their dreams closely matched how sighted people who are awake visually track objects around them, suggesting to the team that the brain perceives dream objects as the product of something other than pure imagination.

Which choice best states the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
selections: A. To offer key evidence that undermines LaBerge and team’s initial hypothesis
B. To show the unexpected result that led LaBerge and team to change the focus of their study
C. To illustrate an important real-world implication of LaBerge and team’s main finding
D. To identify a comparable circumstance that helps justify LaBerge and team’s conclusion
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
为了探究人们在梦中如何视觉感知物体，斯蒂芬·拉伯格及其团队招募了清明梦者（在梦境中意识到自己正在做梦的人）进行一项研究。这些参与者能够在进入梦境状态时可靠地发出信号；随后团队在参与者睡眠时观察他们的眼球运动。参与者在梦中追踪物体时眼动的平滑程度，与清醒的视力正常者在视觉追踪周围物体时的表现极为相似，这让团队得出结论：大脑将梦中物体视为某种超越纯粹想象的事物。
答案解析：
划线部分将梦中的眼动追踪与清醒时的视觉追踪进行对比，指出两者极为相似，从而为研究团队的结论提供了支持依据。选项D准确描述了这一功能：通过指出一个具有可比性的情境，帮助论证研究团队的结论。其他选项均与文本内容不符。因此选D。

question:
“Aunt Sue’s Stories” is a 1926 poem by Langston Hughes. In the poem, the speaker indicates that the stories Aunt Sue tells are based on Aunt Sue’s personal experiences, saying that ______

Which choice most effectively uses a quotation from “Aunt Sue’s Stories” to illustrate the claim?
selections: A. dark shadows “cross and recross / Aunt Sue’s stories.”
B. a listening child “knows that Aunt Sue / Never got her stories out of any book at all, / But that they came / Right out of her own life.”
C. the stories are told during “Summer nights on the front porch.”
D. the people in the stories “Mingle themselves softly / In the flow of old Aunt Sue’s voice, / Mingle themselves softly.”
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
《苏阿姨的故事》是兰斯顿·休斯1926年创作的一首诗。在诗中，说话者指出苏阿姨所讲的故事都基于她个人的亲身经历，说道：______
答案解析：
选项B中的引文直接表明苏阿姨的故事“绝非来自任何书本，而是来自她自己的生活”，最有效地支持了“故事基于个人经历”这一主张。其他选项或描写听故事的氛围与光影，或描写故事中人物的融入方式，均未直接体现故事源于亲身经历。因此选B。

question:
Although the government of the Soviet Union attempted to ______ Georgi Vladimov’s novel Faithful Ruslan, copies of the book circulated in secret among readers in several parts of the country.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
尽管苏联政府试图______格奥尔基·弗拉基莫夫的小说《忠实的鲁斯兰》，但该书的副本仍在该国多个地区的读者之间秘密流传。
答案解析：
根据逻辑，句子想要表达政府试图“压制”这部小说，但未能成功，因此“suppress”（压制）最符合语境。其他选项“replicate”（复制）、“critique”（批评）、“import”（进口）均与“秘密流传”的语境不匹配。因此选D。

question:
Following the eradication of the gray wolf in Yellowstone National Park in 1926, the population of elk—a primary prey of the gray wolf—exceeded a healthy size for the park’s ecosystem. Elk overpopulation led to overgrazing of areas that a multitude of other animals relied on for food and shelter. As scientists began to see how essential the gray wolf was to the Yellowstone food chain, ecological restoration strategies were employed to reintroduce the gray wolf to the park in 1996. The rebound effect in the park’s natural ecosystem was noticed almost immediately.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
selections: A. It summarizes a problem that developed in Yellowstone National Park in the 1920s and then offers potential solutions to that problem.
B. It mentions the elimination of the gray wolf from Yellowstone National Park and then explains why the wolf was eventually restored to the park.
C. It presents a claim about the health of the Yellowstone National Park gray wolf population and then gives specific examples to support that claim.
D. It explains why Yellowstone National Park allowed the eradication of the gray wolf and then discusses the consequences of reintroducing the wolf to the park.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
1926年黄石国家公园的灰狼被消灭后，作为灰狼主要猎物的麋鹿种群数量超出了公园生态系统的健康范围。麋鹿数量过剩导致许多其他动物赖以生存和栖息的区域被过度啃食。当科学家开始认识到灰狼对黄石食物链的重要性后，1996年实施了生态恢复策略，将灰狼重新引入公园。公园自然生态系统的反弹效应几乎立竿见影。
答案解析：
选项B准确地概括了文本结构：先提及灰狼被消灭（elimination），然后解释最终重新引入灰狼的原因（why the wolf was eventually restored）。文本并未提供多种解决方案（排除A），未提出关于灰狼种群数量的主张（排除C），也未解释为何允许消灭灰狼（排除D）。因此选B。

question:
Few animals are known to spit: among them are humans, cobras, and camels. But in January 2022 at a nature preserve in southern England, bird-watcher Clare Jacobs observed a gray seal spitting a jet of water at a white-tailed eagle flying overhead. Seals had never been seen spitting before. Biologist Sean Twiss, who studies gray seals, believes that the seal may have been attempting to scare the eagle away from a food source or that the seal may have just been playing.

Which choice best states the main topic of the text?
selections: B. A previously unseen behavior of gray seals
C. How white-tailed eagles defend their territory against other predators
D. Differences between gray seals and white-tailed eagles
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
会喷吐的动物很少见：其中包括人类、眼镜蛇和骆驼。但2022年1月，在英格兰南部的一处自然保护区，观鸟者克莱尔·雅各布斯观察到一只灰海豹向头顶飞过的白尾海雕喷出一股水柱。此前从未有人见过海豹喷水。研究灰海豹的生物学家肖恩·特维斯认为，这只海豹可能是试图将鹰从食物来源处吓跑，也可能只是在玩耍。
答案解析：
文本的核心内容是灰海豹被观察到一种此前从未记录过的行为——喷水，并引用了生物学家的推测。因此选项B“灰海豹一种此前未见的行为”最准确地概括了主旨。

question:
Since the Hubble Space Telescope was launched into space in 1990, astronauts have needed to complete regular missions to repair the telescope and keep it working smoothly. Researchers hope that robots will soon be able to make these repairs. Employing robots instead of humans to make repairs will be helpful, as ______ astronauts to maintain the telescope can be expensive.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
自1990年哈勃太空望远镜发射升空以来，宇航员需要定期执行维修任务以保持其正常运转。研究人员希望机器人能够很快承担这些维修工作。使用机器人而非人类进行维修将大有裨益，因为______宇航员来维护望远镜成本高昂。
答案解析：
根据逻辑，句意想要表达“依赖宇航员进行维护成本高”，因此“relying on”（依赖）最贴切。其他选项“straightening”（矫正）、“forgetting about”（忘记）、“reducing”（减少）在逻辑和语义上均不符合语境。因此选C。

question:
Founded in 1965 and originally established as a cultural extension of the United Farm Workers—a union representing many Mexican American agricultural workers at the time—the theater troupe El Teatro Campesino has achieved recognition as a source of inspiration for subsequent Chicano theater companies and as a contributor to the dramatic arts. In an article about the company, a theater historian posits that a significant stylistic influence on El Teatro’s early performances was the audience-mediated slapstick comedy of carpa theater, vaudeville-style shows popular in Mexico and the US Southwest in the 1920s and ’30s.

Which quotation from the article would best illustrate the theater historian’s claim?
selections: A. “The company presented actos, short comedy sketches, that often relied on exaggerated physical humor to groups of agricultural workers, whose reactions—enthusiastic cheers of appreciation and, occasionally, loud boos of disapproval—promoted improvisation.”

B. “The company was focused on the reality of the present situation and discovered that humor was often found in that reality; consequently, comedy became a tool to convey social critique while entertaining and inspiring audiences.”

C. “The company relied heavily on satire, humor, and references to contemporary popular culture as well as a make-do aesthetic—often referred to as rasquache—that reflected not only the troupe’s limited financial resources but also its sociopolitical message.”

D. “The members of the company, which in addition to founder Luis Valdez consisted entirely of nonprofessional actors, traveled into farm fields, where they, with minimal props and costumes, performed comedy in the form of brief humorous vignettes.”
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
El Teatro Campesino 剧团成立于1965年，最初作为美国农场工人联合会（当时代表许多墨西哥裔农业工人的工会）的文化延伸机构，后来被公认为为后续奇卡诺戏剧公司提供灵感的重要来源，并为戏剧艺术作出了贡献。在一篇关于该剧团的文章中，一位戏剧史学家提出，对 El Teatro 早期表演产生重要风格影响的，是 carpa 戏剧中由观众参与的滑稽喜剧——这是20世纪20至30年代在墨西哥和美国西南部流行的一种杂耍式表演。
答案解析：
选项A直接体现了“由观众参与的滑稽喜剧”这一风格特征：剧团向农业工人群体表演短喜剧，依靠夸张的肢体幽默，观众的反应（喝彩或嘘声）促进了即兴表演。这与史学家的主张最为吻合。其他选项虽涉及喜剧、讽刺或即兴元素，但未突出观众互动这一核心特征。因此选A。

question:
Text 1
Good art often challenges and disrupts social and aesthetic norms, but the creation of public art—paintings, sculptures, and performance pieces displayed in nonmuseum or nontheatrical public settings—typically requires broad agreement among artists, civic officials, and community members about the works’ message and artistic goals. Public art that fails to appease everyone by being sufficiently aesthetically and conceptually bland almost inevitably provokes backlash.
Text 2
Public art is commonly displayed in spaces intended for purposes other than meaningful aesthetic engagement. Some critics of public art therefore note that norm-defying pieces that aren’t effectively integrated within their surroundings in a manner that primes passersby to appreciate the pieces’ merits (as is often the case) tend to be regarded more unfavorably than similarly provocative art encountered in museums is.

Based on the texts, how would the critics mentioned in Text 2 most likely respond to the underlined claim in Text 1?
selections: A. By arguing that the reason members of the general public might disagree about a public artwork’s merits is unrelated to the unconventionality of its appearance and ideas
B. By agreeing with the idea that only works of art that are universally appealing are suitable for displaying in public spaces
C. By disputing the notion that civic leaders and community members are easily placated by art that is intended mainly to reinforce social norms
D. By contending that the kinds of reactions controversial public artworks often receive aren’t exclusively the result of attributes inherent in the works themselves
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
文本1：优秀的艺术常常挑战并颠覆社会与审美规范，但公共艺术——在非博物馆或非剧院的公共环境中展示的绘画、雕塑和行为艺术作品——的创作通常需要艺术家、市政官员和社区成员就作品的信息和艺术目标达成广泛共识。那些在美学和概念上过于平淡以求取悦所有人的公共艺术，几乎不可避免地会引发反弹。文本2：公共艺术通常陈列在并非为了进行有意义的审美参与而设计的空间。因此，一些公共艺术评论者指出，那些违反规范且未能以恰当方式融入周围环境、使路过者得以欣赏其优点的作品（这往往是常见情况），往往会比在博物馆中遇到的同样具有挑衅性的艺术受到更多负面评价。
答案解析：
文本1划线部分认为，公共艺术之所以需要广泛共识，是因为一旦作品不够平淡就几乎必然引发反弹。文本2中的评论者则会反驳这一观点，指出引发负面反应的往往不是作品本身的属性，而是展示环境的差异（公共空间未预设审美参与，而博物馆则不同）。因此选D，即他们认为争议性公共艺术作品所引发的反应，并非完全源于作品本身的特质。

question:
The following text is adapted from Fanny Burney’s 1778 novel Evelina. The text is an excerpt from a letter by Lady Howard to Evelina’s guardian, Reverend Villars, in which Lady Howard discusses an upcoming trip to London planned by her daughter Mrs. Mirvan’s family.
It is very earnestly [the Mirvans’] wish to enlarge and enliven their party by the addition of your amiable ward, who would share, equally with her own daughter, the care and attention of Mrs. Mirvan. Do not start at this proposal; it is time that [Evelina] should see something of the world. When young people are too rigidly sequestered from it, their lively and romantic imaginations paint it to them as a paradise of which they have been beguiled; but when they are shown it properly, and in due time, they see it such as it really is, equally shared by pain and pleasure, hope and disappointment.

Based on the text, Lady Howard would most likely agree with which statement about Reverend Villars?
selections: A. Although the manner in which he has raised Evelina is in many ways exemplary, he has been misguided in shielding her from the influence of other young people.
B. He has imparted to Evelina his own idealistic view of the world, which results in her being unprepared to face inevitable disappointments.
C. Although his desire to guard Evelina from unscrupulous people is commendable, his general mistrust has led him to be unduly wary of the Mirvans.
D. He is overly protective of Evelina, who would likely benefit from a greater variety of experiences than she has had thus far.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
以下文字改编自范妮·伯尼1778年的小说《埃维莉娜》。文本摘自已故霍华德夫人写给埃维莉娜的监护人维拉斯牧师的一封信，信中霍华德夫人谈到了女儿米尔文太太一家即将前往伦敦的计划。
米尔文一家非常热切地希望，若能让你这位可爱的被监护人加入，他们的旅行将更加热闹、更有活力。米尔文太太会像照顾自己女儿一样照顾她。请不要对这项提议感到惊讶；埃维莉娜是时候去见见世面了。当年轻人被过于严格地与世隔绝时，他们那鲜活而浪漫的想象力会把世界描绘成一片被剥夺的乐园；但若在恰当的时机让他们正确地去见识，他们便会看到世界本来的模样：痛苦与欢乐、希望与失望兼而有之。
答案解析：
霍华德夫人认为埃维莉娜被保护得过于严密，导致她对世界抱有不切实际的浪漫想象，而适当接触世界能让她看到真实的生活。因此她认为维拉斯牧师对埃维莉娜的保护过度，而她本可以从更丰富的经历中受益。选项D最符合这一观点。

question:
Researchers Eugeni Vidal-Tortosa and Robin Lovelace looked at the relationship between street lighting in a city and people’s willingness to ride a bicycle. Their results suggest that poor street lighting can deter new or inexperienced cyclists from riding in a city but has little effect on experienced cyclists. Therefore, increasing the number of streetlights in a city could potentially ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. decrease the number of new or inexperienced cyclists riding in the city.
B. increase the number of experienced cyclists riding in the city.
C. decrease the number of experienced cyclists riding in the city.
D. increase the number of new or inexperienced cyclists riding in the city.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
研究人员 Eugeni Vidal-Tortosa 和 Robin Lovelace 研究了城市街道照明与人们骑自行车意愿之间的关系。研究结果表明，较差的街道照明会阻碍新骑手或经验不足的骑手在城市中骑行，但对经验丰富的骑手影响不大。因此，增加城市中路灯的数量可能会______
答案解析：
研究指出，照明差会阻碍新骑手或经验不足者，但对有经验者影响小。那么改善照明（增加路灯）应能消除这种阻碍，从而吸引更多新手或经验不足者骑行。因此选项D最符合逻辑。其他选项与研究发现的方向相反或无关。因此选D。

question:
In a 2022 study, Nicolás M. Morato and colleagues attempted to resolve a long-standing paradox: although water is critical to most reactions that enable life, during the earliest stages of Earth’s history—when most of the planet’s surface was covered by oceans—the presence of water likely ______ the formation of proteins and other biomolecules that are found in all living organisms.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
在2022年的一项研究中，尼古拉斯·M·莫拉托及其同事试图解决一个长期存在的悖论：尽管水对大多数维持生命的反应至关重要，但在地球历史的最早期——当时地球大部分表面被海洋覆盖——水的存在很可能______了蛋白质及其他在所有生物体中都能找到的生物分子的形成。
答案解析：
根据逻辑，“paradox”（悖论）一词表明，虽然水通常对生命反应很重要，但在早期地球条件下它却起到了相反的作用。因此“hampered”（阻碍）最符合语境。其他选项“reflected”（反映）、“imitated”（模仿）、“exploited”（利用）均与悖论所暗示的阻碍关系不符。因此选B。

question:
Researchers Kate Howlett and Edgar Turner asked 401 schoolchildren in the United Kingdom to draw and label local wildlife. The researchers suggest that the children may be more aware of mammals than of other animals in their environments.

Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the researchers’ conclusion?
selections: A. There were about as many drawings with an example of an insect as there were with an example of a bird.
B. The fewest number of drawings contained an example of a bird.
C. More of the drawings had an example of an insect than an example of a mammal.
D. More of the drawings had an example of a mammal than either an example of a bird or an example of an insect.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
研究人员凯特·豪利特和埃德加·特纳让英国401名学龄儿童绘制并标注当地的野生动物。研究人员推测，孩子们可能对哺乳动物比对环境中其他动物更为熟悉。
答案解析：
选项D指出“画作中包含哺乳动物实例的数量多于包含鸟类或昆虫实例的数量”，这直接支持了研究者关于孩子们对哺乳动物更熟悉的结论。其他选项要么说明昆虫与鸟类数量相近（A），要么说鸟类最少（B），或者昆虫多于哺乳动物（C），均未体现哺乳动物的认知优势。因此选D。

question:
Topographic maps show the elevation of landforms above sea level. Bathymetric maps, ______show the elevation of landforms below the sea, providing valuable information to marine geophysicists like Claudia Flores, who studies seismic data from the northeastern Caribbean.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
地形图显示的是陆地地貌高于海平面的海拔高度。而测深图______显示的是海面以下地貌的海拔高度，为像克劳迪娅·弗洛雷斯这样研究加勒比海东北部地震数据的海洋地球物理学家提供了宝贵的信息。
答案解析：
文本前半句介绍地形图显示陆上地貌，后半句介绍测深图显示海底地貌，二者形成对比关系。因此“by contrast”（相比之下）最符合逻辑。其他选项“in conclusion”（总之）表总结，“for example”（例如）表举例，“afterward”（之后）表时间顺序，均不适用。因此选C。

question:
Most of the ice found on Earth is ice Ih, distinguished by a crystalline structure in which molecules form a hexagonal pattern. Amorphous ice, on the other hand, constitutes most of the ice in the ultrafrigid environment of outer space. Defined by a disorganized molecular structure, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
selections: A. ice Ih contains crystals, whereas amorphous ice, which lacks the thermal energy to form them, does not.
B. amorphous ice lacks the thermal energy to form the crystals found in ice Ih.
C. the lack of thermal energy in amorphous ice explains its inability to form the crystals found in ice Ih.
D. ice Ih differs from amorphous ice in that it possesses the thermal energy to form crystals.
explanations: 逻辑主语一致，defined by disorganized molecular structure根据前文只能对应amorphous ice，所以选B

question:
According to the original text of the US Constitution, written in 1787, the presidential candidate receiving the second-most Electoral College votes becomes vice president. The 12th amendment, ratified in ______separated the elections for the two offices.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 双逗号引导的插入语

question:
Al-Andalus, the historical region of the Iberian Peninsula that includes most of modern-day Spain, was ruled by various Arabic-speaking Muslim states between the eighth and fifteenth centuries. ______many Arabic words, such as “alacrán”—meaning “scorpion”—made their way into the Spanish language.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
安达卢斯是伊比利亚半岛的历史地区，包括现代西班牙的大部分领土。在八世纪至十五世纪期间，该地区由多个讲阿拉伯语的穆斯林国家统治。______许多阿拉伯词汇，如意为“蝎子”的“alacrán”，进入了西班牙语。
答案解析：
前文指出阿拉伯语统治的时期，后文说明阿拉伯词汇进入西班牙语，两者存在因果关系——正是因为阿拉伯语国家的统治，才导致了词汇的引入。因此“Consequently”（因此，结果）最符合逻辑。其他选项“For example”（例如）表举例，“Instead”（相反）表转折，“Specifically”（具体来说）表细化，均不适用。因此选D。

question:
Long thought to be sessile (immobile), adult Chelonibia testudinaria, barnacles that adhere to sea turtle shells, have been observed to shift slightly in position over time—a phenomenon that has been attributed to the barnacles’ passive displacement by water currents. ______a research team found that adult C. testudinaria moved toward the heads of their sea turtle hosts and thus against the prevailing water flow, behavior consistent with self-initiated locomotion.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
长期以来，人们认为成年龟甲藤壶（Chelonibia testudinaria，附着在海龟壳上的藤壶）是固着不动的，但后来观察到它们会随时间推移而发生轻微的位置移动——这一现象曾被归因于水流导致的被动位移。______一个研究团队发现，成年龟甲藤壶会向海龟宿主的头部方向移动，即逆着主要水流方向移动，这种行为符合自主移动的特征。
答案解析：
前文将藤壶的移动归因于水流的被动作用，而后文的研究发现藤壶是逆水流移动，属于主动行为，这与前文的解释相矛盾。因此“Undermining this explanation”（削弱这种解释）最符合逻辑。其他选项“Contrary to this phenomenon”（与这一现象相反）语义不当，“Drawing a similar conclusion”（得出相似结论）和“Confirming this hypothesis”（证实这一假设）均与前后文转折关系不符。因此选B。

question:
The rough frog is a species of amphibian native to Australia. Currently, the frog’s range ______parts of northern New South Wales and southeastern Queensland.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 考察时态，一般现在时，所以选A

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·Edmonia Lewis (1844–1907) was an African American and Mississauga Ojibwe sculptor.
·Forever Free (1867) is a marble sculpture by Lewis.
·It depicts a male figure and a female figure gazing upward.
·It commemorates the 1863 Emancipation Proclamation.
·The phrase “forever free” from the text of the Emancipation Proclamation is inscribed on the sculpture’s base.
·Art historian Kirsten Buick describes the sculpture as a “celebration of liberty.”

The student wants to explain the sculpture’s specific historical context. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. According to art historian Kirsten Buick, Forever Free, which depicts a male figure and a female figure gazing upward, is a “celebration of liberty.”
B. The base of Edmonia Lewis’s 1867 marble sculpture is inscribed with a historically significant phrase: “forever free.”
C. Completed in 1867, Lewis’s sculpture Forever Free commemorates the Emancipation Proclamation, which had been issued four years previously.
D. Forever Free (1867) is a marble sculpture by Edmonia Lewis, an African American and Mississauga Ojibwe sculptor who lived from 1844 to 1907.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
在研究一个主题时，一名学生记录了以下笔记：
·埃德莫尼亚·刘易斯（1844–1907）是一位非裔美国人与密西沙加奥吉布瓦族雕塑家。
·《永远自由》（1867）是刘易斯创作的一件大理石雕塑。
·雕塑描绘了一男一女两个人物仰望的姿态。
·它纪念1863年的《解放黑人奴隶宣言》。
·雕塑底座上刻有《解放黑人奴隶宣言》中的“永远自由”一词。
·艺术史学家柯尔斯滕·布伊克将这件雕塑描述为“对自由的礼赞”。
答案解析：
选项C直接说明了雕塑《永远自由》是为了纪念四年前颁布的《解放黑人奴隶宣言》，将作品与具体历史事件（1863年宣言）联系起来，最有效地呈现了历史背景。其他选项或侧重艺术评价（A）、或仅提及底座题词（B）、或介绍作者身份（D），均未突出历史背景。因此选C。

question:
Cy Twombly, a US painter and sculptor, created many large-scale abstract works, such as his 10-painting series Fifty Days at Iliam. In these works, Twombly’s artistic style is exemplified by his use of graffiti-like ______ often incorporate words or phrases from poetry and mythology.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: that引导定语从句修饰scribbles，先行词和引导词之间不加逗号

question:
In rural Minnesota, ecologist Leroy Walston conducted a study to determine whether seeding solar panel fields with wildflowers could bolster pollinator populations in nearby food crops. Walston’s findings indicate that—assuming solar panel installers’______practice has the potential to increase the number of native bees in crops near solar fields throughout the Midwest by up to 20 percent.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 双破折号引导的插入语

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·“Organ2/ASLSP (As Slow as Possible)” is a musical piece by avant-garde composer John Cage.
·A specially designed automated organ in St. Burchardi Church in Halberstadt, Germany, began playing the piece in 2001.
·It is scheduled to stop playing the piece in 2640.
·The performance will last 639 years.
·It will be the longest continuous musical performance in history.

The student wants to indicate how long John Cage’s musical piece will last. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. John Cage is the composer of the musical piece “Organ2/ASLSP (As Slow as Possible).”
B. “Organ2/ASLSP (As Slow as Possible)” is a musical piece currently being played in St. Burchardi Church in Halberstadt, Germany.
C. Lasting 639 years, John Cage’s musical piece will be the longest continuous musical performance in history.
D. An organ in St. Burchardi Church in Halberstadt, Germany, began playing a musical piece by avant-garde composer John Cage.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
在研究一个主题时，一名学生记录了以下笔记：
·《Organ²/ASLSP（尽可能慢）》是先锋派作曲家约翰·凯奇的音乐作品。
·位于德国哈尔伯施塔特圣伯查迪教堂的一台特制自动管风琴于2001年开始演奏该作品。
·该演出计划于2640年结束。
·这场演出将持续639年。
·它将成为历史上持续时间最长的连续音乐演出。
答案解析：
选项C直接说明了作品将持续639年，并指出这将成为历史上最长的连续音乐演出，最有效地利用了笔记中的相关信息。其他选项或未提及持续时间（A、B、D），或仅说明演奏地点和开始时间，未能实现说明时长这一目标。因此选C。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·In a 2020 study, researchers in California investigated how many potential nesting sites female wood ducks visited during the nesting season.
·The researchers placed nest boxes throughout the survey area and tagged 138 female wood ducks with radio frequency ID trackers.
·These trackers recorded how many nest boxes each duck visited.
·67 ducks (48.5%) visited only one nest box.
·18 ducks (13.0%) visited 10 or more nest boxes.
·Younger ducks were more likely to visit multiple nest boxes.

The student wants to present the methods used in the 2020 study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. By recording how many nest boxes each duck visited, the researchers discovered that only a relatively small percentage (13.0%) of the ducks visited 10 or more nest boxes.
B. After tracking how many nest boxes the 138 wood ducks visited, the researchers found that the younger ducks tended to visit more nest boxes than the older ducks.
C. The researchers tagged 138 female wood ducks with radio frequency ID trackers and recorded how many nest boxes each duck visited during the nesting season.
D. The researchers investigated each nesting site for signs that it had been visited by the female wood ducks.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
在研究一个主题时，一名学生记录了以下笔记：
·在2020年的一项研究中，加利福尼亚州的研究人员调查了雌性林鸭在筑巢季节会探访多少个潜在筑巢点。
·研究人员在整个调查区域内放置了巢箱，并为138只雌性林鸭佩戴了射频识别追踪器。
·这些追踪器记录下每只鸭子探访了多少个巢箱。
·67只鸭子（48.5%）只探访了一个巢箱。
·18只鸭子（13.0%）探访了10个或更多巢箱。
·较年轻的鸭子更可能探访多个巢箱。
答案解析：
选项C直接描述了研究中使用的方法：为138只雌性林鸭佩戴射频识别追踪器，并记录每只鸭子在筑巢季节探访的巢箱数量，涵盖了研究方法的核心步骤。其他选项或侧重于研究结果（A、B），或与笔记内容不符（D）。因此选C。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
·2024: Spain and Portugal sponsored a workshop to address recent encounters between Iberian orcas and marine vessels off the Iberian Peninsula.
·Many of the 637 documented incidents involved pods of orcas damaging vessels by ramming, nudging, or biting the rudders.
·Studies of Iberian orcas suggest recent increases in tuna populations have reduced the time the orcas spend hunting by 99%.
·Researchers believe this shift has increased the number of interactions between marine vessels and understimulated orcas.
·The workshop advised mariners to avoid orcas pending further testing of the efficacy of TAST, a harmless acoustic deterrent.

The student wants to make and support a claim about Iberian orca behavior. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. The recent destructive behavior of Iberian orcas may be the result of understimulation, given that orcas’ interactions with marine vessels have increased as the orcas have spent less time hunting.
B. As supported by the workshop’s analysis of 637 encounters between vessels and Iberian orcas, TAST is a harmless and effective acoustic deterrent.
C. In 2024, Spain and Portugal sponsored a workshop that addressed incidents where pods of Iberian orcas were ramming, nudging, or biting the rudders of vessels.
D. Tuna populations have increased by approximately 99% off the Iberian Peninsula due to changes in the hunting behavior of Iberian orcas.
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
在研究一个主题时，一名学生记录了以下笔记：
·2024年：西班牙和葡萄牙共同主办了一个研讨会，旨在应对伊比利亚虎鲸与伊比利亚半岛附近船只之间近期发生的接触事件。
·在记录的637起事件中，许多涉及虎鲸群通过撞击、轻推或咬船舵来破坏船只。
·对伊比利亚虎鲸的研究表明，近期金枪鱼数量的增加使虎鲸捕猎时间减少了99%。
·研究人员认为，这一变化增加了船只与刺激不足的虎鲸之间的互动次数。
·研讨会建议船员暂时避开虎鲸，等待对一种无害声波驱赶装置TAST的有效性进行进一步测试。
答案解析：
选项A提出了一个观点（虎鲸的破坏性行为可能源于刺激不足），并用笔记中的信息（捕猎时间减少导致互动增加）作为支持，符合“提出并支持观点”的要求。其他选项或仅陈述事实（C）、或与笔记信息不符（B、D）。因此选A。

question:
Text 1
Chemically analyzing bulk rock-core samples from Australia’s Mount McRae Shale, Ariel Anbar et al. found a transient but significant increase in molybdenum (Mo) at a point corresponding to roughly 2.5 billion years ago (Ga). On Earth, Mo is released mainly through oxidative weathering of minerals; Anbar et al. therefore concluded that atmospheric oxygen briefly increased 2.5 Ga, then returned to its earlier negligible level.
Text 2
Sarah Slotznick et al. reexamined the Mount McRae Shale core. Since chemically analyzing bulk samples can occlude contextual details, Slotznick et al. also employed high-resolution microscopy, which revealed volcanic debris—a known Mo host—around 2.5 Ga and microfractures in the surrounding matrix. The researchers assert that fluid could have reached the debris through the microfractures and initiated oxidative weathering long after debris deposition.

Based on the texts, Anbar et al. (Text 1) and Slotznick et al. (Text 2) would most likely disagree about the answer to which question about the portion of the Mount McRae Shale rock-core corresponding to 2.5 Ga?
selections: A. Does the increase in Mo in that portion suggest that atmospheric oxygen levels were not negligible before 2.5 Ga?
B. Is the increase in Mo in that portion indicative of an increase in atmospheric oxygen dating to the same time?
C. Is the increase in Mo in that portion attributable to oxidative weathering of the material found in that portion?
D. Did chemically analyzing bulk samples lead to a false impression that there is an increase in Mo in that portion?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
文本 1
通过对澳大利亚 Mount McRae 页岩的岩石岩心样本进行化学分析，Ariel Anbar 及其同事发现，在大约 25 亿年前的对应地层中，钼（Mo）的含量出现了短暂但显著的增长。在地球上，钼主要通过矿物的氧化风化作用释放出来；因此 Anbar 等人得出结论：大气中的氧气在 25 亿年前曾短暂增加，随后又恢复到之前的极低水平。
文本 2
Sarah Slotznick 及其团队重新检验了 Mount McRae 页岩的岩心样本。由于对整体样本进行化学分析可能会掩盖细节信息，Slotznick 等人还采用了高分辨率显微技术，结果发现大约在 25 亿年前的地层中存在火山碎屑物（已知是钼的载体），并且周围基质中存在微裂缝。研究团队指出，流体可能通过微裂缝进入碎屑物，并在碎屑物沉积后很久才引发氧化风化作用。
答案解析：
两则文本的关键分歧在于：Anbar 等人认为钼含量的增加是当时大气氧增加的证据，而 Slotznick 等人则认为钼的增加是由于后期流体通过微裂缝引发的氧化风化，并非与地层年代同时发生。因此，他们最可能对“钼含量的增加是否代表了同时期大气氧的增加”这一问题存在分歧。选项 B 准确反映了这一争议。

question:
Scholars long thought that the initial spread of silk beyond China occurred in the second century CE, but this view has been ______ by new archaeological evidence from South Asia that reveals that the people of the Indus Civilization made use of silk at least 1,000 years earlier.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
学者们长期以来认为丝绸最初传播到中国以外地区发生在公元二世纪，但这一观点已被南亚新的考古证据______，该证据显示印度河流域文明的人们至少在1000年前就已经使用了丝绸。
答案解析：
新的考古证据显示丝绸的使用时间比之前认为的早了至少1000年，这与原有观点相冲突。因此“contradicted”（反驳，与……矛盾）最符合语境。其他选项“investigated”（调查）、“misinterpreted”（误解）、“anticipated”（预期）均不准确。因此选D。

question:
Many music streaming services also function as social media platforms: by giving users the option to follow friends and share curated playlists or information about their listening history, these platforms allow people to convey their music preferences and listening activities directly to their social networks. In a 2023 study, researcher Michael James Walsh interviewed frequent users of a popular music streaming platform to investigate how its social media dimensions shape their listening habits. Walsh found that these dimensions tended to make study participants feel more mindful of how their listening activities may be perceived, which in turn influenced how they managed those activities.

Which quotation from a music streaming platform user would best illustrate Walsh’s finding?
selections: A. “When I create playlists or choose songs to listen to, I often pick songs that I think the friends who are following me might be interested in listening to, rather than what I might actually prefer listening to in that moment.”
B. “Because the predictions the platform makes about what new songs I might like depend on my past listening habits, at times its recommendations can feel overly repetitive and unvarying.”
C. “The social aspects of music streaming make it really easy to create a sense of a shared listening experience with my friends, even if we aren’t in the same room.”

D. “Listening to music through a streaming platform feels a lot more passive, since I don’t need to make any deliberate choices about what music I’m going to consume, like I do when buying digital downloads or records and CDs.”
explanations:
题目文本翻译：
许多音乐流媒体服务同时也具备社交媒体平台的功能：通过允许用户关注好友、分享精心策划的播放列表或收听历史信息，这些平台让人们能够直接向社交网络传达自己的音乐偏好和收听活动。在2023年的一项研究中，研究员迈克尔·詹姆斯·沃尔什采访了某热门音乐流媒体平台的频繁用户，以探究其社交功能如何影响用户的收听习惯。沃尔什发现，这些功能往往使研究参与者更加在意自己的收听活动会被如何看待，这反过来又影响了他们如何管理这些活动。
答案解析：
沃尔什的发现核心在于：社交功能使用户在意他人如何看待自己的收听活动，并因此调整收听行为。选项A中，用户表示会为了关注自己的朋友而选择歌曲，而非自己当下真正想听的，这正是受到社交审视影响而调整行为的典型例子。因此选A。

question:
Established in 1936 by African American novelist Richard Wright, ______ it would become a vital part of the creative movement known as the Chicago Black Renaissance.
