question:
The following text is from the 1913 story “The King’s Coin” by Emily Pauline Johnson, a Kanienkahagen (Mohawk) writer also known as Tekahionwake. Fox-Foot, a young Ojibwe man, is guiding a group of fur traders who are traveling by canoe and suspects that they are being followed.
At supper time, Fox-Foot would allow no fire to be built, no landing to be made, no trace of their passing to be left. They ate canned meat and marmalade, drank again of the stream and pushed on, until just at dusk they reached the edge of a long, still lake, with shores of granite and dense fir forest.

As used in the text, what does the word “trace” most nearly mean?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择A是最佳答案，因为文本表明Fox-Foot不让团队生火或建立独木舟停靠点，当到了吃晚饭的时候。这个背景表明他不希望任何可能跟踪团队的人看到他们或他们的活动的任何迹象。换句话说，Fox-Foot不希望团队在该地区的活动（“他们的通过”）留下任何痕迹或证据。
B.题目文本解析
以下文本摘自1913年由坎尼卡哈根（莫霍克族）作家Emily Pauline Johnson撰写的故事《国王的硬币》，她也以Tekahionwake的名字闻名。Fox-Foot，一个年轻的奥吉布韦人，正在引导一群乘独木舟旅行的毛皮贸易商，并怀疑他们正在被跟踪。
晚饭时间，Fox-Foot不允许生火，不允许停靠，不允许留下他们经过的任何痕迹。他们吃罐头肉和果酱，再次喝溪水，然后继续前行，直到在黄昏时分到达了一个长长的、宁静的湖边，湖岸是花岗岩和密集的冷杉森林。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
Chile’s Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on Earth. Mary Beth Wilhelm and other astrobiologists search for life, or its remains, in this harsh place because the desert closely mirrors the extreme environment on Mars. The algae and bacteria found in Atacama’s driest regions may offer clues about Martian life. By studying how these and other microorganisms survive such extreme conditions on Earth, Wilhelm’s team hopes to determine whether similar life might have existed on Mars and to develop the best tools to look for evidence of it.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
selections: A. To contrast the conditions in the Atacama Desert with those on Mars
B. To explain why many life-forms cannot survive in the Atacama Desert
C. To indicate why astrobiologists choose to conduct research in the Atacama Desert
D. To describe certain limitations to conducting scientific study in the Atacama Desert
explanations:
A.中文解析
第一句描述了地球上独特的地点——阿塔卡马沙漠。接下来的句子，也就是划线部分，说明了为什么天体生物学家在这个独特的地点研究生命或其遗迹，因为阿塔卡马是一个极端环境，与火星的极端环境非常相似。文本的其余部分解释了研究人员希望他们在阿塔卡马的工作能支持探索火星上的生命。因此，划线部分的主要作用是表明天体生物学家选择在阿塔卡马沙漠进行研究的原因。
B.题目文本解析
智利的阿塔卡马沙漠是地球上最干旱的地方之一。玛丽·贝丝·威廉姆和其他天体生物学家在这个恶劣的地方搜寻生命或其遗迹，因为这个沙漠与火星上的极端环境非常相似。在阿塔卡马最干燥地区发现的藻类和细菌可能提供关于火星生命的线索。通过研究这些以及其他微生物在地球上如何在如此极端条件下生存，威廉姆的团队希望确定类似生命是否可能存在于火星上，并开发最佳工具来寻找其证据。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
The works of Chicana artist Ester Hernandez are now ______ in museums both in the United States and abroad, but the murals she contributed to as a member of Las Mujeres Muralistas early in her artistic career were displayed in outdoor public spaces across San Francisco.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案，因为它在逻辑上最完整地完成了对Ester Hernandez艺术的讨论。在这个语境中，“featured”意味着被显著展示。文本重点介绍了Hernandez的作品曾经并继续被展出的地方，解释说她的早期作品，包括壁画，可以在旧金山的室外空间中观看。文本发展的核心对比是关于她的早期作品可以在哪里观看和她的作品现在可以在哪里观看的，即在美国各地和世界各地的博物馆。因此，这个语境支持Hernandez的作品现在被在全球各地的博物馆中展出或特别展示的想法。
B.题目文本解析
现在，墨西哥裔女艺术家Ester Hernandez的作品如今在美国和国外的博物馆中________，但在她艺术生涯早期作为Las Mujeres Muralistas成员为之贡献的壁画是在旧金山的室外公共空间展出的。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
The Apollo program missions were spaceflights to the moon led by the United States during the 1960s and 1970s during which astronauts collected some samples of the moon’s surface. More recently, China launched the Chang’e 5 mission, which returned additional lunar surface samples. Researchers have analyzed and dated each of the samples, concluding that the lunar samples collected during the Chang’e 5 mission are significant because ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the claim?
selections: A. they are much younger than the samples brought back from any of the Apollo missions.
B. they were collected from the same landing site as the Apollo 11 mission.
C. they are closest in age to the samples brought back by the Apollo 17 mission.
D. they helped confirm the predicted ages of the lunar samples from the Apollo missions.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它有效地使用了表格中的数据来完善关于嫦娥五号月球样本重要性的论断。该表显示了来自四个不同任务的月球样本的大致年龄：三次阿波罗任务和嫦娥五号任务。据称，嫦娥五号样本大约有20亿年的历史，而阿波罗样本每个都被认为有30亿年以上的历史。换句话说，根据表中的数据，嫦娥五号的样本比阿波罗任务的样本要年轻得多。
B.题目文本解析
阿波罗计划是在上世纪60年代和70年代由美国主导的探月航天任务，期间宇航员收集了一些月球表面的样本。更近期，中国发射了嫦娥五号任务，返回了额外的月球表面样本。研究人员对每个样本进行了分析和测年，得出结论说，在嫦娥五号任务期间收集的月球样本具有重要意义，因为______
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
Recently, scientists looked at data collected by NASA’s InSight lander to learn more about seismic activity on Mars, known as marsquakes. The data show that the marsquakes all started from the same location on the planet. This discovery was surprising to scientists, as they expected that the marsquakes would originate from all over the planet because of the cooling of the planet’s surface. Now, scientists believe that there could be areas of active magma flows deep beneath the planet’s surface that trigger the marsquakes.

According to the text, what was surprising to scientists studying the seismic activity data from NASA’s InSight lander?
selections: A. The surface temperature of Mars has been rising.
B. There were different types of seismic waves causing marsquakes.
C. NASA’s InSight lander collected less data than scientists had expecte
D. All the marsquakes started from the same location on the planet.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择D是最佳答案，因为它提供了一个关于科学家感到惊讶的声明，并且这一声明得到了文本的支持。文本中提到，来自NASA“洞察号”着陆器的数据描述了火星上相同地点发生的地震。文本继续说，因为他们预期相反的情况（即火星地震将来自整个行星），这一发现让科学家感到惊讶。
B.题目文本解析
最近，科学家们查看了NASA“洞察号”着陆器收集的数据，以了解火星上的地震活动，即火星地震。数据显示，所有的火星地震都起源于该行星上的同一地点。这一发现让科学家感到惊讶，因为他们原本预期火星地震会由于行星表面的冷却而发生于整个行星的各个地方。现在，科学家们认为，在行星表面下深处可能存在活动的岩浆流区域，这些区域会触发火星地震。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
The Younger Dryas was a period of extreme cooling from 11,700 to 12,900 years ago in the Northern Hemisphere. Some scientists argue that a comet fragment hitting Earth brought about the cooling. Others disagree, partly because there is no known crater from such an impact that dates to the beginning of the period. In 2015, a team led by Kurt Kjær detected a 19-mile-wide crater beneath a glacier in Greenland. The scientists who believe an impact caused the Younger Dryas claim that this discovery supports their view. However, Kjær’s team hasn’t yet been able to determine the age of the crater. Therefore, the team suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. it can’t be concluded that the impact that made the crater was connected to the beginning of the Younger Dryas.
B. it can’t be determined whether a comet fragment could make a crater as large as 19 miles wide.
C. scientists have ignored the possibility that something other than a comet fragment could have made the crater.
D. the scientists who believe an impact caused the Younger Dryas have made incorrect assumptions about when the period began.
explanations:
A.中文解析
根据文本，一些科学家相信一颗彗星碎片撞击地球导致了“幼发期”冷却时期的到来。文本随后指出，一队科学家在格陵兰发现了一个撞击坑，有人认为这支持了彗星碎片撞击地球引发“幼发期”的理论。然而，文本还指出该团队无法确定撞击坑的年龄。如果无法确定撞击坑的年龄，那么它与“幼发期”时段的联系也不能得到确认。因此，不能得出使得坑形成的撞击与“幼发期”的开始有关的结论。
B.题目文本解析
幼发期是在北半球发生的在约11,700至12,900年前的极端冷却时期。一些科学家认为，一颗彗星碎片撞击地球导致了这种冷却。其他人则持不同意见，部分原因是因为没有已知的撞击坑可以追溯到该时期的开始。2015年，由库尔特·凯尔（Kurt Kjær）领导的一个团队在格陵兰的一片冰川下方探测到了一个直径19英里的撞击坑。认为撞击引起了幼发期的科学家声称这一发现支持了他们的观点。然而，凯尔的团队尚未能够确定该撞击坑的年龄。因此，该团队提出______
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
In 1935 Hallie Flanagan was chosen to lead the Federal Theatre Project (FTP). This project was part of the new Works Progress Administration (WPA), a program created by President Franklin D. Roosevelt to provide jobs for unemployed people during the Great Depression. As the director of the FTP, Flanagan created jobs for over 12,500 performers, designers, and other theater professionals across the country. She also kept ticket prices low for the shows they staged, which meant that many people could afford to experience theater for the first time.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
selections: A. Jobs provided by the FTP were intended mainly for performers, designers, and other theater professionals.
B. President Roosevelt created the WPA to provide jobs for unemployed people.
C. During the Great Depression, many people couldn’t afford to buy theater tickets.
D. As the director of the FTP, Flanagan succeeded in creating many jobs and introducing people to theater.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择D是最佳答案，因为它最准确地陈述了文本的主旨。文本开始陈述，弗拉纳根在1935年被选为联邦戏剧项目（FTP）的负责人，该项目是由总统富兰克林·罗斯福创建的计划的一部分。接着文本解释说，作为FTP的负责人，弗拉纳根为超过12,500名戏剧专业人员创造了工作，并确保票价保持低廉，以便许多人能够承担首次体验戏剧。因此，文本的主旨是作为FTP的负责人，弗拉纳根成功地创造了许多工作，并让人们接触到戏剧。
B.题目文本解析
1935年，哈莉·弗拉纳根被选为领导联邦戏剧项目（FTP）的人选。该项目是新成立的工程进展管理局（WPA）的一部分，这是由总统富兰克林·罗斯福创建的旨在在大萧条期间为失业人员提供工作的计划。作为FTP的负责人，弗拉纳根为全国范围内的超过12,500名表演者、设计师和其他戏剧专业人员创造了工作。她还保持了他们演出的票价低廉，这意味着许多人能够承担首次体验戏剧。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
A student is using the table as part of a social studies class presentation on the US auto industry in the early twentieth century. The student notes that, according to the table, from 1910 to 1925 ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
selections: A. the number of cars produced increased but the number of companies producing cars decrease
B. both the number of cars produced and the number of companies producing cars remained unchange
C. the number of cars produced decreased but the number of companies producing cars remained unchange
D. both the number of cars produced and the number of companies producing cars increase
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它最有效地利用了表格中的数据来完成关于二十世纪初美国汽车工业的陈述。该表显示了1910年至1925年间每五年汽车产量和生产汽车公司数量的数据。根据表格，从一个时间段到下一个时间段，汽车产量持续增加，从1910年的123,990辆汽车增加到1925年的3,185,881辆汽车。同时，表格显示，生产汽车的公司数量持续减少，从1910年的320家公司减少到1925年的80家公司。因此，表格显示，从1910年到1925年，汽车产量增加了，而生产汽车的公司数量减少了。
B.题目文本解析
一名学生正在利用这张表格作为社会研究课程中关于二十世纪初美国汽车工业的演示的一部分。该学生指出，根据表格显示，从1910年到1925年______。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
“The Bet” is an 1889 short story by Anton Chekhov. In the story, a banker is described as being very upset about something: ______

Which quotation from “The Bet” most effectively illustrates the claim?
selections: A. “Then the banker cautiously broke the seals off the door and put the key in the keyhole.”
B. “It struck three o’clock, the banker listened; everyone was asleep in the house and nothing could be heard outside but the rustling of the chilled trees.”
C. “The banker, spoilt and frivolous, with millions beyond his reckoning, was delighted at the bet.”
D. “When [the banker] got home he lay on his bed, but his tears and emotion kept him for hours from sleeping.”
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项D是最佳答案，因为它最有效地使用了《赌注》中的引用来说明这样一个观点，即银行家对某事感到非常沮丧。引文表明银行家流下了眼泪，这表明他很可能对某事感到不快，并且他的情绪如此强烈，以至于让他连续几个小时无法入睡。这些细节表明银行家非常沮丧。
B.题目文本解析
《赌注》是安东·契诃夫于1889年创作的短篇小说。在这个故事中，一个银行家被描述为对某件事感到非常沮丧：______
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
Eighteenth-century historian Edward Gibbon thought the only character defect of the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius was his mild temperament—though the emperor was widely considered virtuous, his overly permissive nature led him to ______ the vices of those who surrounded him.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择A是最佳答案，因为它在逻辑上最完整地完成了对罗马皇帝马库斯·奥勒留斯的讨论。在这个语境中，“indulge”意味着过度宽容。文本指出，根据历史学家爱德华·吉本的说法，广为人知的品德高尚的马库斯·奥勒留斯只有一个缺点：他的温和性格。
B.题目文本解析
十八世纪历史学家爱德华·吉本认为罗马皇帝马库斯·奥勒留唯一的性格缺陷是他的温和脾气——尽管这位皇帝被广泛认为是有品德的，但他过于宽容的天性导致他对周围人的恶习过于纵容，容忍而非惩罚那些恶习。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
The following text is adapted from Ann Petry’s 1946 novel The Street. Lutie lives in an apartment in Harlem, New York.
The glow from the sunset was making the street radiant. The street is nice in this light, [Lutie] thought. It was swarming with children who were playing ball and darting back and forth across the sidewalk in complicated games of tag. Girls were skipping double dutch rope, going tirelessly through the exact center of a pair of ropes, jumping first on one foot and then the other.
©1946 by Ann Petry

Which choice best describes what is happening in the text?
selections: A. Lutie is observing the appearance of the street at a particular time of day and the events occurring on it.
B. Lutie is annoyed by the noise of children playing games on her street.
C. Lutie is puzzled by the rules of certain children’s games.
D. Lutie is spending time alone in her apartment because she doesn’t want to interact with her neighbors.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择A是最佳答案，因为它最准确地陈述了文本中发生的事情。叙述者指出Lutie认为街道在日落的光线下看起来很漂亮。叙述者接着描述了Lutie在街上看到的情景：孩子们在玩球或玩捉迷藏，女孩们在跳绳。因此，文本中发生的事情是Lutie正在观察一天中特定时间的街道外观以及上面发生的事件。
B.题目文本解析
以下文本摘自安·佩特里于1946年创作的小说《The Street》。Lutie住在纽约哈莱姆的一间公寓里。
日落的余晖使街道光芒四射。在这种光线下，[Lutie]想道，街道看起来很漂亮。街上挤满了玩球的孩子，他们在人行道上来回穿梭，玩着复杂的捉迷藏游戏。女孩们在跳双人跳绳，不知疲倦地在一对绳子的中心跳，先用一只脚跳，然后再用另一只脚跳。
©1946年安·佩特里。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
Animal researcher Amalia P.M. Bastos led a 2021 study about a wild kea parrot that used small stones as tools to preen its feathers. Skeptical colleagues had initially suggested to Bastos that the kea’s interactions with the stones might simply be ______, but Bastos and her team showed that the kea was using the stones deliberately.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案，因为它在逻辑上最完整地完成了对Bastos对野生凯亚鹦鹉研究的讨论。在这个语境中，“accidental”意味着没有计划或意外的。文本首先描述了Bastos的研究，该研究涉及观察到一只凯亚鹦鹉使用小石头来梳理羽毛。文本随后提到了对Bastos的发现持怀疑态度的同事们，最后描述了Bastos及其团队如何应对那些同事的怀疑。鉴于文本中提到的同事们对Bastos的发现表示怀疑，最佳答案必须是以一种方式完成文本，使得持怀疑态度的人对凯亚鹦鹉使用石头的看法与Bastos及其团队的看法不一致。由于Bastos及其团队表明凯亚鹦鹉使用石头是有意识的，因此在这个语境中，持怀疑态度的人的看法必须是凯亚鹦鹉使用石头是无意识的或偶然的。
B.题目文本解析
动物研究员Amalia P.M. Bastos在2021年领导了一项关于一只野生凯亚鹦鹉使用小石头作为工具梳理羽毛的研究。最初持怀疑态度的同事向Bastos建议，凯亚鹦鹉与石头的互动可能只是________，但Bastos和她的团队证明了凯亚鹦鹉是有意识地使用这些石头的。

question:
How did whales, once no bigger than seals, evolve to become the largest animals on Earth? Brazilian biologist Mariana Nery believes the answer might be found in whales’ DNA. In January 2023, Nery and her colleagues ______ a study showing changes over time in four whale genes associated with body size.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 连贯表达。句子中Nery and her colleagues是主语，空格处为谓语动词，因此选项B、C、D错误，为非谓语动词，选项A正确。

question:
Under normal atmospheric pressure at Earth’s surface, water molecules form a tetrahedral network stabilized by hydrogen bonds between adjacent molecules. Extreme high pressure, such as can be found in deep ocean waters, destabilizes these bonds and compresses water’s structure, allowing water molecules within organisms to permeate proteins and impede crucial biological functions; yet deep-sea organisms known as piezophiles have adapted to extreme pressure. Studies have found a positive correlation between the depths that various piezophiles inhabit and concentrations of a compound called trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) in their muscle tissues, which has led a team of researchers to hypothesize that TMAO reduces water’s compressibility.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers’ hypothesis?
selections: A. Water molecules are found to be impervious to TMAO even when the water molecules’ tetrahedral configuration has been distorted by high pressure.
B. Examination of TMAO’s molecular structure shows that TMAO molecules retain their shape even as pressure increases.
C. A positive correlation is found between concentrations of TMAO and the rate at which water’s molecular structure compresses as pressure increases.
D. Analysis of water’s molecular structure under high pressure reveals that hydrogen bonds are more stable when TMAO is present than when it is not.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项 D 是最佳答案，因为它提出了一个发现，如果属实，将支持研究人员的假设，即 TMAO 可减少水的可压缩性。文本解释说，在海洋深处，极端压力通过破坏相邻分子之间的氢键，从而压缩水的分子结构，使水能够渗透蛋白质并伤害相关生物。然而，被称为高压菌的深海生物已经适应在这些深度生存，先前的研究显示高压菌物种生存深度与化合物 TMAO 水平之间存在正相关。由于这一假设将 TMAO 水平与水的四面体分子结构的可压缩性降低联系起来，一个发现 TMAO 有助于在高压下保持水分子之间的氢键将强烈支持这一假设。
B.题目文本解析
在地球表面的正常大气压下，水分子形成由相邻分子之间的氢键稳定的四面体网络。极端高压，例如在深海水域中可以找到的高压，会破坏这些键并压缩水的结构，使水分子能够渗透生物体内的蛋白质并阻碍重要的生物功能；然而被称为高压菌的深海生物已经适应了极端压力。研究发现，各种高压菌栖息的深度与它们肌肉组织中的一种叫做三甲胺 N-氧化物（TMAO）的化合物浓度之间存在正相关，这导致一组研究人员假设 TMAO 可减少水的可压缩性。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
In Koasati, an Indigenous language from what is now the southeastern United States, misip-lin is the singular form of “to wink,” whereas mis-lin is the plural form of “to wink”; similarly, lataf-kan is the singular form of “to kick something,” whereas the plural form is lat-kan. These are instances of subtractive morphology, in which a base word is truncated—removing the ip and af, in these cases—to form a new, related word. This kind of subtractive morphology is pervasive in Koasati.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
selections: A. It describes the relationship between Koasati and several other languages, raises a question about the nature of that relationship, and then answers that question.

B. It identifies the most frequently occurring words in Koasati, explains why it is difficult to translate those words into English, then provides examples of languages other than English into which those words can be translate
C. It presents some specific words in Koasati, describes the general linguistic phenomenon exemplified by those words, then states that this phenomenon occurs frequently in Koasati.

D. It explains the phenomenon of subtractive morphology, discusses why subtractive morphology has been controversial among scholars, then argues that an analysis of Koasati could help resolve that controversy.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最好的答案，因为它最准确地描述了文本的整体结构。文本首先提供了科阿萨蒂语中一些单词（misip-lin、mis-lin、lataf-kan、lat-kan）及其英文翻译的例子。然后，文本解释了这些单词是一种称为减法形态学的语言现象的例子。最后，文本断言文本中所示减法形态学在科阿萨蒂语中是“普遍的”或常见的。因此，文本首先呈现了科阿萨蒂语中的一些具体单词，描述了这些单词所体现的一般语言现象，然后陈述了这种现象在科阿萨蒂语中经常出现。
B.题目文本解析
在科阿萨蒂语中，一种源自当前美国东南部地区的土著语言，misip-lin是“眨眼”的单数形式，而mis-lin是“眨眼”的复数形式；类似地，lataf-kan是“踢某物”的单数形式，而复数形式是lat-kan。这些都是减法形态学的例子，其中基础词被截断——在这些情况下移除了ip和af——形成一个新的，相关的词。这种减法形态学在科阿萨蒂语中是普遍存在的。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
When they were first introduced to western Europe from Byzantium in the eleventh century, table forks were met with much resistance. The Bishop of Ostia, St. Peter Damian, condemned the eating utensils because he considered ______ dangerous and unnecessary luxury items.

question:
What makes the theremin a unique musical instrument? You play it without touching it. When you place your ______ the pitch will shift as your hands move through the air.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
selections: A. hand’s between the two antenna’s,
B. hands between the two antennas,
C. hands’ between the two antennas’,
D. hands’ between the two antennas,
explanations: 所有格。hands后没有修饰它的名词等成分，因此hands后不需要加所有格，因此选项A、C、D错误。又因为这句话是when引导的时间状语从句及其主语，the pitch应该为主句的主语，因此antennas不需要用所有格形式。选项B正确。

question:
In 2014, Nestor Gomez won his first-ever storytelling competition, relating a tale about his life as a Guatemalan immigrant living in Chicago. ______ in 2017, Gomez created the show 80 Minutes Around the World as a platform for others to share stories about their immigration experiences.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案。"后来"在逻辑上表明，这个句子中关于2017年戈麦斯创立了一个平台，让他人分享他们的移民经历的信息，发生在比之前关于戈麦斯在2014年赢得他的第一个讲故事比赛的信息更晚的事件序列中。
B.题目文本解析
2014年，内斯托·戈麦斯赢得了自己的首次讲故事比赛，讲述了他作为一名住在芝加哥的危地马拉移民的生活故事。 然后，2017年，戈麦斯创建了节目《环游世界80分钟》，作为让他人分享他们的移民经历故事的平台。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
In most deer species, males grow antlers, and females don’t. ______ reindeer are different. They are the only deer species in which the females grow antlers, too.

explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案。"然而"在逻辑上表明，关于这个句子中驯鹿的说法与前一个句子中大多数鹿种类的信息形成对比。
B.题目文本解析
在大多数鹿种中，雄性长角，雌性不长。 然而，驯鹿不同。 它们是唯一一种雌性也会长角的鹿种。

question:
The French directors Colas Koola and Vivien Mermet-Guyenet (known as Koola and Viv) founded the video game studio BlueTwelve. question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●In 1965, Yale University historians claimed that a world map called the Vinland Map was drawn in the fifteenth century.
●Since that time, the map’s age has been the subject of debate.
●In 2021, researchers conducted a study to analyze the elemental composition of the map’s ink.
●Their analysis revealed that the ink contains a titanium compound not used in inks until the 1920s.
●The researchers concluded that the map was drawn in the twentieth century.

The student wants to present the study and its findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Given the debate about the Vinland Map’s age, researchers in 2021 conducted a study to analyze the elemental composition of the map’s ink.
B. A 2021 study of the Vinland Map’s ink revealed that it contains a titanium compound not used in inks until the 1920s, indicating that the map was drawn in the twentieth century.
C. The Vinland Map, believed by some to have been drawn in the fifteenth century, was the focus of a 2021 study.
D. Aware that a certain titanium compound was not used in inks until the 1920s, researchers in 2021 studied the elemental composition of the Vinland Map’s ink.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择B是最佳答案。这个句子有效地介绍了这项研究及其发现，提供了相关信息：对文兰德地图的一项2021年的研究发现，地图上的墨水含有一种直到20世纪才使用的化合物。
B.题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生记录了以下内容：
- 1965年，耶鲁大学历史学家声称一幅名为文兰德地图的世界地图是在15世纪绘制的。
- 自那时以来，这幅地图的年代一直是争论的焦点。
- 2021年，研究人员进行了一项研究，分析了地图墨水的元素组成。
- 他们的分析显示，这种墨水含有一种直到20世纪20年代才被使用的钛化合物。
- 研究人员得出结论，这幅地图是在20世纪绘制的。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●Traditionally, manufacturers have dyed denim jeans blue by dipping them in a solution containing indigo powder.
●Indigo doesn’t dissolve in just water, so manufacturers must mix hazardous chemicals with water to dissolve the powder.
●Textile researcher Smriti Rai discovered a process for dyeing blue jeans without chemicals.
●Rai added indigo powder to a hydrogel containing nanocellulose and produced a dye that could be spread directly onto the denim.
●Nanocellulose is a natural, plant-based substance that separates the molecules of indigo powder.

The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two approaches to dyeing blue jeans. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Though created using a different process, Rai’s dye contains the same ingredient as the dye produced by blue jean manufacturers.
B. Nanocellulose is a natural, plant-based substance that separates the molecules of indigo powder, which doesn’t dissolve in water.
C. The traditional approach to dyeing blue jeans is to dip them in a solution containing hazardous chemicals.
D. Rai’s approach substitutes a natural, plant-based substance for the hazardous chemicals that manufacturers have traditionally use
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择D是最佳答案。这个句子强调了染蓝牛仔裤的两种方法之间的区别，指出Rai的方法使用天然植物为基础的物质代替有害化学品。
B.题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生记录了以下内容：
- 传统上，制造商通过将牛仔裤浸泡在含靛蓝粉末的溶液中来将牛仔裤染成蓝色。
- 靛蓝不会仅仅在水中溶解，因此制造商必须将有害化学品与水混合以溶解粉末。
- 纺织研究员施米蒂·莱发现了一种无需化学品染蓝牛仔裤的过程。
- 莱将靛蓝粉末加入含有纳米纤维素的水凝胶中，并制造出一种可以直接涂抹在牛仔布上的染料。
- 纳米纤维素是一种天然的、以植物为基础的物质，它可以分离靛蓝粉末的分子。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
While light is known as one of the fastest-moving substances, it slows down when passing through some types of matter. One such type of matter is a form of cooled, condensed gas called a Bose-Einstein condensate ______ Dutch physicist Lene Hau famously used a BEC to slow a beam of light to a complete halt.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 用标点符号连接句子。首先空格处前是完整的一句话，谓语为is，空格处后也是完整的一句话，谓语为used。可以连接两个完整句子的标点符号有句号、分号、冒号、破折号，或者逗号/破折号加并列连词。选项C正确。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
Historians agree that the jazz pianist Jelly Roll Morton was exaggerating when he claimed to have invented jazz music. No one can deny, ______ that Morton’s innovative compositions and remarkable improvisational skills helped shape jazz as a genre during its early years.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项 D 是最佳答案。"Though" 逻辑上表明，该句中的论断——即莫顿的即兴技能在爵士乐早期塑造了这一流派（"没有人能否认"这一点）——是真实的，尽管之前提到莫顿夸大地声称自己发明了爵士乐。
B.题目文本解析
历史学家们一致认为，爵士钢琴家 Jelly Roll Morton 在声称自己发明了爵士音乐时夸大其词。然而，没有人能否认，莫顿创新的作品和出色的即兴技能在爵士乐早期的发展过程中塑造了这一流派。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
In 1929, Edwin Herbert Land invented a polarizing filter that was featured in a number of products, from sunglasses to 3D movies. A decade later, Land ______ his technology to invent the world’s first instant camera, the Polaroid Land camera.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 连贯表达。句子中Land是主语，空格处为谓语动词，因此选项B、C、D错误，为非谓语动词，选项A正确。
exam_name: Bluebook Practice 6 阅读语法（Easy Module）

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●Leigh Torres is a marine ecologist.
●She conducted a study of blue whales in New Zealand’s South Taranaki Bight region.
●She wanted to know how ocean temperature affects where the whales forage for krill in that region.
●She found that during a marine heat wave, the whales foraged farther offshore than they had during cooler periods.
●The offshore waters, which were colder than areas closer to shore, had a higher relative abundance of krill.

The student wants to emphasize the aim of the research study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Analyzing ocean temperature data, Torres found that during a marine heat wave, blue whales foraged farther offshore than they had during cooler periods.
B. In her study, Torres sought to determine how ocean temperature affects where blue whales forage for krill in the South Taranaki Bight region.
C. Torres’s study revealed that blue whales were attracted to offshore waters with a relatively high abundance of krill.
D. Torres, a marine ecologist, studied blue whales in the South Taranaki Bight region, where the whales forage.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择B是最佳答案。这个句子强调了研究的目的或目标，指出托雷斯试图确定海洋温度如何影响蓝鲸在哪里觅食磷虾。
B.题目文本解析
在研究一个主题时，一名学生记录了以下内容：
- 莱·托雷斯是一位海洋生态学家。
- 她进行了一项关于新西兰南塔拉纳基湾地区蓝鲸的研究。
- 她想知道海洋温度如何影响这个地区蓝鲸寻找磷虾的地点。
- 她发现在一次海洋热浪期间，蓝鲸在寻找磷虾时比在较冷的时期更远离海岸。
- 远离海岸的海域比靠近海岸的地区更冷，磷虾的相对丰度更高。

question:
Taking photographs in the mid-1800s was complicated and expensive, but this changed with the 1854 invention of the carte de visite, a small photo that cost little to make. Carte de visite photos helped to ______ photography: they made it easy and enjoyable for everyday people to have their pictures taken, and people at the time loved exchanging these small photos with friends and family.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案，因为它最合乎逻辑地完成了文本对“名片式照片”的讨论。“普及”一项技术意味着让它被广泛使用和欣赏。文本解释说，与早期的摄影技术所生产的照片不同，“名片式照片”价格便宜，普通人也能轻松获得，并乐于交换这些图像。因此，“名片式照片”有助于普及摄影。
B.题目文本翻译
在19世纪中叶，拍照既复杂又昂贵，但随着1854年“名片式照片”的发明，这一切发生了变化。名片式照片是一种制作成本低的小照片。名片式照片帮助______摄影：它让普通人轻松愉快地拍照，人们在那个时候喜欢与朋友和家人交换这些小照片。

question:
On the basis of extensive calculations and models, astronomers in the 1990s predicted that the collision of two neutron stars or a neutron star and a black hole could release a massive burst of gamma rays in an event called a kilonova. This ______ was confirmed with observations in 2017.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它最合理地完成了文本对关于千新星的预测的讨论。在这个上下文中，“理论”是指被认为在科学上可接受的解释。文本提到，天文学家在1990年代预测，黑洞与中子星之间的碰撞或两个中子星之间的碰撞可能会释放出一种被称为千新星的大规模伽马射线爆发，并解释说他们是基于对现有数据和模拟（“计算和模型”）的广泛研究来确定这种可能性的。换句话说，这一预测是一种理论——一种有充分支持的解释——正如文本所示，这一理论在2017年通过观测得到了确认。
B.题目文本翻译
根据广泛的计算和模型，1990年代的天文学家预测，两颗中子星或一颗中子星与一颗黑洞的碰撞可能会在一种被称为千新星的事件中释放出巨大的 gamma 射线爆发。这一______空白在 2017 年的观测中得到了确认。

question:
The majority of plastics today wind up in landfills or are, at best, recycled into materials that have a very limited range of applications. To address this problem, chemist Guoliang Liu and colleagues designed a reactor that melts polyethylene and polypropylene—two widely used plastics—into a wax. The wax can then be transformed into a surfactant (a chemical compound usable as a detergent). With this promising new method, plastic waste could be turned into a range of useful cleaning products.

Which choice best states the function of the underlined portion of the text?
selections: A. It clarifies the meaning of a scientific term.
B. It describes an environmental concern.
C. It explains the significance of a scientific discovery.
D. It identifies a result that confused the team.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它最准确地描述了下划线短语在整篇文本中的功能。文本指出，刘和同事的反应器生产的蜡可以转化为表面活性剂。下划线短语用括号括起来，随后提供了“表面活性剂”这一术语的定义，解释它是一种可以用作洗涤剂的化学化合物。因此，文本中的下划线部分的功能是澄清一个科学术语的含义。
B.题目文本翻译
如今，大多数塑料最终被送入垃圾填埋场，或者充其量被回收成应用范围非常有限的材料。为了解决这个问题，化学家刘国亮及其同事设计了一种反应器，可以将聚乙烯和聚丙烯——这两种广泛使用的塑料——熔化成蜡。然后，这种蜡可以转化为表面活性剂（可用作洗涤剂的化学化合物）。通过这种有前景的新方法，塑料废料可以转变为一系列有用的清洁产品。

question:
In 2023 literary scholar Jeremy Douglass cautioned technology investors and enthusiasts who predict conventional books’ ultimate displacement by newer forms of media. Douglass observed that the concept of an “interactive” text is much older than technologists assume, extending back to the first time readers scratched notes into a text’s margins. In addition, newer media, such as video games, haven’t replaced older forms of entertainment, such as comic books, but rather exist alongside them. Douglass believes that rather than supplanting books, technology is simply making new forms of expression possible.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
selections: A. It challenges the stance of the investors and enthusiasts who are mentioned earlier in the text.
B. It explains the basis for the claim made by the technologists mentioned in the text.
C. It suggests that academics are better suited than investors to see the potential uses of contemporary interactive texts.
D. It provides a historical anecdote about the technological challenges involved in reading the earliest interactive texts.
explanations:
A.中文翻译
选择A是最佳答案，因为它最准确地描述了划线部分在整体文本中的功能。文本的第一句引入了文学学者杰里米·道格拉斯对技术投资者和爱好者的警告，警告他们不要预测新媒体形式会取代传统书籍。接下来的句子，即部分划线的内容，提出了道格拉斯的观察：互动文本并不是什么新鲜事；它们的出现比技术专家假设的要早，最早可以追溯到读者第一次在书籍的边缘写下笔记时。因此，划线部分的功能是挑战文本中提到的技术投资者和爱好者的立场。正如文本的其余部分所指出的那样，新媒体并不一定会取代旧媒体，而是如道格拉斯所相信的那样，导致新的表达形式的出现。
B.题目文本翻译
在2023年，文学学者杰里米·道格拉斯警告那些预测传统书籍最终会被新媒体形式取代的科技投资者和爱好者。道格拉斯观察到，“互动”文本的概念远比技术人员所认为的要古老，早在读者第一次在文本的边缘写下笔记时就已存在。此外，视频游戏等新媒体并没有取代漫画书等旧娱乐形式，而是与之并存。道格拉斯认为，科技并不是在取代书籍，而是使新的表达形式成为可能。

question:
In the 1990s, conservationists began planting more than 500,000 native trees in the habitat of the Azores bullfinch to boost the bird’s numbers. This approach was apparently ______: the Azores bullfinch’s population size increased from as few as 100 birds at the end of the 1980s to around 1,300 in 2023.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项C是最佳答案，因为它最合理地完成了文本对保护主义者增加亚速尔朱雀数量努力的讨论。在这个语境中，“成功”意味着实现一个目标或目的。根据文本，保护主义者在亚速尔朱雀的栖息地种植了超过50万棵本土树木，以提高这种鸟的种群数量。文本随后指出，种植树木的确导致了种群数量的增长。因此，在这个语境中，保护主义者通过种植本土树木所采取的方法是成功的，因为它达到了增加鸟类种群数量的目标。
B.题目文本翻译
在1990年代，保护主义者开始在亚速尔朱雀的栖息地植植超过50万棵本地树木，以增加这种鸟的数量。这种方法显然是______：亚速尔朱雀的种群数量从1980年代末的不足100只增加到2023年的约1300只。

question:
Hevea brasiliensis, a tree in the Amazon rainforest, is the world’s main source of natural rubber. The tree produces a milky substance called latex that is used to make rubber. The bark of Hevea brasiliensis is helpful for the process of making rubber because it has a unique structure that makes it easy to collect latex. A network of tubes in the tree’s inner bark helps the latex to flow out easily when people make small cuts into the bark.

What feature of Hevea brasiliensis does the text say is helpful for the process of making rubber?
selections: A. Its latex produces rubber of an especially high quality.
B. Its bark has a unique structure that makes it easy to collect latex.
C. It is able to grow in a wide variety of climates around the world.
D. It is one of only two trees in the Amazon that produce latex.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项B是最佳答案，因为它最准确地说明了巴西橡胶树（Hevea brasiliensis）在制作橡胶过程中的有用特征。根据文本，这种树种会产生乳胶，而乳胶用于制作橡胶，并且它的内树皮中包含一个“管道网络”，当被切割时，能够使乳胶流出。文本明确指出，巴西橡胶树的这一特征对制作橡胶的过程是“有帮助的”。
B.题目文本翻译
巴西橡胶树（Hevea brasiliensis）是亚马逊雨林中的一种树木，也是世界上主要的天然橡胶来源。这棵树会产生一种称为乳胶的乳白色物质，用于制造橡胶。巴西橡胶树的树皮在橡胶制作过程中非常有用，因为它具有独特的结构，便于收集乳胶。树内皮中的一系列管道有助于乳胶在对树皮进行小切割时顺利流出。

question:
Painter Alma W. Thomas was fascinated by the colors and shapes found in nature. The flowers and trees in the garden at her home in Washington, DC, ______ her work. For example, Thomas’s use of broken brushstrokes was inspired by the way that light would shine through the leaves of a tree in front of her house.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择 D 是最佳答案，因为它最合理地补充了文本对画家阿尔玛·W·托马斯作品的讨论。在这个语境中，“影响”意味着对某事的发展产生了作用。文本指出，托马斯的作品与她家园中的花草树木之间存在联系，举例说明托马斯的笔触受到她家前面树叶间透过的光线的启发。这一背景传达了托马斯的作品受到花草树木的影响。
B.题目文本翻译
画家阿尔玛·W·托马斯对自然界中的色彩和形状充满了 fascination。她位于华盛顿特区的家中的花园里的花草树木，______ 了她的作品。例如，托马斯运用破碎的笔触，受到了光线透过她家前面树叶的方式的启发。

question:
One of the earliest known maps is a Babylonian clay tablet thought to be almost 4,500 years old. The map ______ the area of a plot of land, shows a river valley, and includes the cardinal directions.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项A是最佳答案。所测试的规范是句子中动词形式的使用。单数动词“describes”与单数主语“map”在数上保持一致。

question:
Archaeologists studying the ancient city of Pompeii in Italy recently discovered a well-preserved food shop known as a thermopolium. The site contains food remains, artworks, and decorations. These items give researchers a better understanding of what daily life in Pompeii may have been like. For example, the archaeologists found a ceramic jar that they believe likely contained a meat and seafood stew.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
selections: A. To compare ancient artworks with modern ones
B. To discuss the political system of Italy
C. To present a recent archaeological discovery
D. To describe a region’s climate
explanations:
A.中文翻译
选项C是最佳答案，因为它最准确地描述了文本的主要目的。文本指出，考古学家最近在意大利庞贝发现了一家保存完好的食品商店，或称热食店。接着，文本进一步描述了这一发现的内容，并提供了所发现物品的例子。因此，文本的总体目的是介绍最近的考古发现。
B.题目文本翻译
考古学家在意大利古城庞贝的研究中，最近发现了一家保存完好的食品商店，称为“热食店”（thermopolium）。该遗址包含食品残留物、艺术品和装饰品。这些物品使研究人员更好地理解庞贝的日常生活可能是什么样的。例如，考古学家发现了一个陶瓷罐，他们认为这个罐子很可能装有肉类和海鲜炖菜。

question:
Researcher Judith Hilton and her team interviewed 55 people about which factors would make them switch from using single-use plastic containers to reusable containers. The graph shows three of the factors mentioned in the interviews and the percentage of participants who mentioned them.

According to the graph, about what percentage of participants mentioned costs in the interviews?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择D是最佳答案，因为它指出了在Judith Hilton及其团队进行的访谈中提到成本的参与者的百分比。文本提到，Hilton及其团队采访了参与者，讨论了促使他们从一次性塑料容器转向可重复使用容器的因素。图表呈现了访谈中提到的三个因素（便利性、成本和既定行为）以及提到每个因素的参与者百分比。图表显示约50%的参与者将成本作为一个因素提到。
B.题目文本翻译
研究人员朱迪斯·希尔顿及其团队对55人进行了采访，了解哪些因素会使他们从使用一次性塑料容器转向可重复使用的容器。图表展示了访谈中提到的三个因素以及提到这些因素的参与者的百分比。

question:
Treasure Island is an 1883 novel by Robert Louis Stevenson. When the narrator was a child, his father ran a hotel. A mysterious sailor came to stay at the hotel. The narrator was frightened of the sailor, as can be seen when the narrator says, ______

Which quotation from Treasure Island most effectively illustrates the claim?
selections: A. “I remember [the sailor] as if it were yesterday, as he came plodding to the inn door, his sea-chest following behind him in a hand-barrow.”
B. “[The sailor] was a very silent man by custom. All day he hung round the cove or upon the cliffs with a brass telescope.”

C. “All the time he lived with us [the sailor] made no change whatever in his dress but to buy some stockings from a hawker. One of the [corners] of his hat having fallen down, he let it hang from that day forth, though it was a great annoyance when it blew.”

D. “How [the sailor] haunted my dreams, I need scarcely tell you. On stormy nights, when the wind shook the four corners of the house and the surf roared along the cove and up the cliffs, I would see him in a thousand forms, and with a thousand diabolical expressions.”
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项 D 是最佳答案，因为它最有效地说明了叙述者对水手感到恐惧的说法。引用的内容描述了水手在叙述者的梦中徘徊，呈现出“千种形态”和“千种恶魔般的表情”。这种生动的意象传达了叙述者在思考水手时所经历的强烈心理恐惧。此外，引用通过描绘风摇动房屋和咆哮的海浪的暴风夜景，唤起了叙述者的恐惧和 dread。
B.题目文本翻译
《金银岛》是罗伯特·路易斯·史蒂文森于1883年出版的一部小说。当叙述者还是个孩子时，他的父亲经营着一家酒店。一位神秘的水手来到酒店住宿。叙述者对这位水手感到害怕，这可以从叙述者所说的内容中看出，______。

question:
In terms of area and population, the three smallest Arabian Peninsula countries are Bahrain, Qatar, and Kuwait.

According to the table, what is the total area of Bahrain?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项 C 是最佳答案，因为它表明了表中所示的巴林的总面积。该表列出了巴林、卡塔尔和科威特的总面积（以平方英里为单位）和人口，并指出巴林的总面积为 304 平方英里。
B.题目文本翻译
在面积和人口方面，阿拉伯半岛三个最小的国家是巴林、卡塔尔和科威特。

question:
“The Mountain” is a 1914 poem by Robert Frost. In the poem, the speaker visits a town next to a mountain. The speaker claims to feel protected by the mountain, saying ______

Which quotation from “The Mountain” most effectively illustrates the claim?
selections: A. “A dry ravine emerged under boughs / Into the pasture.”
B. “The mountain stood there to be pointed at.”
C. “I felt it like a wall / Behind which I was sheltered from a wind.”
D. “I crossed the river and swung round the mountain.”
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案，因为它最有效地使用了《山》的引用来说明讲述者感到被山保护的观点。在引用中，讲述者回忆说，山就像一面墙，提供了抵御风的庇护。讲述者感到被山庇护，表明山给他提供了一种被保护的感觉。
B.题目文本翻译
《山》是罗伯特·弗罗斯特于1914年创作的一首诗。在诗中，叙述者造访一个位于山旁的小镇。叙述者声称感到受到山的保护，表示______。

question:
The Nacional tree is a rare variety of cacao. Nacionals were thought to have gone extinct by the twentieth century due to a fungus. This fungus can spread from tree to nearby tree through the air and causes disease. But around 2013, cacao expert Servio Pachard located some of these Nacional trees. The trees were in the Piedra de Plata coastal forest, within a hard-to-reach valley in Ecuador. Conservationists inferred that the Nacional trees in Piedra de Plata might have avoided the diseases that wiped out the other Nacionals because ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. early twentieth-century scientists did not know why so many Nacionals were becoming infected.
B. the ability of the fungus to travel through the air was only recently discovered.
C. they were too far from the other Nacional trees infected by the fungus to become infected themselves.
D. the chocolate made from their pods was highly valued.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案，因为它最合乎逻辑地完成了文本对Nacional树在Piedra de Plata生存的讨论。文本指出，引起其他地方Nacional树生病的真菌通过空气从一棵树传播到附近的树。文本还提到，幸存的Nacional树是在厄瓜多尔一个难以到达的山谷中发现的。根据这些信息，可以合理推测，这些树可能因为与感染的Nacional树在地理上隔离，从而避免了感染，阻止了空气中的真菌传播到它们身上。
B.题目文本翻译
Nacional树是一种稀有的可可品种。到了二十世纪，人们认为Nacional树已经灭绝，原因是受到了一种真菌的侵袭。这种真菌可以通过空气从一棵树传播到附近的树木，并导致疾病。然而，在2013年，可可专家Servio Pachard发现了一些Nacional树。这些树位于厄瓜多尔一个难以到达的山谷中的Piedra de Plata沿海森林。保护主义者推测，Piedra de Plata的Nacional树可能避免了那些消灭其他Nacional树的疾病，因为______。

question:
Pigments give paints and dyes their color. Ocher is a mineral-based pigment used to make several colors, including red. Red ocher gets its color from iron oxide. Pigments can also be plant-based; plant-based pigments contain a high level of carbon. In a 2023 study, archaeologists tested the red pigment on decorated beads made by members of the Natufian culture approximately 15,000 years ago. The test showed that the pigment found on several beads contained no iron but had a high level of carbon. This finding led the researchers to conclude that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
selections: A. the Natufian beads examined in the study are the oldest surviving examples of the use of plant-based pigments for decorating beads.
B. the Natufian beadmakers used plant-based pigments rather than ocher to decorate some of the beads examined in the study.
C. the Natufian beadmakers preferred to use plant-based pigments because they are much brighter than mineral-based pigments are.
D. the pigments used by the Natufian beadmakers likely came from plants because ocher was difficult to find.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择B是最佳答案，因为它提出的结论最符合文本对颜料化学成分的讨论。文本首先区分了两种颜料：矿物基颜料，如红土，它们的颜色来自氧化铁；以及植物基颜料，它们的碳含量较高。接着，文本描述了考古学家对大约15000年前纳图夫文化成员制作的装饰性珠子的颜料进行的分析。考古学家发现一些珠子上的红色颜料不含铁，但碳含量较高。由于红土的颜色来自氧化铁，而植物基颜料的碳含量较高，研究人员得出结论，纳图夫珠子制造者使用植物基颜料装饰了所研究的一些珠子。
B.题目文本翻译
颜料赋予油漆和染料颜色。土黄土是一种矿物质颜料，用于制造多种颜色，包括红色。红土的颜色源自氧化铁。颜料也可以是植物基的；植物基颜料含有高水平的碳。在2023年的一项研究中，考古学家对大约15000年前纳图非文化成员制作的装饰珠子上的红色颜料进行了测试。测试显示，在几颗珠子上发现的颜料不含铁，但含有高水平的碳。这个发现使研究人员得出结论，______。

question:
Increasing the heat on an uncovered boiling pot of water does not increase the temperature of the water. What increases is the rate at which the water turns to ______ a pressure cooker pot, though, an airtight seal traps the vapor in the pot, creating pressure that allows the temperature of the water to increase past its boiling point.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项A是最佳答案。被测试的规则是句子之间的标点使用。在这个选项中，句号被正确地用来标记一个句子（“What…vapor”）和另一个句子（“With…point”）之间的分界。

question:
The Dust Bowl was a period of severe drought that plagued the Great Plains of the US during the 1930s. During this time, dust storms ______ over 100 million acres of land. They even reached as far east as New York City.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项 D 是最佳答案。所测试的惯例是使用动词来表达句子的时态。在这个选项中，过去式动词“affected”与短语“during this time”搭配使用，正确地表明了尘暴发生在1930年代。

question:
Between 322 and 184 BCE, the Maurya Empire established a complex economic system that, through trade and centralized ______ funded major infrastructure projects throughout the Indian subcontinent. This included the building of many roads, canals, and hospitals.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项 B 是最佳答案。此处考查的语法规则是句子中的标点使用。在“taxation”后面的逗号与“that”后面的逗号配对，起到将补充成分“通过贸易和集中税收”与句子的其余部分分开的作用。这个补充成分用于识别摩揭陀经济的资金来源，而这对逗号则表明，即使去掉这个成分，句子的语法连贯性也不会受到影响。

question:
In his painting At the Cycle-Race Track, Jean Metzinger aims to depict a bike race in four-dimensional space. Of course, Metzinger’s painting doesn’t technically represent a fourth dimension; humans can only see in three dimensions. ______ by depicting the race through multiple, simultaneous perspectives, Metzinger offers a fascinating glimpse at what this other universe might look like.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项B是最佳答案。“也就是说”在逻辑上表明，这句话中的陈述——梅青格通过描绘多个同时的视角提供了对四维空间的洞察——是正确的，尽管前一句提到的观点（梅青格的画作在技术上并不代表第四维，因为人类只能在三维中观察）与之相悖。
B.题目文本翻译
在他的画作《在自行车赛道上》中，简·梅青试图描绘一个四维空间中的自行车比赛。当然，梅青的画作并不真正代表第四维；人类只能在三维空间中观察。______通过以多种同时的视角描绘比赛，梅青提供了一个迷人的视角，让人们得以窥见这个其他宇宙可能的样子。

question:
Many mechanical calculators were powered by a notched cylinder mechanism called the Leibniz wheel. Leibniz wheel calculators were popular in the first half of the twentieth ______ these ingenious devices were eventually replaced by electronic calculators.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 许多机械计算器是由一种称为莱布尼茨轮的凹槽圆筒机制驱动的。莱布尼茨轮计算器在二十世纪上半叶非常受欢迎，______空白______这些巧妙的装置最终被电子计算器取代。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●“Raymond’s Run” is a short story.
●It was written by African American author Toni Cade Bambara.
●It was first published in her book Gorilla, My Love in 1972.
●It is told from a first person perspective.
●It takes place in Harlem.

The student wants to indicate where the short story takes place. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. “Raymond’s Run” takes place in Harlem.
B. “Raymond’s Run” was published in Gorilla, My Love.
C. “Raymond’s Run” is told from a first person perspective.
D. “Raymond’s Run” was written by Toni Cade Bambara
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项A是最佳答案。句子指出了《雷蒙德的奔跑》发生的地点，即哈莱姆。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，学生做了以下笔记：
- 《雷蒙德的奔跑》是一篇短篇小说。
- 它是由非裔美国作家托尼·凯德·班巴拉创作的。
- 它首次发表于她1972年的书《大猩猩，我的爱》中。
- 故事是以第一人称的视角叙述的。
- 故事发生在哈莱姆区。

question:
Wanting to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Alaska Purchase, ______ up with a motto that best captured the state’s unique character. The commission selected “North to the Future,” submitted by Juneau journalist Richard Peter, as its winning entry.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
selections: A. a contest sponsored by the Alaska Centennial Commission would award $300 to an individual who came
B. an award of $300 would go to an individual in a contest sponsored by the Alaska Centennial Commission for coming
C. $300 would be awarded to an individual by the Alaska Centennial Commission in a contest for coming
D. the Alaska Centennial Commission sponsored a contest that would award $300 to an individual who came
explanations: 想要庆祝阿拉斯加购买100周年，______提出了一个最佳体现该州独特特征的口号。委员会选择了由朱诺记者理查德·彼得提交的“北方走向未来”作为获胜作品。

question:
Eighteen letters written by Louisa May Alcott, author of the popular novel Little Women (1868), can be found at the New York Historical Society. ______ letters demonstrate Alcott’s keen business sense in her interactions with publishers.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项 D 是最佳答案。此题测试的惯例是句子中限定词的使用。复数限定词“these”与它所修饰的复数名词“letters”在数上保持一致。这个选项清楚地表明，这些信件展示了阿尔科特的商业头脑。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●Political scientist Graham Allison is known for his Thucydides trap theory.
●Allison’s theory states that whenever “a rising power is threatening to displace a ruling power,” conflict is likely.
●The theory is based on Thucydides’s explanation of the conflict between Athens and Sparta.
●Thucydides wrote that “the rise of Athens and the fear this instilled in Sparta” made conflict “inevitable.”
●History professor Edmund Stewart recently challenged the historical basis of the theory.
●Stewart claimed that Athens was not a rising power and that the rivals experienced a “clash of cultures” instead.

The student wants to use a quotation to challenge Thucydides’s explanation of the conflict between Athens and Sparta. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. According to Allison’s Thucydides trap theory, whenever “a rising power is threatening to displace a ruling power,” conflict is likely.
B. Thucydides wrote that conflict between the two powers was “inevitable,” although Stewart later challenged the historical basis of this claim.
C. According to Stewart, a “clash of cultures” between Athens and Sparta caused the conflict, not Athens’s rise.
D. Thucydides explained that conflict was caused by “the rise of Athens and the fear this instilled in Sparta,” but Allison disagreed, seeing the conflict as an example of the Thucydides trap.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项C是最佳答案。引用斯图尔特的话，这句话质疑了修昔底德关于雅典崛起导致冲突的解释，暗示冲突实际上是由“文化冲突”引起的。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，一名学生记录了以下笔记：
- 政治学家格雷厄姆·阿利森以其“修昔底德陷阱”理论而闻名。
- 阿利森的理论指出，每当“一个崛起的力量威胁要取代一个统治力量”时，冲突就很可能发生。
- 该理论基于修昔底德对雅典与斯巴达之间冲突的解释。
- 修昔底德写道，“雅典的崛起以及这给斯巴达带来的恐惧”使得冲突“不可避免”。
- 历史教授埃德蒙·斯图尔特最近质疑了该理论的历史基础。
- 斯图尔特声称，雅典并不是一个崛起的力量，而是对手经历了一场“文化冲突”。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●Georeferencing is the process of assigning geographic coordinates to an image.
●This process enables mapping software to place the image in its real-world location.
●A 2017 project by Tania López Marrero and colleagues georeferenced a set of aerial photographs of Puerto Rico’s coastline taken in 1930.
●These photographs are the earliest known aerial photographs of Puerto Rico.
●López Marrero’s project provided data that can help researchers analyze changes in Puerto Rico’s coastline.

The student wants to define the term “georeferencing.” Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. A 2017 project by Tania López Marrero and colleagues assigned geographic coordinates to photographs of Puerto Rico’s coastline and also used georeferencing.
B. Tania López Marrero and colleagues used georeferencing in their analysis of the earliest known aerial photographs of Puerto Rico.
C. Georeferenced aerial photographs from 1930 can help researchers analyze changes in Puerto Rico’s coastline.
D. Georeferencing is the process of assigning geographic coordinates to an image so that mapping software can place it in its real-world location.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择D是最佳答案。该句定义了“地理参考”这一术语，指出这是将地理坐标分配给图像的过程，以便制图软件能够将图像放置在其现实世界的位置。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 地理参考是将地理坐标分配给图像的过程。
- 这个过程使得制图软件能够将图像放置在其现实世界的位置。
- 塔尼亚·洛佩斯·马雷罗（Tania López Marrero）及其同事于2017年进行的一个项目，对1930年拍摄的波多黎各海岸线的一组航拍照片进行了地理参考。
- 这些照片是已知的最早的波多黎各航拍照片。
- 洛佩斯·马雷罗的项目提供的数据可以帮助研究人员分析波多黎各海岸线的变化。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●The engineer Robert Fulton designed the Clermont steamboat in 1807.
●He designed it in New York City.
●Clermont was the world’s first commercially successful steamboat.
●The city of Fulton, Missouri, is named after Robert Fulton.
●New York City’s Fulton Street is named after him.

The student wants to indicate how Fulton, Missouri, got its name. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Fulton, Missouri, shares its name with Fulton Street in New York City.
B. Fulton Street is in New York City, where the steamboat Clermont was designed in 1807.
C. Designed in 1807 in New York City, Clermont was the first commercially successful steamboat.
D. Fulton, Missouri, is named after Robert Fulton, designer of the first commercially successful steamboat.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项 D 是最佳答案。这句话说明了密苏里州富尔顿市是如何得名的，提到该市是以第一艘商业成功的蒸汽船设计师罗伯特·富尔顿的名字命名的。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
- 工程师罗伯特·富尔顿于1807年设计了克莱蒙特蒸汽船。
- 他在纽约市设计了这艘船。
- 克莱蒙特是世界上第一艘商业上成功的蒸汽船。
- 密苏里州的富尔顿市是以罗伯特·富尔顿的名字命名的。
- 纽约市的富尔顿街也是以他命名的。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●The Royal Alcázar of Seville is a historic royal palace in Andalucía, Spain.
●The palace is famous for its intricate tilework.
●The palace features majolica and arista tiles.
●In the majolica style, designs are painted directly on the ceramic tiles.
●In the arista style, designs are stamped into the ceramic tiles.

The student wants to contrast the two styles of tiles. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. Tiles in the majolica and arista styles can be found in the Royal Alcázar of Seville in Andalucía, Spain.
B. Featuring tiles in the majolica and arista styles, the Royal Alcázar of Seville in Spain is famous for its intricate tilework.
C. In the arista style, designs are stamped into the ceramic tiles, whereas in the majolica style, the designs are painted directly on them.
D. Among the famous tilework of the Royal Alcázar of Seville are majolica style tiles, made by painting designs directly on the ceramic tiles.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项C是最佳答案。该句对比了两种风格的瓷砖，指出阿里斯塔风格的瓷砖上有压印的图案，而马约利卡风格的瓷砖则是直接绘制图案。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，一位学生做了以下笔记：
- 塞维利亚王宫是西班牙安达卢西亚的一座历史皇家宫殿。
- 该宫殿以其复杂的瓷砖工艺而闻名。
- 宫殿中有马约利卡瓷砖和阿里斯塔瓷砖。
- 在马约利卡风格中，图案直接绘制在陶瓷瓷砖上。
- 在阿里斯塔风格中，图案是压印在陶瓷瓷砖上的。

B.题目文本翻译
1929年，《大西洋月刊》发表了几篇文章，这些文章基于新发现的信件，声称是林肯总统与一位名叫安·拉特利奇的女性之间的往来信件。然而，历史学家们无法______空白信件的真实性，并迅速将其视为骗局。

question:

B.题目文本翻译
对于画家雅各布·劳伦斯来说，保持______空白是艺术创作过程中的一个重要部分。由于他密切关注哈莱姆社区的所有细节，劳伦斯的艺术作品捕捉了哈莱姆文艺复兴和“大迁徙”期间黑人经历中的美和活力的细微差别。

question:
Text 1
A tiny, unusual fossil in a piece of 99-million-year-old amber is of the extinct species Oculudentavis khaungraae. The O. khaungraae fossil consists of a rounded skull with a thin snout and a large eye socket. Because these features look like they are avian, or related to birds, researchers initially thought that the fossil might be the smallest avian dinosaur ever found.
Text 2
Paleontologists were excited to discover a second small fossil that is similar to the strange O. khaungraae fossil but has part of the lower body along with a birdlike skull. Detailed studies of both fossils revealed several traits that are found in lizards but not in dinosaurs or birds. Therefore, paleontologists think the two creatures were probably unusual lizards, even though the skulls looked avian at first.

Based on the texts, what would the paleontologists in Text 2 most likely say about the researchers’ initial thought in Text 1?
selections: A. It is understandable because the fossil does look like it could be related to birds, even though O. khaungraae is probably a lizard.
B. It is confusing because it isn’t clear what caused the researchers to think that O. khaungraae  might be related to birds.
C. It is flawed because the researchers mistakenly assumed that O. khaungraae  must be a lizard.
D. It is reasonable because the O. khaungraae skull is about the same size as the skull of the second fossil but is shaped differently.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择A是最佳答案，因为它反映了文本2中的古生物学家对文本1中的研究人员最初想法的看法。文本1重点介绍了一种奇特化石的发现，该化石由已灭绝物种Oculudentavis khaungraae的头骨组成。根据文本1的描述，这个化石具有一些似鸟类的特征，这使得研究人员最初认为这可能是一种非常小的鸟类恐龙。文本2开头提到发现了第二个与文本1中讨论的化石相似的化石，随后解释了通过对这两个化石的详细研究，古生物学家认为这两种生物可能是一些不寻常的蜥蜴，即使它们的头骨在最初看起来像是鸟类。这表明文本2中的古生物学家认识到这些化石确实看起来可能与鸟类有关。因此，文本2中的古生物学家最有可能会说，文本1中的研究人员最初的想法——认为这个化石是鸟类的——是可以理解的，即使这个化石可能不是鸟类，而是蜥蜴的。
B.题目文本翻译
文本 1
在一块9900万年前的琥珀中发现了一个微小而独特的化石，属于已经灭绝的物种Oculudentavis khaungraae。O. khaungraae化石由一个圆形的头骨、一个细长的口鼻和一个大的眼窝组成。由于这些特征看起来像是鸟类或与鸟类相关，研究人员最初认为这个化石可能是迄今发现的最小的鸟类恐龙。
文本 2
古生物学家们兴奋地发现了第二个与奇特的O. khaungraae化石相似的小化石，但它有部分下身以及一个类似鸟类的头骨。对这两种化石的详细研究揭示了几种特征，这些特征在蜥蜴中存在，但在恐龙或鸟类中不存在。因此，古生物学家认为这两种生物可能是非常独特的蜥蜴，尽管它们的头骨在最初看起来像鸟类。

question:
O Pioneers! is a 1913 novel by Willa Cather. In the novel, Cather portrays Alexandra Bergson as having a deep emotional connection to her natural surroundings: ______

Which quotation from O Pioneers! most effectively illustrates the claim?
selections: A. “She had never known before how much the country meant to her. The chirping of the insects down in the long grass had been like the sweetest music. She had felt as if her heart were hiding down there, somewhere, with the quail and the plover and all the little wild things that crooned or buzzed in the sun. Under the long shaggy ridges, she felt the future stirring.”

B. “Alexandra talked to the men about their crops and to the women about their poultry. She spent a whole day with one young farmer who had been away at school, and who was experimenting with a new kind of clover hay. She learned a great deal.”

C. “Alexandra drove off alone. The rattle of her wagon was lost in the howling of the wind, but her lantern, held firmly between her feet, made a moving point of light along the highway, going deeper and deeper into the dark country.”

D. “It was Alexandra who read the papers and followed the markets, and who learned by the mistakes of their neighbors. It was Alexandra who could always tell about what it had cost to fatten each steer, and who could guess the weight of a hog before it went on the scales closer than John Bergson [her father] himself.”
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它引用了最直接说明凯瑟尔描绘亚历山德拉与自然环境之间深厚情感联系的内容。这段引用指出乡村对亚历山德拉意味着很多，并详细描述了她的自然环境在情感上对她的影响：昆虫的声音像是“最甜美的音乐”，她感觉“她的心似乎藏在草丛中，与鹌鹑和石班鱼在一起”，而在山脊附近，她感受到“未来的涌动”。
B.题目文本翻译
《开拓者！》是威拉·凯瑟于1913年创作的一部小说。在这部小说中，凯瑟描绘了亚历山德拉·伯格森与她的自然环境之间深厚的情感联系：______

question:
The following text is adapted from Oscar Wilde’s 1891 novel The Picture of Dorian Gray. Dorian Gray is taking his first look at a portrait that Hallward has painted of him.
Dorian passed listlessly in front of his picture and turned towards it. When he saw it he drew back, and his cheeks flushed for a moment with pleasure. A look of joy came into his eyes, as if he had recognized himself for the first time. He stood there motionless and in wonder, dimly conscious that Hallward was speaking to him, but not catching the meaning of his words. The sense of his own beauty came on him like a revelation. He had never felt it before.

According to the text, what is true about Dorian?
selections: A. He wants to know Hallward’s opinion of the portrait.
B. He is delighted by what he sees in the portrait.
C. He prefers portraits to other types of paintings.
D. He is uncertain of Hallward’s talent as an artist.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择B是最佳答案，因为它提出了一个关于多里安的陈述，该陈述得到了文本的直接支持。文本的叙述者提到，当多里安看到他的肖像时，“他的脸颊因高兴而稍微泛红”，“他的眼中流露出一丝喜悦”。叙述者接着说，多里安“惊奇地”看着肖像，并表现出他对肖像如此着迷，以至于没有注意到霍华德在对他说什么。所有这些细节都支持了多里安因看到肖像而感到高兴的描述。
B.题目文本翻译
以下文字改编自奥斯卡·王尔德1891年的小说《道林·格雷的画像》。道林·格雷第一次看到了霍尔沃德为他画的肖像。
道林无精打采地走到肖像前，转身朝它看去。当他看到画作时，退后了一步，脸颊瞬间因愉悦而泛红。他的眼中闪现出一丝喜悦，仿佛第一次认出了自己。他静静地站在那里，神情恍惚，隐约意识到霍尔沃德在对他说话，却没有听懂他的话语。对自己美丽的意识如同启示般袭来，他从未感受过这种感觉。

question:
The following text is adapted from Cynthia Kadohata’s 2004 novel Kira-Kira.
[Uncle Katsuhisa] was as loud as my father was quiet. Even when he wasn’t talking, he made a lot of noise, clearing his throat and sniffing and tapping his fingers.
©2004 by Cynthia Kadohata

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?
selections: A. It lists the kinds of topics Uncle Katsuhisa enjoys discussing.
B. It suggests that Uncle Katsuhisa dislikes meeting new people.
C. It contrasts Uncle Katsuhisa with the narrator’s father.
D. It describes a conversation between the narrator and the narrator’s father.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项C是最佳答案，因为它最准确地描述了划线句子在整篇文本中的功能。划线句子通过将叔叔胜久描述为“吵闹”，而将叙述者的父亲描述为“安静”，建立了二者之间的差异。文本接着详细阐述了这种对比，描述了一些即使在不说话时，叔叔胜久也非常吵闹的方式。
B.题目文本翻译
以下文本改编自辛西娅·卡多哈塔（Cynthia Kadohata）2004年的小说《闪闪发光》（Kira-Kira）。
[叔叔胜久]的声音和我父亲的安静形成了鲜明的对比。即便在他不说话的时候，他也会发出很多声音，清嗓子、嗅鼻子和敲打手指。
©2004 辛西娅·卡多哈塔

question:
One challenge of generating electricity from ocean waves is that wave power isn’t ______: it varies in unpredictable ways that pose technological and planning problems for electricity generation.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项 D 是最佳答案，因为它最符合文本对从海浪中产生电力挑战的讨论。在这个背景下，“一致性”意味着在时间上稳定或不变。文本介绍了一个挑战，然后解释了波浪能量以不可预测的方式变化，导致电力生成出现问题。这一背景表明，所描述的挑战是缺乏一致性。
B.题目文本翻译
从海洋波浪中发电的一个挑战是波浪能不是______空白：它以不可预测的方式变化，这给电力生成带来了技术和规划上的问题。

question:
Predatory animals differ widely in how they ______ food for their young. Some leave dead prey nearby for their young to consume, some bring live prey to their young, and some feed their young directly from their own mouths.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案，因为它最合乎逻辑地完成了文本对捕食者如何喂养幼仔的讨论。在这个语境中，“提供”意味着供应或使所需的东西可用。文本指出，一些捕食者通过将死去的猎物留在附近或将活猎物带给幼仔来为他们提供食物。文本还提到，其他捕食者则直接从自己嘴里喂养幼仔。这一背景支持了捕食性动物有多种方式为幼仔提供食物的观点。
B.题目文本翻译
捕食性动物在如何为幼崽提供食物方面差异很大。有些把死去的猎物留在附近让幼崽食用，有些则把活猎物带给幼崽，还有一些直接从自己嘴里喂食幼崽。

question:
In his 1963 exhibition Exposition of Music—Electronic Television, Korean American artist Nam June Paik showed how television images could be manipulated to express an artist’s perspective. Today, Paik ______ considered the first video artist.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项 D 是最佳答案。此次测试的规范是使用动词来表达时态。在这个选项中，现时动词 "is" 与 "today" 一起使用，正确地表明 Paik 目前被认为是第一位视频艺术家。

question:
The following text is from Jane Austen’s 1811 novel Sense and Sensibility. Elinor lives with her younger sisters and her mother, Mrs. Dashwood.
Elinor, this eldest daughter, whose advice was so effectual, possessed a strength of understanding, and coolness of judgment, which qualified her, though only nineteen, to be the counsellor of her mother, and enabled her frequently to counteract, to the advantage of them all, that eagerness of mind in Mrs. Dashwood which must generally have led to imprudence. She had an excellent heart;—her disposition was affectionate, and her feelings were strong; but she knew how to govern them: it was a knowledge which her mother had yet to learn; and which one of her sisters had resolved never to be taught.

According to the text, what is true about Elinor?
selections: A. Elinor often argues with her mother but fails to change her mind.
B. Elinor can be overly sensitive with regard to family matters.
C. Elinor thinks her mother is a bad role model.
D. Elinor is remarkably mature for her age.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项 D 是最佳答案，因为它提供了文本中对埃莉诺的一个细节。文本指出，尽管埃莉诺“只有十九岁”，她却能给予良好的建议，并表现出如此高的理解力和判断力，以至于她成为了“她母亲的顾问”。因此，埃莉诺的成熟超出了她的年龄。
B.题目文本翻译
以下文字摘自简·奥斯汀1811年的小说《理智与情感》。艾莉诺与她的妹妹们和母亲达什伍德夫人生活在一起。
艾莉诺，作为长女，她的建议非常有效，具备了理解的力量和冷静的判断力，这使得她虽然只有十九岁，却能够成为母亲的顾问，并且常常能有效地抵消达什伍德夫人那种通常会导致轻率的急切心态，从而使她们全家受益。她心地善良；性情温和，感情强烈；但她懂得如何控制自己的情感：这是她母亲尚需学习的知识，而她的一个姐妹则决心永不学习。

question:
Utah is home to Pando, a colony of about 47,000 quaking aspen trees that all share a single root system. Pando is one of the largest single organisms by mass on Earth, but ecologists are worried that its growth is declining in part because of grazing by animals. The ecologists say that strong fences could prevent deer from eating young trees and help Pando start thriving again.

According to the text, why are ecologists worried about Pando?
selections: A. It isn’t growing at the same rate it used to.
B. It isn’t producing young trees anymore.
C. It can’t grow into new areas because it is blocked by fences.
D. Its root system can’t support many more new trees.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它提供了文本中直接说明的关于生态学家为何对Pando感到担忧的解释。文本指出，Pando是一个由约47,000棵颤杨树组成的群落，代表着地球上最大的生物之一。根据文本，生态学家担心Pando的生长正在下降，部分原因是动物在啃食这些树木。换句话说，生态学家担心Pando的生长速度没有以前那么快。
B.题目文本翻译
犹他州是Pando的家园，这是一片约47,000棵颤抖杨树的群落，它们都共享一个根系。Pando是地球上按质量计算最大的单一生物之一，但生态学家担心它的生长正在下降，部分原因是动物的放牧。生态学家表示，坚固的围栏可以防止鹿吃掉幼树，帮助Pando重新繁荣起来。

question:
For a school project, a forestry student needs to recommend a maple tree that is native to North America and won’t grow more than 60 feet in height. Based on the characteristics of five common maple trees, she has decided to select a ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项C是最佳答案，因为它最有效地利用了表格中的数据来完成关于林业学生项目的陈述。表格显示了五种枫树，每种树的最大高度，以及每种树是否为北美本土树种。文本指出，学生需要推荐一种北美本土的枫树，并且其高度不会超过60英尺。红枫是表中唯一符合这些标准的树种：它的最大高度为60英尺——这意味着它不会长得超过60英尺——而且它是北美本土树种。
B.题目文本翻译
为了一个学校项目，一名林业学生需要推荐一种原产于北美且不会长得超过60英尺高的枫树。根据五种常见枫树的特征，她决定选择一个______。

question:
Some oceanic fish species live very deep underwater. Researchers collected data about the depths at which various species live.

Based on the information in the table, at what depth does the southern stoplight loosejaw live?
selections: A. More than 2,000 meters below the surface
B. 150 to 400 meters below the surface
C. 500 to 2,000 meters below the surface
D. 250 to 500 meters below the surface
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项C是最佳答案。表格显示了四种深海鱼类生存的海洋表面以下的深度。根据表格，南方红绿灯鱼的生存深度范围为海面以下500至2000米。
B.题目文本翻译
一些海洋鱼类物种生活在非常深的水下。研究人员收集了关于各种物种生活深度的数据。

question:
In 2007, computer scientist Luis von Ahn was working on converting printed books into a digital format. He found that some words were distorted enough that digital scanners couldn’t recognize them, but most humans could easily read them. Based on that finding, von Ahn invented a simple security test to keep automated “bots” out of websites. The first version of the reCAPTCHA test asked users to type one known word and one of the many words scanners couldn’t recognize. Correct answers proved the users were humans and added data to the book-digitizing project.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
selections: A. To discuss von Ahn’s invention of reCAPTCHA
B. To explain how digital scanners work
C. To call attention to von Ahn’s book-digitizing project
D. To indicate how popular reCAPTCHA is
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项A是最佳答案，因为它最准确地陈述了文本的主要目的。在简要介绍计算机科学家路易斯·冯·安的背景后，文本重点讨论了冯·安的数字化工作如何促成了一种被称为reCAPTCHA的数字安全测试的发明。
B.题目文本翻译
在2007年，计算机科学家路易斯·冯·安（Luis von Ahn）正在致力于将印刷书籍转换为数字格式。他发现一些单词的扭曲程度足以使数字扫描仪无法识别，但大多数人类可以轻松读取它们。基于这一发现，冯·安发明了一种简单的安全测试，以防止自动“机器人”访问网站。reCAPTCHA测试的第一个版本要求用户输入一个已知单词和一个扫描仪无法识别的单词。正确的答案证明用户是人类，并为书籍数字化项目增加了数据。

question:
In a recent study, researchers found that relatively few video games released over the decades remain available today. For example, only 14.22 percent of games are still available that were initially released in ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项B是最佳答案，因为它最有效地利用表中的数据来完成关于视频游戏可用性的陈述。文本指出，过去发布的只有少数游戏今天仍然可用，并且指出在某个年份段内，只有14.22%的游戏仍然可用。表格显示，从1995年至1999年发布的游戏中，仍有14.22%可用。
B.题目文本翻译
在最近的一项研究中，研究人员发现，过去几十年发布的相对较少的视频游戏如今仍然可以获得。例如，最初在______发布的游戏中，仅有14.22%仍然可以获得。

question:
The Alvarez theory, developed in 1980 by physicist Luis Walter Alvarez and his geologist son Walter Alvarez, maintained that the secondary effects of an asteroid impact caused many dinosaurs and other animals to die ______ it left unexplored the question of whether unrelated volcanic activity might have also contributed to the mass extinctions.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项B是最佳答案。所测试的语法规则是句子中主句的协调。这个选项正确使用了逗号和并列连词“but”来连接第一个主句（“the Alvarez…out”）和第二个主句（“it left…extinctions”）。

question:
In 1933, the Twentieth Amendment to the US Constitution was ratified. The amendment mandates that presidential inaugurations be held on January 20, approximately ten weeks after the November election. ______ this amendment requires newly elected US senators and representatives to be sworn into their respective offices on January 3.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择 D 是最佳答案。“此外”在逻辑上表明，这句话中的信息——第二十修正案要求新当选的美国参议员和众议员在 1 月 3 日宣誓就职——与该修正案关于总统就职的要求是分开的，并且是额外的信息。
B.题目文本翻译
在1933年，美国宪法的第二十修正案获得批准。该修正案规定总统就职典礼应在1月20日举行，约在11月选举后的十周左右。_______ 该修正案要求新当选的美国参议员和众议员在1月3日宣誓就职。

question:
The classic children’s board game Chutes and Ladders is a version of an ancient Nepalese game, Paramapada Sopanapata. In both games, players encounter “good” or “bad” spaces while traveling along a path; landing on one of the good spaces ______ a player to skip ahead and arrive closer to the end goal.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 在历史小说《投降树》中，古巴裔美国作家玛格丽塔·恩格尔使用诗歌而非散文来生动地揭示古巴民间英雄罗莎·拉·巴亚梅萨的真实故事。

question:
At two weeks old, the time their critical socialization period begins, wolves can smell but cannot yet see or hear. Domesticated dogs, ______ can see, hear, and smell by the end of two weeks. This relative lack of sensory input may help explain why wolves behave so differently around humans than dogs do: from a very young age, wolves are more wary and less exploratory.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案。“相对而言”在逻辑上暗示了这句话中的信息——即狗在两周结束时能够看到、听到和嗅到——与之前的信息形成对比（即狼在同龄时能够嗅到但不能看到或听到）。
B.题目文本翻译
在两周大时，狼的关键社会化期开始，他们能够嗅闻，但还不能看见或听见。而家养犬在两周结束时，______够看见、听见并嗅闻。这种相对缺乏感官输入的情况或许可以解释为什么狼在与人类相处时表现得与狗如此不同：从很小的时候起，狼就更加谨慎，探索性较差。

question:
In the 1950s, a man named Joseph McVicker was struggling to keep his business afloat when his sister-in-law Kay Zufall advised him to repurpose the company’s product, a nontoxic, clay-like substance for removing soot from wallpaper, as a modeling putty for kids. In addition, Zufall ______ selling the product under a child-friendly name: Play-Doh.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项 A 是最佳答案。正在测试的惯例是使用动词来表达时态。在这个选项中，简单过去时动词“suggested”恰当地表明了Zufall在过去为产品名称提供了她的建议。这个动词时态与前一句中使用的简单过去时动词（“advised”）一致，后者描述了Zufall在1950年代对McVicker的建议。

question:
There are three basic steps you should follow when planning a scientific inquiry. First, thoroughly research the question you wish to answer. ______ come up with a prediction (also called a hypothesis) about the answer to your question. Third, develop an experiment that can test the accuracy of your hypothesis.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项D是最佳答案。“第二”在逻辑上表明，这句话中描述的活动——提出预测——是文本中描述的三步序列中的下一步。
B.题目文本翻译
在规划科学探究时，您应该遵循三个基本步骤。首先，彻底研究您想要回答的问题。______空白 进行预测（也称为假设），关于您问题的答案。第三，设计一个可以测试您假设准确性的实验。

question:
Some members of the US Supreme Court have resisted calls to televise the court’s oral arguments, concerned that the participants would be tempted to perform for the cameras (and thus lower the quality of the discourse). ______ the justices worry that most viewers would not even watch the full deliberations, only short clips that could be misinterpreted and mischaracterized.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
B 选项是最佳答案。“此外”在逻辑上表示本句中的主张——一些最高法院法官担心观众（观看法庭辩论的电视节目）只会观看短而误导的片段——是对前一句信息的补充。具体而言，前一句指出了反对法庭口头辩论电视直播人士提出的一个担忧，而随后的主张则指出了第二个额外的担忧。
B.题目文本翻译
美国最高法院的一些成员对要求将法庭口头辩论进行电视直播的呼声表示抵制，他们担心参与者会受到镜头的诱惑而表演（从而降低辩论的质量）。____空白____法官们担心大多数观众根本不会观看完整的辩论，只会观看可能被误解和歪曲的短片段。

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
●Some sandstone arches in Utah’s Arches National Park have been defaced by tourists’ carvings.
●Park rangers can smooth away some carvings using power grinders.
●For deep carvings, power grinding is not always feasible because it can greatly alter or damage the rock.
●Park rangers can use an infilling technique, which involves filling in carvings with ground sandstone and a bonding agent.
●This technique is minimally invasive.

The student wants to explain an advantage of the infilling technique. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
selections: A. To remove carvings from sandstone arches in Utah’s Arches National Park, power grinding is not always feasible.
B. Filling in carvings with ground sandstone and a bonding agent is less invasive than smoothing them away with a power grinder, which can greatly alter or damage the sandstone arches.
C. Park rangers can use a power grinding technique to smooth away carvings or fill them in with ground sandstone and a bonding agent.
D. As methods for removing carvings from sandstone, power grinding and infilling differ in their level of invasiveness.
explanations:
A.中文解析
选项B是最佳答案。该句有效地解释了填充的一个优点：它比使用电动磨床更不具侵入性。
B.题目文本翻译
在研究一个主题时，一名学生做了以下笔记：
● 犹他州拱门国家公园的一些砂岩拱门被游客的刻痕破坏了。
● 公园护林员可以使用电动磨光机抹去一些刻痕。
● 对于较深的刻痕，电动磨光机并不总是可行，因为这样可能会严重改变或损坏岩石。
● 公园护林员可以使用填充技术，这种技术包括用磨碎的砂岩和粘合剂填补刻痕。
●这种技术是微创的。

question:
Roughly once an hour, a torrent of boiling water shoots up 100 feet or more from Yellowstone’s Old Faithful geyser before plunging back to the surface—a cycle seemingly inhospitable to life. ______ as microbiologist Eric Boyd attests, “the geyser is…almost like a cradle for biodiversity,” home to numerous bacteria species that thrive in its sulfurous waters.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanations:
A.中文解析
选择C是最佳答案。“然而”在逻辑上表明，这句话中关于老忠实泉繁荣的细菌物种的信息是真实的，尽管之前的说法认为间歇泉的条件似乎对生命不利。
B.题目文本翻译
大约每小时一次，黄石公园的老忠实间歇泉喷出100英尺或更高的沸水，然后又猛然沉回地面——这个循环似乎对生命极为不利。_________如微生物学家埃里克·博伊德所证实，“这个喷泉几乎像是生物多样性的摇篮”，是许多在其含硫水域中茁壮成长的细菌物种的栖息地。

question:
The term “retroflex” derives from Latin and means “bent back,” an apt descriptor for the branch of consonants—retroflex consonants—pronounced with the tongue curling up and back in the mouth. In many languages, including English, these consonants are ______ in some dialects of Mandarin, however, four such consonants (“ch,” “sh,” “zh,” and “r”) are relatively common

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项D是最佳答案。所测试的惯例是句子中的标点符号使用。这个选项以一种传统的方式使用分号，将这个句子的第一个主句（“在许多……稀有”）和第二个主句（“在一些……常见”）连接起来。

question:
In the historical novel The Surrender Tree, Cuban American author Margarita Engle uses poetry rather than prose ______ the true story of Cuban folk hero Rosa La Bayamesa.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选择D是最佳答案。测试的规范是句子中有限动词和非有限动词形式的使用。非有限不定式“to tell”被正确使用，形成一个非有限（不定式）从句，解释了Engle在她的小说中使用诗歌的原因。

question:
In winter, the diets of Japanese macaques, also known as snow monkeys, are influenced more by food availability than by food preference. Although the monkeys prefer to eat vegetation and land-dwelling invertebrates, those food sources may become unavailable because of extensive snow and ice cover, ______ the monkeys to hunt for marine animals in any streams that have not frozen over.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanations: 选项C是最佳答案。所测试的惯例是句子中有限动词和非有限动词形式的使用。非有限现在分词“forcing”被正确地用来形成一个分词短语，该短语补充主句“those...cover”，描述了缺乏食物来源对猴子的影响。
